anyOf.description: No admin tools.
Reads lmgw's configuration and state.
Also changes them.

AdminLevel.description:
A level of lmgw's admin tools, written `off`, `read_only` or `full`:
what a device's admin tools may do now (the change feed's
`hello.self_admin` and `state.self_admin`), the level set on a device
key (`KeyRow.self_admin`, and `self_admin` in `key_create` and
`key_set`), or the gateway's own (`GatewayStatus.self_admin`,
`SettingsFull.self_admin`).

Forward compatible like every enum a client reads: a value a newer
gateway sends reads as `AdminLevel::Unknown`, as sent, and writes back
unchanged. The document lists the known values only.

AgentBatchShape.description:
What a `batch` manifest can actually do, for the Run tab.

Derived server-side from the manifest **and the stored config**, because
both halves matter and only one of them is in the manifest: the review
columns are the author's, in the author's order, while the values an
editable field may be set to come from the config field `enum_from` names —
so widening the taxonomy is a config edit and the table picks it up.
A client re-deriving this from the manifest text would also lose the column
order, since a JSON object parses into a sorted map here.

apply_tools.description:
The tools Apply reaches, named next to the button so the reviewer knows
what is about to be called.

apply_tools_are_ceiling.description:
`apply_tools` is the ceiling the agent's token enforces rather than the
calls the step makes — true for a container, whose image decides. The
Run tab says "may call" instead of "calls".

columns.description: Review-table columns, in the manifest's order.

decide.description:
The output can classify through a question set (its `decide`); `None`
when it cannot.

editable.description: Output fields the reviewer may override, with their allowed values.

has_apply.description: The manifest declares an apply step, so there is something to write.

has_classify.description: The manifest declares a per-item model call, so "Dry run" applies.

AgentBudget.description:
The visible bounds a turn runs under: one pair from Settings → Agents & tools,
never a second one invented per agent.

AgentDecide.description:
A batch output that classifies through a Decision lab question set
(labs-store design §4): the config field holding the set, the set's
question it asks, and how the stored config's set reads.

enum_from.description:
The config field the enum comes from without a set (`enum_from`),
which a run with a set does not read.

field.description: The config field holding the set's id (`QUESTION_SET_FORMAT`).

measured.description:
The threshold was measured on a labelled set run. Only a measured
threshold is applied: an answer whose confidence is below it needs
attention. An unmeasured one is shown, not applied (Decision 10).

model_field.description:
The config field the agent's model alias is (`{{config.<field>}}`),
when it is one: a classify needs it or a set, so the Run tab blocks
Classify while both are empty.

problem.description:
Why the stored config's set cannot classify (gone, no such question,
not a choice, no default model); a run refuses with it.

question.description:
The set's question that answers the output field: the output field's
own name. It must be a `choice` question, whose options are the
review's values with the fallback last.

set.description:
The set the stored config names; `None` classifies with the model
call, as without `decide`.

threshold.description:
The threshold the set keeps for its question (0 when it has none),
measured or not: see `measured`.

AgentField.description:
One rendered config field. `ty` is `string | integer | number |
boolean | array`; `format` is `secret | model_alias | multiline | directory
| file` or empty, or `QUESTION_SET_FORMAT` on an integer.

access.description:
For a `directory` or `file` field: `ro` or `rw`, as the **manifest**
declared it. Empty for every other field — the mode is a
property of the agent, never of the form.

has_value.description:
For a `secret` field: whether one is stored. Always false otherwise —
the value itself is in `config`.

kind.description: `git`, `image` or `url`.

AgentPortability.description:
Whether the export of this agent lands on another box.

Shown before the download, never enforced: exporting to the same box is the
common case, and the wrong answer is a file that looks complete while naming
an image only the exporter has.

notes.description:
What the receiver would have to do, one sentence each. Empty when
`portable`.

portable.description: Nothing about this agent is local to this machine.

AgentProvenance.description:
Where this row's document came from.

`None` on the detail document for a row nobody installed from an image — an
agent written in the Definition editor has no package and says so by having
no provenance, rather than by carrying one full of empty strings.

`installed_at` and `pulled_at` are two facts on purpose: the first is when
the row was written from the image, the second when the digest was last
read. `agent_pull` moves only the second.

digest.description:
`podman image inspect --format '{{.Digest}}'` at the last read. Absent
when podman could not say — never a placeholder that reads like a digest.

image.description: The image reference as it was given at install, tag and all.

manifest_path.description: Where in the image the manifest was found (`/lmgw/agent.json`).

AgentRequirement.description:
One `tools[]` entry measured against what the gateway offers right now.

A gap is a warning, never a refusal: an agent is imported before its server
is wired, the same way a server is registered before its image is pulled.

install.description:
The manifest's install hint, for prefilling the MCP page. lmgw never
fetches anything from it.

missing_tools.description: Names in `allowed` the source does not list right now.

registered.description: The label resolves to a registered server or a built-in toolset.

AgentReviewField.description:
One editable output field. An empty `options` means free text: there is no
enum behind it to offer.

AgentRowSet.description:
The question set that classified a batch row (labs-store design §4),
stamped on the row as the run read the set: its id, its name and its
`updated_at`. "Save as labelled set" saves a run's rows into the set
that classified them; a row the model call classified has none.

digest.description:
A digest of the output question's definition (type, text, options
with descriptions, levels) as it was asked. "Save as labelled set"
reports the set changed only when the question's digest differs, not
on any `updated_at` bump (a threshold write). Empty on a row stamped
without one, which reads as unchanged.

name.description: Its name then.

updated_at.description: Its `updated_at` then: the version of the set that answered.

output.description: Any JSON value; carried into the stored result verbatim.

AgentRunEventsBody.description: One ledger event object ({row, ...} or {log: "..."} or {done: true, ...}) or a JSON array of them. The same events may be sent as application/x-ndjson instead, one object per line; lmgw reads the raw body either way, whatever its Content-Type. A line or entry it cannot parse is skipped and counted in the response's rejected list, and never fails the whole call.

AgentRunSummary.description:
One `agent_run` job as the Runs tab lists it.

The universal job fields plus the run's own `detail`/`result`, whose inner
shape belongs to the executor rather than to this DTO — the same
split `JobView` already makes for every other job kind.

cost_micro.description:
What those tokens cost, in micro-units of the gateway's currency.
`None` is "nobody could price this", which is also not zero.

duration_ms.description: Wall clock from claim to finish. `None` while it is still going.

model_calls.description:
The model calls the run made, from its result: calls answered without
an error. `None` until it has a result. `Some(0)` with no `cost_micro`
and no tokens is a run that had nothing to price; `Some(0)` can also
come with a cost, from calls that failed or were stopped after their
rows were priced.

tokens.description:
Prompt + completion tokens the run spent, from its result.
`None` until it has one — "not known yet", which is not zero.

AgentRuntime.description:
What a `container` agent runs under.

Every limit is here with its default printed next to it on the Run tab:
a container's bounds are shown, never guessed, like a run's tool-call and
wall-clock budget. `0` means "no
limit" everywhere except `stop_grace_seconds`, where it means SIGKILL at
once — the page says which.

output_validated.description:
The phases whose `output` event is validated against a declared schema.
A phase absent here is unvalidated, which the Run tab says out loud
rather than leaving the reader to assume a check that is not happening.

phases.description: Which phases the image implements, in declaration order.

podman_note.description: Why it did not, when it did not.

AgentService.description:
Service mode as the App tab describes it.

Everything a bound here is read from is a manifest field with its value
printed: the idle window, the start timeout and the health path are the
manifest's, and `0` means what it says everywhere else — never idle-stop,
and wait as long as the start takes.

health_path.description: `run.service.health_path`. Empty = a TCP connect instead of an HTTP GET.

host_port.description:
The host port this start published on — ephemeral, per start. `0` when
nothing is running.

idle_seconds.description: `0` = never idle-stop, exactly as an MCP server's `idle_seconds` means it.

idle_seconds_now.description:
How long ago the last proxied request finished. `None` when nothing is
running.

in_flight.description: Requests in flight, which is what the idle sweep skips on.

log_tail.description:
The container's own log tail, read while it is running. Empty when
nothing is up — `podman logs` on a container that is gone has nothing to
say.

log_tail_lines.description:
How many lines `log_tail` is at most, printed beside
it so nobody has to guess whether they are seeing all of it.

mounts.description:
The host mounts this agent's container holds, in the manifest's field order and
only the ones that are bound.

The App tab lists them. `host` is filled for an `Admin` reader and left
out for the container reading its own row, which is told
`/lmgw/mounts/<field>` and nothing else.

origin.description:
The origin this agent's UI is served on, as a URL with its slash:
`http://board.localhost:8001/`. The container's
own `LMGW_APP_ORIGIN` is the same origin *without* the slash — an
origin to concatenate onto, rather than an `href`.

origin_resolves.description:
`<id>.<suffix>` resolves on the machine lmgw is running on — the server
asked the resolver when it rendered this. False is not an error: the
App tab prints the `/etc/hosts` line that fixes it, and Chrome and
Firefox resolve `*.localhost` regardless of what the system says.

port.description: The in-container port the manifest declares.

provides_mcp.description:
`run.provides.mcp`, when declared: the path inside the container that
speaks MCP, registered as the `agent:<id>` server.

running.description: The container is up and answering.

start_timeout_seconds.description: `0` = wait as long as the container takes.

started_at.description: When the running container was started.

starting.description: A start is in flight right now.

AgentServiceMount.description: One bound mount as a reader is shown it.

field.description: The config field that names the slot.

host.description:
The canonical host path — **`Admin` only**. `None` is what the agent's
own view sees, and it is absent from the JSON rather than empty: a
container is not told there is a path it is not being given.

inside.description: `/lmgw/mounts/<field>` — what the container sees, for every reader.

kind.description: `directory` | `file`, from the field's `format`.

AgentToken.description: The agent's credential as the detail page describes it.

has_value.description:
A token has been minted. `false` until the first run or the first Copy
token: an agent that is never run never mints a credential.

name.description: `agent:<id>` — the name Logs and the usage page print.

scope_note.description:
The derived scope in words — "token: any model", or the aliases it is
fenced to. Shown next to Copy token so the scope is never invisible.

AgentWarning.description:
One warning that is not a tool gap.

Beside `requires`, of the same shape and rendered in the same place. The
Start gate is `requires_ok` **and** no warning with `blocks_start`.

char_end.description:
One past the word's last matched letter or digit in `text`, in the
same units as `char_start`: the span is `[char_start, char_end)`.

char_start.description:
Where the word starts in `text`, counted in Unicode scalar values
(not bytes, not UTF-16 units). The span is matched on letters and
digits only, case-insensitively, in order: `Nuova,` and `Nuova` both
cover the five letters of `Nuova` in the transcript. Absent, with
`char_end`, for a word that could not be found in the transcript.

confidence.description:
How sure the model is, when it says (several families send `0`
for every word, which means "not computed", not "unsure").

end.description: Where the word ends in the clip, in seconds; as `start`.

start.description:
Where the word starts in the clip, in seconds. Taken from the model,
or computed from `start_sample` and `sample_rate` when it sends only
samples.

start_sample.description:
`start` in samples of `sample_rate`: as the model answered, or
computed from the seconds when the rate is known. Absent when the
model sends none and the rate is unknown.

word.description:
The word as the model reported it, punctuation and all (CrisperWhisper
keeps the comma on `Nuova,`, Qwen3's aligner strips it).

AnthropicCompaction.description:
`compaction`: on-demand compaction (the top-level `compaction`), and
which of its types work.

supported.description:
An Anthropic route (lmgw's `context_editing` is present) whose
catalog names an on-demand compaction type for the model
(`context_editing.compaction`): the field goes out as written and
the `compaction` block comes back as it came. Unpublished is `false`.

AnthropicContextManagement.description:
`context_management`: whether a request's `context_management` reaches
the model, and which of its edit types work.

compact_20260112.description:
`context_management.edits` names `compact_20260112`: the edit goes
out as written and the `compaction` block Anthropic answers with
comes back as it came.

supported.description:
An Anthropic route, which sends `context_management` on as written
(lmgw's `context_editing` is present), whose catalog says the model
takes it (`context_editing.supported` is `true`); unpublished is
`false`.

content.description: A string, or an array of blocks: {type:text,text}, {type:image,source:{type:base64,media_type,data} | {type:url,url}}, {type:tool_use,id,name,input} (the id as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's carries its thought signature and runs to hundreds of characters; echo it exactly, and do not send it to another provider directly), {type:tool_result,tool_use_id,content,is_error}, {type:thinking,thinking,signature} (replayed; unsigned when lmgw itself produced it). Every other block type (redacted_thinking, the provider's own tool blocks, a type newer than lmgw) goes to an Anthropic upstream as written; any other upstream is sent none of it, and x-lmgw-params-ignored names it as content.<type>. A block without a type is refused with 400. A custom tool without input_schema (a server tool) is refused with 400.

system.description: A string, or an array of {type:text,text} blocks.

context_management.description: Anthropic's own count of the input before the request's context edits ({original_input_tokens}), as it reported it. Only on an Anthropic model's count of a request with context_management.

AnthropicEffort.description:
`effort`: whether `output_config.effort` reaches the model, and which
levels it takes.

supported.description:
The model has selectable effort levels (`reasoning.kind` is
`levels`): a request's `output_config.effort` reaches it.

type.description: e.g. invalid_request_error, not_found_error, permission_error, overloaded_error, api_error.

items.description: {type:text,text} | {type:tool_use,id,name,input}; a leading {type:thinking,thinking} block when the completion carried reasoning (unsigned: produced by lmgw, not by Anthropic); a leading {type:compaction,content,signature,…} block exactly as an Anthropic model answered a compaction (send it back unchanged).

context_management.description: The context management an Anthropic model applied ({applied_edits: [...]}), as Anthropic reported it; a stream carries it on its closing message_delta. Absent from every other model's answer.

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Present only when the upstream reported cache writes.

cache_read_input_tokens.description: Present only when the upstream reported a cache read.

iterations.description: An Anthropic model's per-iteration usage, as it reported it (a compaction entry for a compaction it ran, which the top-level counts leave out). Present only when the upstream reported it.

compaction.description: Anthropic's on-demand compaction ({type: summarize}; send its beta flag in anthropic-beta). To an Anthropic model it goes as written, and the compaction block Anthropic answers with comes back as it wrote it (stop_reason compaction). Every other model's provider has no equivalent: it is left out and named in x-lmgw-params-ignored. A model's capabilities.context_editing.compaction says which types it takes.

context_management.description: Anthropic's context management ({edits: [...]}; send its beta flag in anthropic-beta). To an Anthropic model it goes as written, and Anthropic answers for it; a compaction edit (compact_…) included, whose compaction block comes back as Anthropic wrote it. Every other model's provider has no equivalent: it is left out and named in x-lmgw-params-ignored. A model's capabilities.context_editing on GET /v1/models says what it takes.

content.description: A string, or an array of blocks: {type:text,text}, {type:image,source:{type:base64,media_type,data} | {type:url,url}}, {type:tool_use,id,name,input} (the id as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's carries its thought signature and runs to hundreds of characters; echo it exactly, and do not send it to another provider directly), {type:tool_result,tool_use_id,content,is_error}, {type:thinking,thinking,signature} (replayed; unsigned when lmgw itself produced it). Every other block type (redacted_thinking, the provider's own tool blocks, a type newer than lmgw) goes to an Anthropic upstream as written; any other upstream is sent none of it, and x-lmgw-params-ignored names it as content.<type>. A block without a type is refused with 400. A custom tool without input_schema (a server tool) is refused with 400.

output_config.description: lmgw reads output_config.effort as the same reasoning tier x-lmgw-reasoning-effort sets, and output_config.format ({type:json_schema, schema}; the deprecated top-level output_format too) as the structured output every upstream gets in its own spelling. Its refusals are 400 invalid_request_error with the upstream's message. To an OpenAI model the schema goes with strict: true (this format guarantees the schema), so OpenAI's strict-mode rules apply — every property in required, additionalProperties false — and a schema that breaks them comes back as OpenAI's invalid_json_schema refusal, its message kept.

system.description: A string, or an array of {type:text,text} blocks, joined with blank lines.

thinking.description: {type:enabled,budget_tokens} | {type:disabled} | {type:adaptive} (enabled, no budget — "think as much as judged necessary") | {type:between_tools} (no up-front thinking: an off that goes to an Anthropic model as written; every other model gets its own off, and x-lmgw-reasoning-ignored names between_tools). Any other type is refused with 400. display goes to an Anthropic model inside adaptive and enabled; beside an off, and to every other model, it is left out and x-lmgw-params-ignored names thinking.display.

tools.description: Custom tools only (input_schema required); a server tool (web_search, computer use, …) is refused with 400.

lifecycle.description: Always active: a model lmgw lists is one it serves.

max_input_tokens.description: Alias of context_window, under the name the Anthropic SDK types it by.

prompt.description: USD per prompt token, as a decimal string; "0" for a local model.

AnthropicModelCapabilities.description: lmgw's own capabilities object (as on the OpenAI shape, where an absent field means unknown) plus Anthropic's ten capability blocks. In the blocks, supported: true means a /v1/messages request using the feature works on this model through lmgw; false means lmgw does not serve it yet or does not know — Anthropic's schema has no unknown.

batch.description: Always `false` yet: lmgw serves no `/v1/messages/batches` yet.

citations.description:
Always `false` yet. A `document` or `search_result` block reaches an
Anthropic-protocol route as the client wrote it and an answer's
citations come back to a Messages client (gateway design §6.1,
"Citations", 2026-11-06), but lmgw does not read the catalog's
`citations` block yet, so it cannot say per model.

code_execution.description:
Always `false` yet: the code execution tool is a server tool, which
the Messages ingress refuses.

context_editing.description:
Anthropic's context management (`context_management` on
`/v1/messages`: context editing and threshold compaction, and the
top-level on-demand `compaction`), under a name of its
own because the Anthropic-shaped model entry puts Anthropic's
`context_management` block beside lmgw's object. Present only on an
Anthropic-protocol route, the one route that sends a request's
`context_management` on as written; every other route leaves it out
and names it in `x-lmgw-params-ignored`.

endpoints.description: The lmgw routes that accept this model id.

image_input.description:
`vision` is `true` and the model is served on `/v1/messages`, whose
ingress takes `image` blocks (base64 and URL sources).

input_modalities.description:
Subset of `text`, `image`, `audio`, `video`, `file`, `pdf`,
`embedding`. `pdf` is a catalog's word (Anthropic's `pdf_input`,
Kilo's and OpenRouter's modality).
Absent = unknown, never "none".

languages.description:
ISO 639-1 codes (a few three-letter ones, `yue`) of the languages a
local audio model works in, whatever its task: speech, recognition,
alignment. A request's `language` takes them (lmgw sends each in the
model's own spelling). Absent when the model's package names none
as codes; see `multilingual` for a family that says only that it
covers many.

multilingual.description:
The model's family says it is multilingual without listing codes
("multilingual", "80+ languages"): it works in more languages than
`languages` names, which then holds few or none. Absent otherwise;
absent along with `languages` means unknown, never "one language".

output_modalities.description:
The same vocabulary, plus `decisions`: what a decision model answers
with (llama.cpp's and OpenRouter's word). A client that checks
llama.cpp's `architecture.output_modalities` for `decisions` reads
this list instead. Absent = unknown.

pdf_input.description:
An Anthropic-protocol route (`context_editing` present) to a model
whose catalog says `pdf_input` (`input_modalities` holds `pdf`): a
`document` block reaches it as the client wrote it, base64, URL or
Files API source (gateway design §6.1, "Anthropic blocks lmgw does
not model"). `false` on every other route, which is sent no
`document` block.

source.description:
Where the facts came from: `gguf+config`, `catalog`, `config`, or
`owner` (an alias's capabilities override).

speech.description:
A text-to-speech model's expressive controls — what `instructions`,
inline tags, `language` and `stream_format` do on it
(the speech capabilities object). A local audio model's is derived; a
cloud alias has one only through an alias's capabilities override.

structured_outputs.description:
`structured_output.json_schema` is `true`: the ingress reads
`output_config.format` (and the older `output_format`) of type
`json_schema`.

task.description:
`chat` | `embedding` | `rerank` | `decision` (a decision model,
answering on `/v1/systemone`) | `tts` | `asr` | an audio.cpp task
name | an image task | `realtime` (an OpenAI Realtime model, no lmgw
route). Determines `endpoints`.

vision.description:
`input_modalities` contains `image`. Redundant with the list on
purpose: a client can read this one boolean to decide whether to
send images, e.g. whether a session gets a screenshot tool. Absent
exactly when `input_modalities` is absent.

code_execution.description: The code execution server tool; `false` yet, as `supported`.

supported.description:
Always `false` yet: the Messages ingress refuses every tool without an
`input_schema` (a server tool) before any upstream sees it.

web_search.description: The web search server tool; `false` yet, as `supported`.

AnthropicStreamEvent.description: SSE event: <type>, data: <this object>, one per line of the sequence above.

supported.description:
`true` only when a `/v1/messages` request using this feature works on
this model through lmgw; `false` when lmgw does not serve it yet or
does not know.

The model reasons: `reasoning.kind` is `toggle` or `levels`, or
`fixed` with `enabled: true`.

types.description: Which `thinking` types work; all `false` when `supported` is.

adaptive.description:
`{"type": "adaptive"}` (lmgw's bare "on") makes the model think. On
an Anthropic route, which sends it as thinking type adaptive: the
model's catalog names the type (`reasoning.thinking_types`). Elsewhere:
its default is on, or "on" reaches it (the template's
`enable_thinking` on a local row).

between_tools.description:
`{"type": "between_tools"}` (no up-front thinking) reaches a model
that takes it: on an Anthropic route, which sends the type as
written, the model's catalog names it (`reasoning.thinking_types`).
Elsewhere `false`: those routes send their own off instead, and say
so in `x-lmgw-reasoning-ignored`.

disabled.description:
`{"type": "disabled"}` switches thinking off
(`reasoning.can_disable` is `true`; on an Anthropic route, the
catalog's `thinking.types.disabled`).

enabled.description:
`{"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": n}`: the budget reaches the
model. On an Anthropic route, which forwards the budget form as
written: the model's catalog names the type
(`reasoning.thinking_types`). Elsewhere: `reasoning.control` names
`x-lmgw-reasoning-budget`.

ApiError.description: Uniform error body for every non-2xx `/api` response.

message.description: Human-readable description, shown verbatim in the UI.

AppliedToCurrent.description:
What a folder patch applied to the folder's current thread (`applied`
in the patch's answer): the thread and the settings it changed, as the
thread settings name them (`temperature`, `voice.tts_alias`).

reason.description:
Why, for a declined call: the model reads "The user declined this
tool call: <reason>".

ApprovalRequest.description: One call that waits for an approval.

approval_request_id.description: The id a decision quotes (`mcpr_…`), unique in the gateway.

arguments.description: The arguments as the model wrote them: a JSON string.

call_id.description:
The call's id, as its `ready` and `result` frames carry it
(`mcp_apps::ToolReadyFrame::call_id`). Absent from an lmgw
before 2026-10-09, and from an `ApprovalRequest` read off a bound
session's `mcp_approval_request` item (OpenAI's shape has none):
there the `lmgw.chat.frame` relaying the `approval` frame has it.

name.description:
The tool's own name: the name the model called, without its
label's `<prefix>__`.

server_label.description: The thread's label the tool came from.

ApprovalRequested.description:
`approval.requested`: a turn in the thread stopped on a call that waits
for an approval (client-apps design §6.5). Rendered from the reply's
pending state at delivery; a reply gone by then (deleted, regenerated),
or a call decided by then (its `approval.decided` follows),
is not delivered. With `thread_title`, `server_label`, `name` and
`arguments` a client shows it, or a notification, without a fetch. Also
the shape of `Hello::open_approvals`' entries.

call_id.description:
The call's id, as the turn's `ready`, `approval` and `result` frames
carry it. Absent from an lmgw before 2026-10-09.

name.description: The tool's own name, as `chat_approvals::ApprovalRequest`.

thread_title.description: The thread's title at delivery (in `hello`, at the head it read).

AttachmentFacts.description:
What extraction found in an attachment (`AttachmentMeta::meta`): which
keys are there depends on the kind. A key a gateway version adds is kept
beside these, so a reader never loses it.

format.description: An office file's or audio clip's format, as sniffed (`docx`, `wav`, ...).

media.description:
A file an image or audio tool made: the model, its parameters and
times (chat-media-tools design §9).

parts.description: How many parts an office file has.

textless.description: A PDF's pages without a text layer, numbered from 1.

tokens.description:
The extracted text's token estimate (text, PDF, office files and
transcribed audio).

transcript_alias.description: The speech-to-text alias that wrote an audio clip's transcript.

transcript_error.description: Why an audio clip's transcription failed, until a retry succeeds.

AttachmentMeta.description: One attachment's metadata, never its bytes.

blockers.description: For a draft: why it cannot be sent to the thread's current model.

call_id.description:
The tool call that made a `tool` file, or the card action that made
an `action` file (its `act-<boot>-<n>` id, the one its stream's
frames carried); absent for an upload.

extracted_tokens.description: The extracted text's token estimate; `null` when there is none.

hints.description:
For a draft: what it becomes on the way, sent all the same (an image
as a placeholder, a PDF's pages as its text) under a fallback that
cannot see.

kind.description: `image`, `pdf`, `text`, `audio`, ... as the upload was classified.

meta.description:
What extraction found: pages, text-less pages, class, sheets,
transcript alias or error, tokens. `{}` for an image.

mode.description:
A text-class PDF's choice, `text` or `images`; `null` when it does
not apply or is not chosen yet.

source.description:
Where the file came from: `upload` (the user sent it), `tool` (an
image or audio tool of a turn made it) or `action` (an image card's
action made it).

AudioAlignmentsRequest.description: multipart/form-data only — lmgw's own route (for models whose row has task "align"), not an OpenAI shape.

anyOf.description: The chat model reads the transcript.

A chat model that takes audio hears the turn; the transcript is
made beside it.

AudioInputMode.description: Whether a voice turn may reach the chat model as audio.

AudioInputShown.description: `audio_input`: the setting, the level it came from, and the verdict.

blocked.description:
The verdict a GPU block would bring: its fallback's, or the refusal
when there is none. Absent unless no block is live now and one would
hand the turn elsewhere.

lead.description:
What handed the turn to `model` when the resolve swapped ("under the
GPU hold"). Absent when nothing did.

model.description:
The model the turn goes to: the thread's, or the fallback a block hands
it to.

path.description: `audio` when the model hears the turn, `transcript` otherwise.

why.description: Why the transcript, in the page's words; `null` on the audio path.

AudioInputVerdict.description: Where a voice turn's words go: as audio, or as the transcript and why.

blocked.description:
The verdict a GPU block would bring: its fallback's, or the refusal
when there is none. Absent unless no block is live now and one would
hand the turn elsewhere.

lead.description:
What handed the turn to `model` when the resolve swapped ("under the
GPU hold"). Absent when nothing did.

model.description:
The model the turn goes to: the thread's, or the fallback a block hands
it to.

path.description: `audio` when the model hears the turn, `transcript` otherwise.

why.description: Why the transcript, in the page's words; `null` on the audio path.

AudioSpeechRequest.description: OpenAI's TTS shape plus audio.cpp's own request options, forwarded with model rewritten to the upstream's own id; a row's configured voice presets apply on top. input may carry inline tags ([laughs], or a stage direction such as (sighs)): rendered by a model whose capabilities.speech.inline_tags says so, stripped everywhere else — never read out. An input of nothing but tags is 400 empty_input, refused before any model is started.

input.description: The text. A local model whose engine refuses a character its package lacks (Supertonic) is sent an equivalent it has in its place, or nothing; the x-lmgw-speech response header names each one. An input left with nothing to say (a lone emoji) is 400 empty_input, refused before any model is started.

instructions.description: A speaking style, or the description a voice-design model builds its voice from (required there: 400 instructions_required without one, unless the row has a default). Dropped for a model that reads none: capabilities.speech.instructions says which, and the x-lmgw-speech response header says when.

language.description: An ISO 639-1 code or BCP-47 tag; a local model gets it in its own vocabulary.

stream_format.description: Streams PCM16 (with response_format pcm) as speech.audio.delta events (sse) or as raw chunked PCM (audio). A local model streams only when its row runs in streaming mode; an offline row is 400 streaming_unsupported before anything starts (capabilities.speech.streaming says which). The x-lmgw-sample-rate response header states the PCM's rate.

voice.description: A row's own voice preset id, when it defines any (GET /v1/audio/voices). A voice-library clip with no transcript, for a model that cannot clone one without, is 400 voice_needs_transcript before anything starts (lmgw.needs_transcript in the voice list); send reference_text, or transcribe the clip in the dashboard's Audio lab. A local model whose audio.cpp image lacks eSpeak NG is 400 audio_image_lacks_espeak.

AudioTiming.description:
The engine's own account of one inference. Each figure is absent when the
engine leaves it out.

audio_duration_ms.description: Milliseconds of audio the engine processed.

rtf.description:
Real-time factor: `wall_ms` over `audio_duration_ms`; below 1 is
faster than real time.

AudioTranscriptionDetails.description: The same transcription, plus the detail arrays the plain route leaves out.

AudioTranscriptionsRequest.description: multipart/form-data (also accepted as application/json with the same fields but no upload: instead of file, audio names a clip by its path on the model server's own filesystem, e.g. /models/clip.wav, and the body is relayed with model rewritten; the multipart form is what real clients send).

AudioVoices.description: lmgw's own route. A local audio model is answered from lmgw's catalog without starting it (?probe=engine asks its own server, starting it); a remote one is asked.

lmgw.description: Only on a local audio model answered from lmgw's catalog (x-lmgw-voices-source: config).

default.description: What speaks when a request names no voice.

send.description: Where lmgw puts the name in the engine's request; clients always send it as `voice`.

transcript.description: A library clip's transcript is recorded.

held.description: The GPU hold (or a benchmark run) holds the card and the model has no fallback: the list stands, its speech is refused (503 gpu_hold) until the hold is released.

missing.description: Voices the spec names whose file the package lacks.

needs_transcript.description: The model cannot clone a library clip without its transcript: speech with an entry whose `transcript` is false is refused (400 voice_needs_transcript) until it has one (the dashboard's Audio lab, Transcribe).

voices.description: Every name the model answers to as `voice`, sorted; for a probe of the engine or of a remote upstream, as that source sent it.

CancelKind.description: What cancelling a running image job does (design §5.4).

oneOf.description: The image server's own cancel: the job is dropped, the model stays.

The image server cannot stop a running picture, and this call is the
model's only request: lmgw stops its container, and the next picture
loads it again.

The image server cannot stop a running picture, and another request
uses the model: the call stops waiting, the picture finishes in the
background and is thrown away.

logprobs.description: Always null: lmgw relays no log probabilities yet. Present because OpenAI's schema requires the field.

completion_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported reasoning tokens.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported prompt-cache counts, and each field only when reported: cached_tokens read from the cache, cache_write_tokens written to it. Both are part of prompt_tokens.

ChatCompletionChunk.description: One frame: `data: <this object>`, repeated, ending with the literal `data: [DONE]`.

usage.description: Only with stream_options.include_usage: null on every frame but the last, whose choices is [] and which carries the request's usage.

completion_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported reasoning tokens.

prompt_tokens_details.description: Present only when the upstream reported prompt-cache counts, and each field only when reported: cached_tokens read from the cache, cache_write_tokens written to it. Both are part of prompt_tokens.

chat_template_kwargs.description: Only enable_thinking is read (llama-server's own template toggle, distinct from the protocol-neutral reasoning controls above); every key is forwarded verbatim.

json_schema.description: llama.cpp's own top-level schema; without a response_format, or next to a {type:text} one, it is read as response_format {type:json_schema} and sent in that spelling. Next to a grammar it is 400 bad_request, as llama-server refuses the pair.

max_completion_tokens.description: Wins over max_tokens when both are sent.

content.description: A string, or an array of parts: {type:text,text}, {type:image_url,image_url:{url}} (a plain URL or a data: URI), {type:input_audio,input_audio:{data,format}} (data: URI, or raw base64 with format required). A tool message keeps only its text, as OpenAI defines it; any other part is dropped with a WARN naming it.

name.description: role: tool only. Forwarded as the tool result's name.

reasoning_content.description: role: assistant only. Replayed as the leading reasoning part (also accepted spelled 'reasoning', as OpenRouter spells it; DeepSeek and llama.cpp use reasoning_content).

role.description: system and developer are both treated as a system message; tool and function are both treated as a tool-result message.

tool_calls.description: role: assistant only: [{id, type:function, function:{name, arguments: <JSON string>}}]. Send each id back as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's call id carries the model's thought signature, which Gemini 3 refuses a replayed call without. Such ids run to hundreds of characters; echo them exactly, and do not send them to another provider directly (lmgw strips the signature there).

model.description: An alias, a local model id, a candidate alias, or 'prefix/…' to pass through to an exposed upstream.

reasoning.description: lmgw extension, OpenRouter's shape: {effort, max_tokens, enabled, exclude}. Read for the reasoning tier and forwarded verbatim.

reasoning_budget_tokens.description: lmgw extension: a thinking-token budget (also x-lmgw-reasoning-budget). Forwarded verbatim alongside thinking_budget_tokens — whichever spelling a llama-server version reads.

reasoning_effort.description: lmgw extension: an effort level, or 'none' for off — one spelling of the reasoning control (also x-lmgw-reasoning-effort, and reasoning.effort below); the header wins when both are sent.

response_format.description: {type:text} | {type:json_object} | {type:json_schema, json_schema:{name, description, schema, strict}} — translated for every upstream: Anthropic output_config.format (json_schema only; json_object is refused with response_format_unsupported), Gemini responseMimeType + responseJsonSchema. A type the model's capabilities.structured_output flag says false is refused before any upstream call (400 response_format_unsupported, param response_format); a schema the upstream rejects is 400 invalid_json_schema with its message. Another type goes verbatim to OpenAI-compatible upstreams. Keys lmgw does not model, on the object and on json_schema, reach OpenAI-compatible and llama.cpp upstreams as sent.

service_tier.description: OpenAI's processing tier (auto, default, flex, priority, fast, scale, ultrafast), forwarded as sent; on an OpenAI platform row lmgw sends auto when it is unset, and prices the answer at the tier the answer reports. A request by a caller with a budget (its key's, or the gateway's) on a cloud model with no price on file for what it is billed in is refused before the send: 403 budget_unpriced, naming the model and the missing price. A flex request needs a flex price: no other tier's price bounds a flex answer's spend, which is cheaper.

stop.description: A string, or an array of strings.

stream_options.description: With stream: true, include_usage ends the stream with a chunk whose choices is [] and that carries usage; every other chunk then has usage: null. Without it no chunk carries usage. Not forwarded: lmgw asks the upstream for usage itself, for its request log.

thinking_budget_tokens.description: Same as reasoning_budget_tokens; both are read and both stay in the forwarded body.

top_k.description: Not part of the OpenAI API, but accepted; llama.cpp supports it.

ChatCompletionStreamError.description: The frame a stream carries instead of a chunk when the upstream fails after the first byte was sent.

ChatKnowledgeBase.description: One knowledge base, as the Chat shows it.

embed_resolvable.description:
Whether a model on the gateway still resolves to the base's pinned
embedding model; without one a search is by keyword only.

name.description: Unique across the bases.

kind.description: What the bytes were sniffed as.

name.description: The name it was uploaded under (a label, never a path).

pages.description: Pages, slides or sheets, when the file has them.

ChatTool.description: One tool a thread may tick.

name.description:
The exposed name (`docs__query`): what a thread's `allowed_tools`
and `require_approval` name.

ChatToolSource.description: One toolset a thread may attach.

description.description: A toolset's purpose in one line; empty for a server.

kind.description:
`builtin` (one of lmgw's own toolsets), `server` (a registered MCP
server) or `agent` (a service agent's tools).

name.description: A server's configured name; a toolset's label.

reason.description: Why it offers nothing now, when it does not.

server_label.description:
What a thread's `mcp_tools` entry names: a toolset's own label, a
server's tool prefix, else its name.

status.description:
A server's connection now: `ready`, `connecting`, `error` or
`stopped`. A built-in toolset is `ready` when it offers tools and
`unavailable` when it offers none (`reason` says why).

tool_count.description:
The tools of it the caller may tick now: a built-in toolset's
`tools`; a server's tools as last listed, the owner's
switched-off ones and those outside the caller's tool scope left out
(`0` before it was first listed).

tools.description:
A built-in toolset's tools. Empty for a server:
`GET /chat/api/tools/{label}` lists those, connecting it.

confidence.description: How certain the model is, derived from the probabilities.

probabilities.description: Every option with its probability; they sum to 1.

criteria.description:
Each option with its description, or `null` when it needs none, in
the order the options are offered. TypeSafe takes up to 255; llama.cpp
names its own per-type limit when a request crosses it.

instructions.description: The question: a string, an object or an array.

ChunkSpan.description: Where a chunk sits in its file, without its text.

page.description: 1-based page, slide or sheet, when the file has them.

seq.description: The chunk's position in the file.

span_start.description: Byte range in the file's extracted text.

CompletionRequest.description: Forwarded to an OpenAI-protocol upstream verbatim (a llama.cpp row's response_format excepted, see there): this route refuses anything else (an Anthropic or Gemini alias gets 400 rather than a request its upstream cannot answer).

n_predict.description: llama.cpp spelling of max_tokens; folded into it for local models with a guard or a ladder.

prompt.description: A string, an array of strings, an array of token ids, or a mix of both.

response_format.description: As on /v1/chat/completions. llama.cpp's own /v1/completions reads no response_format, so for a llama.cpp row it is sent as the top-level json_schema that route reads; a type with no such spelling is 400 response_format_unsupported, and a JSON type next to a grammar 400 bad_request, with nothing sent.

ContextEditingCaps.description:
The `context_editing` object of a model on an Anthropic route: what
its provider's catalog says about Anthropic's context management
(`capabilities.context_management` on Anthropic's own `/v1/models`).

compaction.description:
The top-level `compaction.type` values (on-demand compaction) the
provider says the model takes (`summarize`, …), sorted: its catalog's
`capabilities.compaction`. lmgw sends the field on as written, and
the `compaction` block Anthropic answers with comes back as it came.
Omitted when the provider names none.

edits.description:
The `context_management.edits[].type` values the provider says the
model takes, all of which lmgw sends on (`clear_thinking_20251015`,
`clear_tool_uses_20250919`, `compact_20260112`, …), sorted. A
compaction edit's `compaction` answer block comes back as Anthropic
sent it. Omitted when the provider names none.

supported.description:
The provider says whether the model takes `context_management` at
all. Absent when its catalog says nothing.

ContextExcerpt.description: One retrieved excerpt, as a user message stores it.

file.description: The file's name when it was retrieved.

file_sha.description:
The sha256 of the file version the chunk was cut from; empty for a
context stored before it was kept.

kb.description: The base's name when it was retrieved.

span_start.description: Byte range in the file's extracted text.

ContinueState.description: Whether a thread's last reply can be continued, and why not.

CountTokensRequest.description: Routed by model exactly like the chat endpoints, so counting a cold local model's tokens starts its container. The key's alias scope applies: a refused count answers 403 key_scope and is logged; a successful count is not logged. No budget applies, neither the key's nor the gateway's: a count costs nothing.

CurrentReason.description: Why `current` answered with a new thread.

oneOf.description:
The folder had no current thread (for a device key: none it can
reach).

Its current thread can no longer be continued in the folder. Only
the dashboard and admin keys are given this reason.
Its current thread had no message for the folder's idle minutes.
The caller asked for a new thread (`new: true`).

DictatedVoice.description:
How a dictated message says it was dictated (`voice` of a send): the
facts of the transcribe answer, nothing a reply carries. Unknown fields
are refused.

asr.description: The speech-to-text alias that was asked.

asr_answered_by.description: The alias that answered in its place, when a fallback did.

via.description:
Must be `dictation`: a realtime turn is written by the bound session
and cannot be sent.

dimensions.description: Forwarded (Gemini: outputDimensionality). A route that answers with another length — llama-server has no such parameter — is refused with 400 rather than served full-length vectors.

encoding_format.description: Encoded by the gateway, whatever the upstream: base64 is the little-endian float32 bytes, as OpenAI serves it.

input.description: A string, or an array of strings. Token-id arrays are refused with 400: an alias can route to a model with another tokenizer.

embedding.description: Floats, or a base64 string when encoding_format was base64.

prompt_tokens.description: What the model reported; 0 when it reported nothing.

total_tokens.description: The same number: embedding generates nothing.

id.description: The device row's `api_keys.id`; re-pairing keeps it.

name.description: The device's name as lmgw gave it, without `device:`.

Example.description:
One static example exchange: what the user says, and how the model
replies. Both sides are non-empty.

ExportAttachment.description: An attachment as the export carries it: its metadata, position and bytes.

blockers.description: For a draft: why it cannot be sent to the thread's current model.

call_id.description:
The tool call that made a `tool` file, or the card action that made
an `action` file (its `act-<boot>-<n>` id, the one its stream's
frames carried); absent for an upload.

data.description: The file's bytes, base64 (standard alphabet, padded).

extracted.description:
The text extracted from it (a PDF's pages, an office file, an audio
file's transcript); `null` when there is none.

extracted_tokens.description: The extracted text's token estimate; `null` when there is none.

hints.description:
For a draft: what it becomes on the way, sent all the same (an image
as a placeholder, a PDF's pages as its text) under a fallback that
cannot see.

kind.description: `image`, `pdf`, `text`, `audio`, ... as the upload was classified.

meta.description:
What extraction found: pages, text-less pages, class, sheets,
transcript alias or error, tokens. `{}` for an image.

mode.description:
A text-class PDF's choice, `text` or `images`; `null` when it does
not apply or is not chosen yet.

ord.description: Its position among its message's files.

source.description:
Where the file came from: `upload` (the user sent it), `tool` (an
image or audio tool of a turn made it) or `action` (an image card's
action made it).

ExportMessage.description:
A message as the export carries it: the columns of a stored message with
its `ir_messages` parsed, and the files sent with it.

ir_messages.description:
An agentic turn's tool calls and results as the JSON value the
record holds; `null` for a plain turn. When the record does not
parse, its raw text and `ir_messages_unparsed: true`.

ir_messages_unparsed.description:
Set (to `true`) only when `ir_messages` is the raw text of a record
that did not parse.

origin.description: A user message's origin: where its client said the user wrote it.

ExportRef.description: A folder or personality profile named in an export.

ExportThread.description:
A thread as the export carries it: the columns of the thread list's row
(`ThreadRow`) except the two derived from other rows, `last_message_at`
and `purge_at`.

kind.description: `chat` or `admin`.

media_defaults.description: The image and audio tools' default models of its own.

temporary.description: The thread was held in memory only (a temporary chat).

Fallback.description:
The fallback that answers for a blocked model, and whether it is a local
model: a local one may be a fallback too, and answers where it may run
(a row on the CPU under the hold).

FallbackUnusable.description:
A named hold fallback that cannot answer: `why` is the clause the hold's
refusal names it with ("does not resolve", "is itself a candidate alias").

FeedHold.description:
The GPU hold: whether local models are paused. A held model answers with
its own fallback, where one is set (each thread's model says which). The
`hold` event and part of `Hello`.

active.description: The owner's GPU hold is on: models on the graphics card are paused.

benchmark.description:
A benchmark run holds the graphics card: every local model waits
until it ends, one on the CPU too, or answers with its fallback
(chat-plane design D6).

FeedPrincipal.description:
Who the feed is for: its kind and the name it is known by, without the
kind's prefix. A paired device is kind `device`, named as it was paired
("desktop", not "device:desktop"); the gateway's administrator has the
other kind: the dashboard (named `dashboard`) or an admin key (named as
the key without its prefix).

Folder.description:
A Chat folder as `GET /chat/api/folders` lists it, with its thread
counts as the caller may see them.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

FolderChanged.description:
`folder.created` / `folder.updated` for a folder that exists at
delivery: the folder as `GET /chat/api/folders` lists it now (its counts
as the reader may see them), with `by` beside its fields.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

by.description: Who made the change; `null` for the gateway's own.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

FolderGone.description:
`folder.deleted`, and `folder.created` / `folder.updated` for a folder
that is gone by the time the event is delivered.

FolderOngoing.description:
The `ongoing` field of a folder: `null` for a folder that is not an
ongoing conversation.

current_thread_id.description:
The thread the conversation continues in; `null` until the first
`current` call, after its thread was deleted, moved out of the
folder or archived by hand, and, for a device key, while the thread
is out of the key's reach.

idle_minutes.description:
Minutes without a message after which the next `current` call starts
a new thread. `0`: a new thread only when a client asks for one.

FolderRef.description: A folder named by its id and name.

HelloCert.description: `Hello::cert`: the device certificate's dates, RFC 3339 UTC.

notice_after.description:
From when the device says "this certificate lapses on `<not_after>`;
pair it again before then" (two thirds of its validity).

ImageEditsRequest.description: Refused unless the resolved model's row has its edit pipeline enabled.

image.description: One or more image files. lmgw relays every multipart field named image verbatim, with no cardinality check of its own.

ImageGenerationsRequest.description: Other keys are forwarded for a cloud image upstream.

prompt.description: May carry a trailing <sd_cpp_extra_args>{…}</sd_cpp_extra_args> block of raw sd.cpp CLI arguments; the dashboard's Image lab builds this block and is the reference for its contents.

ImageGenerationsResponse.description: The upstream's answer, relayed as it sends it: each image carries what response_format asked for, plus whatever else the upstream adds (revised_prompt).

items.description: One image: b64_json, or url when the request asked for response_format url (an upstream's default, dall-e's, for instance).

anyOf.description: The model heard the turn's audio.
The model read the speech-to-text transcript.

InputPath.description: How a voice turn's words reached the chat model.

id.description: Absent on a notification (e.g. notifications/initialized); string or number otherwise.

method.description: e.g. initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/templates/list, resources/read, notifications/initialized.

anyOf.description:
Search before every turn and send the excerpts with the user's
message.

Give the model the knowledge search tools; it searches when it
decides to.

KbMode.description: How a thread's knowledge bases reach the model.

LanguageNote.description:
A speech model its language does not reach as set — the ASR the spoken
language, the TTS the reply language: a thread's `voice_resolved.language_notes`,
and Settings' `chat_voice_language_notes` for the Chat's own models.

message.description:
The whole sentence the page shows: the model, then what it does
("text-to-speech model 'audio/…' takes no language: …").

LiveTurn.description:
A turn answering a thread now, who started it, and whether it is a
bound realtime session's voice turn.

LiveVoice.description:
A realtime session bound to a thread now, and who bound it ("the
dashboard", "device 'phone'").

code.description: The HTTP status, repeated in the body as llama.cpp does.

lmgw_code.description: lmgw's own machine-readable error code, e.g. gpu_hold, gpu_benchmark, gpu_deferred, gpu_setup, engine_download.

description.description: A toolset's purpose; "" for a server.

kind.description: builtin: lmgw's own toolsets (lmgw, for owner credentials only; docs; kb); server: a registered MCP server; agent: a service agent's tools.

name.description: A server's configured name; a toolset's label.

server_label.description: What goes into a {"type": "mcp", "server_label"} tool on /v1/realtime or /v1/responses: a built-in toolset's label, a registered server's tool prefix, else its name.

name.description: The server's own name for the tool: its exposed name minus the <prefix>__ namespace.

description.description: A toolset's purpose; "" for a server.

kind.description: builtin: lmgw's own toolsets (lmgw, for owner credentials only; docs; kb); server: a registered MCP server; agent: a service agent's tools.

name.description: A server's configured name; a toolset's label.

server_label.description: What goes into a {"type": "mcp", "server_label"} tool on /v1/realtime or /v1/responses: a built-in toolset's label, a registered server's tool prefix, else its name.

MediaAction.description: What an image card's action does (design §8.3).

oneOf.description: The same prompt and settings, a new seed.
A variation (img2img) of the picture, on a row without `edit`.
An instruction edit of the picture, on a row with `edit`.
An ESRGAN upscale of the picture.

MediaChoice.description: One model a media tool can use, as a picker lists it.

label.description:
What a person reads: the name, and what it is (its family, on this
machine, a cloud model via its upstream).

local.description: One of lmgw's own rows rather than an alias.

name.description: The name the tool's `model` takes and a default stores.

MediaChoices.description:
What each media tool can use, for the default pickers: the same rows
and aliases its `model` enum lists for the caller.

voices.description:
The voices of each speech row, by its name; a cloud alias has none
listed (its voices are the provider's own).

MediaDefaults.description:
One level's default models, by tool (module doc).

Input is strict (`deny_unknown_fields`): a write that names a field this
build does not know is refused with the fields it does, rather than
stored as nothing. A stored level is read through
`MediaDefaults::from_stored`, which drops such a key on its own.

generate.description:
`image__generate`'s model, as its `model` enum names it
(`image/<id>` or an alias).

voice.description:
The voice `audio__speak` uses with the default speech model when a
call names none.

MediaFacts.description:
The facts of a produced file, under `meta.media` of its attachment
(design §9). Every field is optional: what a call did not have is left
out, never guessed.

answered_by.description:
The model or alias that answered instead of `model`: its fallback,
for whatever reason it could not answer.

job_ms.description: The job's own time, `completed − started` (sd-server's job API).

not_applied.description:
What the answering route could not take and so did not apply
(`seed`, `steps`, ...): a cloud fallback gets no smuggled parameters.

parent.description: The attachment this one was made from (a card action's source).

wall_ms.description: The call's whole time, loading included.

MediaPhase.description: What a running image or audio call is doing (`ToolProgressFrame::phase`).

oneOf.description:
The call's model's engine image is being downloaded before the model
can be loaded (machine-check design §5): `image`, `done_bytes`, and
`total_bytes` where the size is known.
Another model is being stopped to make room: `model` names it.
The call's own model is being brought onto the GPU.

Nothing more can be stopped yet: the call waits for memory
(`needs_bytes`, `free_bytes`).
The image server holds the job in its queue (`queue_position`).

The picture is being drawn (`pass`, `step`, `total_steps`, `preview`
where the image server reports them).

MediaUnavailable.description:
A stored default that does not resolve now, and why: the model was
switched off or deleted, an alias lost the route, the caller's key may
not use it, a voice its model does not have.

name.description: The stored name.

Message.description: One stored message of a thread.

answered_by.description:
The alias that actually answered, when it was not `model` (a
fallback); `null` when `model` itself answered.

attachments.description: The files sent with this message.

context.description: The retrieval that ran for this user message; `null` when none ran.

created_at.description: When the message was written (UTC, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`).

images_note.description:
For a reply that a fallback without sight answered: who, for which
model, and what went to it in the images' place. Absent otherwise.

ir_messages.description:
An agentic turn's tool calls and results as JSON text; `null` for a
plain chat turn.

kb_refs.description: Knowledge bases picked with `#` for this user message only.

model.description:
A reply's model: the alias its turn asked for. `null` on user
messages and on replies saved before it was recorded.

origin.description:
A user message's origin: the sentence its client sent with it about
where the user wrote it (`origin` of the send or the edit), which
the model reads before the message's text. `null` when its client
sent none, and on every other role.

pending_approvals.description:
The calls a gated turn's reply still waits on
(`POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/approvals` decides them). Absent when
none wait.

reasoning.description: A reasoning model's thinking trace; empty otherwise.

task.description:
On a late MCP task result (role `tool`): the task's facts. Absent
otherwise.

voice.description: How the turn was spoken; `null` for a typed turn.

MessageContext.description:
The retrieval that ran for one user message. Excerpt `n` in the
`<context>` block (and `[n]` in the answer) is `excerpts[n - 1]`.

budget_tokens.description: The budget the retrieval ran with.

dropped.description: Excerpts that ranked but did not fit the budget.

kb_ids.description:
The bases asked for: the thread's and the message's, as they were
then.

notes.description: Why something was not searched, or not fully: one sentence each.

searched.description: The bases that were searched, by name.

tokens.description: Tokens the excerpts use, heading paths included.

MessageTask.description: What a result row says of its task: `task` on a message of role `tool`.

ended_by.description:
Who cancelled it, for a cancel lmgw sent ("the dashboard", "device
'phone'"); `null` otherwise.

server_label.description: The label the tool was offered under when it was called.

status.description:
How it ended: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, or `abandoned`
(the server no longer knows it, or its server row was removed).

structured_content.description:
The result's MCP `structuredContent`, for a view of the call
(client-apps design §7.5): the model reads the result's `content`,
and this only when the content was empty. Absent when the result
had none, and for a result stored by an earlier lmgw.

task_id.description: The server's id of the task.

MessageVoice.description:
How a turn was spoken, on its message: `null` on the message for a typed
turn. On a user message: how it was dictated or spoken in realtime mode,
the speech-to-text alias that was asked and the one that answered, and
the audio's length. On a spoken reply: the text-to-speech alias, the
voice, the part that was never heard and the turn's timing.

input.description:
On a user message: `audio` when the chat model heard the turn;
absent on the transcript path.

transcript_error.description: On a user message the model heard: why its transcription failed.

unheard.description:
The reply's text after the heard part, shown behind a "not heard"
marker. Not in `content`, so the model never sees it.

ModelById.description: The OpenAiModel shape unless the caller sent anthropic-version, in which case AnthropicModel. No lmgw block on the single-model route.

ModelCapabilities.description:
The `capabilities` object of one model on `GET /v1/models`.

`task`, `endpoints` and `source` are always present — they are what makes
the entry actionable at all ("this id exists, here is where to send it,
here is how much to trust the rest"). Everything else is absent unless a
source stated it.

context_editing.description:
Anthropic's context management (`context_management` on
`/v1/messages`: context editing and threshold compaction, and the
top-level on-demand `compaction`), under a name of its
own because the Anthropic-shaped model entry puts Anthropic's
`context_management` block beside lmgw's object. Present only on an
Anthropic-protocol route, the one route that sends a request's
`context_management` on as written; every other route leaves it out
and names it in `x-lmgw-params-ignored`.

endpoints.description: The lmgw routes that accept this model id.

input_modalities.description:
Subset of `text`, `image`, `audio`, `video`, `file`, `pdf`,
`embedding`. `pdf` is a catalog's word (Anthropic's `pdf_input`,
Kilo's and OpenRouter's modality).
Absent = unknown, never "none".

languages.description:
ISO 639-1 codes (a few three-letter ones, `yue`) of the languages a
local audio model works in, whatever its task: speech, recognition,
alignment. A request's `language` takes them (lmgw sends each in the
model's own spelling). Absent when the model's package names none
as codes; see `multilingual` for a family that says only that it
covers many.

multilingual.description:
The model's family says it is multilingual without listing codes
("multilingual", "80+ languages"): it works in more languages than
`languages` names, which then holds few or none. Absent otherwise;
absent along with `languages` means unknown, never "one language".

output_modalities.description:
The same vocabulary, plus `decisions`: what a decision model answers
with (llama.cpp's and OpenRouter's word). A client that checks
llama.cpp's `architecture.output_modalities` for `decisions` reads
this list instead. Absent = unknown.

source.description:
Where the facts came from: `gguf+config`, `catalog`, `config`, or
`owner` (an alias's capabilities override).

speech.description:
A text-to-speech model's expressive controls — what `instructions`,
inline tags, `language` and `stream_format` do on it
(the speech capabilities object). A local audio model's is derived; a
cloud alias has one only through an alias's capabilities override.

task.description:
`chat` | `embedding` | `rerank` | `decision` (a decision model,
answering on `/v1/systemone`) | `tts` | `asr` | an audio.cpp task
name | an image task | `realtime` (an OpenAI Realtime model, no lmgw
route). Determines `endpoints`.

vision.description:
`input_modalities` contains `image`. Redundant with the list on
purpose: a client can read this one boolean to decide whether to
send images, e.g. whether a session gets a screenshot tool. Absent
exactly when `input_modalities` is absent.

ModelList.description: OpenAiModelList unless the caller sent anthropic-version, in which case AnthropicModelList.

endpoints.description: Every path listed here exists in this API and carries the capability its own operation documents.
Every path listed here exists in this API and carries the capability its own operation documents.

criteria.description: What a yes and a no mean, when the question alone does not say.

instructions.description: The yes/no question: a string, an object or an array.

OngoingInput.description:
`ongoing` in a folder create or patch: an object marks the folder as one
ongoing conversation (its defaults must name a model), `null` ends that.

idle_minutes.description:
Minutes without a message after which a new thread starts; `0`: only
when a client asks. A whole number of zero or more.

code.description: lmgw's own machine-readable error code (e.g. gpu_hold, gpu_benchmark, gpu_deferred, gpu_setup — a 503: the local model could not start on the graphics card, and the message says what on the computer lmgw runs on is not ready (fixed there, not by retrying), engine_download — a 502: the engine the local model runs in could not be downloaded, response_format_unsupported — the model or its upstream cannot produce the asked structured output type, invalid_json_schema — the upstream rejected the schema, its message kept, budget_unpriced — a budgeted caller's request on a cloud model with no price on file for what it is billed in, flex without a flex price among them), not the HTTP status.

param.description: The request field the error is about: response_format (chat completions, completions) or text.format (/v1/responses) for the codes response_format_unsupported and invalid_json_schema; null for every other error.

type.description: e.g. invalid_request_error, authentication_error, not_found_error, rate_limit_error, api_error.

created.description: Stable for the life of the gateway process rather than the time of each request; the catalog's own timestamp when it has one.

prompt.description: USD per prompt token, as a decimal string; "0" for a local model.

PreviewTokens.description: The token counts of a preview, through the universal counter.

answered_by.description: The alias that counted, when it was not `alias` (a fallback).

approx.description:
How the counts are approximate, as `x-lmgw-count-approximate` says
it; empty when they are exact.

builtin.description:
The built-in profile this row is (`concise`); `null` for one of the
owner's own. Read only.

follows_builtin.description:
The fields a built-in row takes from the built-in text, so they
follow its improvements. Read only.

length_rule.description: How long replies are; empty for none.

name.description: Unique in any case; never `default`.

persona.description:
Who the model is and how it sounds; empty for none. When set, it
takes the thread's system prompt's place.

voice_block.description:
The voice turn's block: `null` for the generic one, `""` for none, a
text to use as it is.

ProfileDraft.description:
A profile's content fields, with nothing saved: what Preview, Test and
Speak take, and what a create fills in.

ProfileVoice.description:
The speech part of a profile: the subset of a thread's voice settings a
profile carries, with the same checks and meanings. Each `null` inherits.

speech_style.description:
The speaking style the text-to-speech model is given; an empty text
is none.

voice.description:
A voice of that text-to-speech model, or of the Chat's own when
`tts_alias` is `null`.

ProfileVoiceInput.description:
The speech part of a profile: the subset of a thread's voice settings a
profile carries, with the same checks and meanings. Each `null` inherits.

speech_style.description:
The speaking style the text-to-speech model is given; an empty text
is none.

voice.description:
A voice of that text-to-speech model, or of the Chat's own when
`tts_alias` is `null`.

RealtimeAvailability.description: Whether voice mode may bind the thread.

admin_tools.description:
The thread carries lmgw's admin tools while the self-admin level is
`full`: its tools can change lmgw. Shown, never a refusal.

code.description:
The refusal's code, the one the bind answers with
(`chat_thread_admin`); `null` when `ok`.

Reasoning.description:
A profile's reasoning switch; `null` where it is used inherits (the
thread's own fields win over it, the route's default comes after it).

ReasoningCaps.description: Reasoning / thinking support and how a request controls it.

budget_tokens.description:
The configured default thinking-token budget, when set and non-zero
(a zero budget is published as `enabled: false`, not as a budget).

can_disable.description:
Whether a request can switch thinking off entirely. On an Anthropic
route: the catalog's `thinking.types.disabled.supported`.

control.description:
The exact header and body fields that work on this route; omitted when
empty (nothing to control on a `fixed` model).

default.description: The effort in force when the request sets none.

enabled.description:
The default state as this alias is configured. Absent when no source
states it — "the catalog says the model supports reasoning" does not
say whether it is on.

kind.description:
`fixed` (nothing to change per request), `toggle` (on/off per
request), `levels` (effort selectable per request).

levels.description:
Accepted effort values, least → most in the canonical order. Only for
`kind == "levels"`; omitted entirely when empty.

preserve_history.description: Whether replayed reasoning of earlier turns reaches the model again.

thinking_types.description:
The Messages `thinking` types the model takes, as an Anthropic
upstream's catalog publishes them (`capabilities.thinking.types`), in
Anthropic's order: `adaptive`, `between_tools`, `disabled`, `enabled`
(the budget form). Only on an Anthropic route; omitted when the
catalog names none of them as supported.

texts.description: TEI's spelling — either works; an embedding-only row is refused.

RerankResponse.description: Jina's results shape, regardless of which request spelling was sent. Built by lmgw from the model's scores, never relayed: no result carries its document.

model.description: The model as the request named it.

index.description: The document's position in the request.

prompt_tokens.description: What the model reported; 0 when it reported nothing.

total_tokens.description: The same number: reranking generates nothing.

Response.description: An upstream that speaks the Responses API natively is relayed as it sends the body: such a body may carry status queued (background), a null or missing usage and no store. lmgw's own translation always sends usage and store.

access_programs.description: Always null; present because OpenAI's schema requires the field.

output.description: Items are loosely typed here. An output_text part of a message item carries `logprobs: []`: lmgw relays no log probabilities yet; OpenAI's schema requires the field.

store.description: Whether lmgw stored this response, so a later request can continue from it with previous_response_id. Sent by lmgw's own translation; a verbatim upstream body may leave it out.

input_tokens_details.description: Tokens read from and written to the prompt cache, both part of input_tokens; 0 when the upstream reported none (cache_write_tokens is lmgw's own addition and absent from a verbatim upstream body).

ResponseStreamEvent.description: SSE event: response.<name>, data: <this object>. The response.output_text.delta and .done events carry `logprobs: []` (lmgw relays no log probabilities yet; OpenAI's schema requires the field).

type.description: response.created … response.completed/.incomplete/.failed, response.output_text.delta, the mcp_*/function_call_* tool-call events, …

background.description: true is refused on every path: a background response finishes after its answer has left, so lmgw could never record what it spent or hold it to a budget.

input.description: A string (one user turn), or an array of items.

items.description: A message ({type:message,role,content}), a prior turn's {type:function_call,call_id,name,arguments} (call_id as lmgw gave it: a Gemini model's carries its thought signature and runs to hundreds of characters; echo it exactly, and do not send it to another provider directly) or {type:function_call_output,call_id,output} (output a string, or an array of {type:input_text,text} and {type:input_image,image_url} items: a base64 data: image goes on as an image where the upstream's tool results take one and as a named placeholder elsewhere, another URL as a resource naming it, and any other item as its JSON text), an mcp_call echo, or an {type:mcp_approval_response,approval_request_id,approve,reason} verdict on a previous response's pending call. On an upstream that implements the Responses API itself (the OpenAI platform, a compatible row flagged for it) every other item the API defines goes there as sent: an {type:item_reference,id} (or an untyped {id}), a hosted tool's record (web_search_call, file_search_call, code_interpreter_call, image_generation_call, computer_call and its output, …), and content parts lmgw's loop has no reading for (input_file, an input_image by file_id). lmgw's own loop refuses each of them by name (400 unsupported). For a client key, an item_reference id and any input item's own id (a reasoning item's rs_…, a message's msg_…, a hosted call's) pass only when a native answer given to that key carried the item, and a file_id anywhere in the body never does (lmgw does not proxy /v1/files, so no client key made one): either answers 404 as an unknown previous_response_id does. The owner key passes.

instructions.description: Becomes the leading system message; an explicit empty string drops it on a chained call.

metadata.description: Echoed back verbatim on the response object.

previous_response_id.description: Continues a stored response: its conversation, tool calls and results included, goes ahead of this call's input, and mcp_approval_response items settle the calls it stopped at. 400 while the gateway's response store is switched off; 404 when no stored response has this id (it was evicted, or created with storing off).
