On an upstream that implements the Responses API itself, an id lmgw holds continues in lmgw's own loop and any other id goes to the upstream with the body; with mcp tools lmgw serves, such an id is a 400, since neither side can serve both.

reasoning.description: The one reasoning control this dialect reads: reasoning.effort.

service_tier.description: OpenAI's processing tier (auto, default, flex, priority, fast, scale, ultrafast), forwarded as sent; on an OpenAI platform row lmgw sends auto when it is unset, and prices the answer at the tier the answer reports. A request by a caller with a budget (its key's, or the gateway's) on a cloud model with no price on file for what it is billed in is refused before the send: 403 budget_unpriced, naming the model and the missing price. A flex request needs a flex price: no other tier's price bounds a flex answer's spend, which is cheaper.

store.description: Whether lmgw keeps this response, so a later call can continue it with previous_response_id (default true). Storing also needs the gateway's response store, which is on by default: a request can turn storing off, never on. The response object's store says whether this response was kept, so a client can see up front whether previous_response_id will work. On an upstream that implements the Responses API itself the body goes there as sent, and storing is the provider's.

text.description: text.format (json_schema, json_object, text) is the structured output every upstream gets in its own spelling, as on /v1/chat/completions; a native Responses upstream gets the body as sent. Its refusals are 400 response_format_unsupported / invalid_json_schema with param text.format.

tool_choice.description: "auto" | "none" | "required" | {type:function,name} everywhere; any other form the upstream's API defines ({type:web_search_preview}, {type:allowed_tools,…}, {type:mcp,server_label}, …) goes natively to an upstream that implements the Responses API itself and is refused by lmgw's own loop.

tools.description: function tools the loop hands back to the client; mcp tools run server-side on lmgw's own registered MCP servers, and keep the request in lmgw's own loop on an upstream that implements the Responses API itself (an mcp label lmgw does not serve goes there with the body). Hosted tools (web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, image_generation, computer_use_preview, …) go natively to such an upstream, which runs them, and are refused by lmgw's own loop.

allowed_tools.description: Tool names, as a list or {tool_names}; a name matches the exposed or the server's own spelling (docs__query or query). An empty list leaves nothing. read_only is refused: lmgw does not read MCP tool annotations.

connector_id.description: One of OpenAI's connectors: never lmgw's to serve, handled as a foreign server_url.

require_approval.description: "never" (default) | "always" | {never:{tool_names}, always:{tool_names}}. read_only is refused, as in allowed_tools.

server_label.description: Matches a registered MCP server's own tool prefix (or its name when it has none) — lmgw resolves this against its own servers, never against a client-supplied server_url.

server_url.description: A server for the upstream to dial (OpenAI's hosted MCP tool); lmgw never dials it. A block whose server_url is not this gateway's own /mcp is not lmgw's to serve: it goes to an upstream that takes /v1/responses natively, and a request served by lmgw's own loop is refused with a 400 naming it. This gateway's own /mcp reads as no server_url.

oneOf.description: A hosted tool: goes with the body to an upstream that implements the Responses API itself, which runs it; lmgw's own loop refuses it (400 unsupported), and so does a request that also needs the loop (mcp tools lmgw serves, a previous_response_id lmgw stored), naming both. For a client key, a tool that names something stored under the provider account (a file_search vector_store_ids entry, a code_interpreter container id or file_ids, a shell container_reference or skill_id) answers 404 as an unknown id does; the owner key passes. Fees such a tool bills beyond its tokens (web search, file search, containers, image generation) are not priced yet: its row is unpriced, with a price_note naming the calls, and budgets count its token part as a lower bound.

type.description: web_search, file_search, code_interpreter, image_generation, computer_use_preview, shell, … as the upstream's own Responses API defines them.

truncation.description: "auto" goes natively to an upstream that implements the Responses API itself; lmgw's own loop refuses it, since it never silently drops conversation history.

ResultTask.description: The MCP task a call started, on its `result` frame.

task_id.description: The server's id of the task.

RevokeKind.description:
What revoked a key, as a `CLOSE_REVOKED` close's reason starts with it
and the change feed's `revoked` event carries it (`kind`):

- `device_disabled`: a paired device was disabled; it may be enabled
  again, so it keeps its pairing;
- `key_expired`: a paired device's key passed its expiry;
- `key_unknown`: a paired device's key was rotated or deleted: pair the
  device again;
- `certificate_expired`: a paired device's client certificate passed its
  `notAfter` while the connection was open (device link design §5.1):
  pair the device again;
- `revoked`: any other kind of key, for any of these.

Forward compatible like every enum a client reads: a token a newer
gateway sends reads as `RevokeKind::Unknown`, as sent. One an older
gateway does not send at all — a close reason without a token, a
`revoked` event without `kind` — is an empty `Unknown`, the default, so
a client never reads a device's rotation as another key's revocation.

Row.description:
One row of the review table.

Both a live frame and a stored result use this shape, so the table renders
the same whether the run is in flight or was finished last week.

attention.description:
The output equals the fallback, or the call failed; through a question
set also a confidence below the set's measured threshold (`decide`).

columns.description:
The manifest's `columns`, rendered. Order comes from the manifest, not
from this map.

id.description:
`item.id` rendered. Empty marks the row errored — there is no
stable identity to apply anything against.

item.description:
The **source** item, kept so a re-run can re-fetch and re-classify this
row without re-listing the mailbox. Not shown anywhere.

output.description: The structured answer. `null` for a list-only run, which makes no call.

prompt.description:
Exactly the `user` text the model received, for the details modal.
Kept per row because "why did it say that" is the question the
review table exists to answer.

raw.description: What the model actually replied, so a surprising answer is explainable.

set.description:
The question set that classified this row, as the run read it
(`decide`); `None` for the model call. "Save as labelled set" saves
a run's rows into the set stamped on them.

legend.description: Each level's index (`"0"`, `"1"`, …) with its description.

probabilities.description: Each level's index with its probability.

score.description:
The expected level index, weighted by probability: it can fall between
two levels.

criteria.description: The levels' descriptions, lowest first: 2 to 10 of them.

instructions.description: The question: a string, an object or an array.

kind.description: `t` the title, `m` a message, `a` an attachment's name.

snippet.description:
The text around the match, with the match between U+E000 and U+E001
(private-use characters; escape the text before turning them into
markup).

folder_id.description:
`null` for a thread in no folder, and for one in a folder the
caller cannot see.

hits.description: The best matches, up to three.

match_count.description: How many places in the thread match.

ServedModel.description:
An alias a stage asked for, the one that answered when it was another,
and (for the text-to-speech stage) the voice.

Sourced_Nullable_string.description: A value and the level it came from; `source: null` when no level sets it.

Sourced_TurnDetectionMode.description: A value and the level it came from; `source: null` when no level sets it.

Sourced_boolean.description: A value and the level it came from; `source: null` when no level sets it.

SpeechCaps.description:
The `speech` object of a text-to-speech model's capabilities. Absent
fields are unknown, as everywhere in the schema.

inline_tags.description:
What inline tags in `input` do: `none` (stripped, never read out),
`fixed` (the ones in `tags` are rendered, stage directions mapped
onto them, the rest stripped), `free` (every `[tag]` is rendered).

instructions.description:
What `instructions` do: `none` (dropped — said in `x-lmgw-speech`),
`style` (a speaking style for the voice), `voice_design` (the voice
is designed from them), `passthrough` (sent; the model reads them —
it declares an instruction option, or lmgw knows its engine reads
one anyway — and decides what they do).

instructions_required.description:
A request without instructions is refused (`instructions_required`)
unless the row has a default description.

sample_rate.description:
The sample rate of its audio, in Hz, as its last answer through lmgw
said (a streamed answer's PCM has no header of its own; the same
figure is the `x-lmgw-sample-rate` header on it). Absent until the

streaming.description:
`stream_format` (`sse` or `audio`, `response_format: pcm`) works on
this row: it runs in streaming mode.

tags.description: The tags a `fixed` model renders, written `[tag]`.

source.description:
The level the text came from; `row` when the text-to-speech model's
own description stands in for it.

cpu.description:
An audio model that runs on the CPU: the GPU hold does not stop it, a
benchmark run's lease does.

fallback.description:
What answers instead while the model is blocked; `null` off this
machine, or when the model has no usable fallback.

fallback_unusable.description: A fallback the model names that cannot stand in, and why.

inherited.description:
What the levels below the thread give: the alias the thread uses once
its own override is cleared; equal to `alias` when the thread sets
none.

local.description:
`false` for an alias served off this machine; `null` when the alias
does not resolve.

managed.description:
A model lmgw starts itself: the GPU hold and a benchmark run's lease
apply to it.

source.description: The level `alias` came from; `null` with no alias.

oneOf.description: Pick one of the named options.
Rate on 2 to 10 ordered levels.
Yes or no.

SystemOneResponse.description:
`POST /v1/systemone`'s answer, as the upstream sent it.

`model` is the upstream's own: the versioned id that answered on TypeSafe
(`jev-1.13.0`), a dated id on OpenRouter, the server's `--alias` on
llama.cpp. lmgw does not write the requested name back; which alias
answered is `x-lmgw-fallback`'s to say (§2.1).

answers.description: One answer per question, under the question's key.

provider.description: OpenRouter's extension: the provider that answered.

SystemOneUsage.description:
What a request processed: lmgw logs `input_tokens` as the row's prompt
tokens and `output_tokens` as its completion tokens, and prices them from
its own price rows (§2.6).

cost.description:
OpenRouter's extension: what the request cost there, in USD. Relayed,
never read: lmgw prices from its own rows.

output_tokens.description:
Always 0 on llama.cpp; TypeSafe and OpenRouter report a non-zero
count, which Jev's price does not charge.

Takeover.description: `?takeover=`: whether a bind may take its thread from another session.

oneOf.description: Take the thread over (what a bind without the parameter does).
Never: refuse while another session is bound to the thread.

Ask first (WebRTC calls only, realtime calls design §2.8): a thread
held when the call's channel opens makes the call wait,
`lmgw.session.bind_pending`, for the client's
`lmgw.session.take_over` or the holder's end.

Target.description: A device the caller can offer a file to.

last_seen_at.description:
When one of its connections last opened or closed (RFC 3339 UTC);
`null` for one that never connected.

name.description: Its paired name, without `device:`.

online.description:
Whether it holds its Chat feed open now, so it hears an offer at

request.description: Relayed to audio.cpp's generic task endpoint untouched; its shape is the task's own and is not modeled here.

TestUsage.description: A test call's token usage, as the model reported it.

TextCompletion.description: Relayed as the upstream sends it.

TextCompletionChunk.description: One frame, relayed as the upstream sends it: `data: <this object>`, repeated, ending with the literal `data: [DONE]`.

Thread.description:
One Chat thread with what an open thread shows: its list row, what its
voice resolves to now, and (where it is read whole) whether its last
reply can be continued.

agent_id.description: The agent the thread was opened from, if any.

archived_at.description: When the thread was archived; `null` while it is active.

continue.description:

folder_id.description: The folder the thread is in; `null` for none.

kb_budget_tokens.description:

kb_ids.description: Knowledge bases the thread searches, by id.

kind.description:

configuration (never listed for a device key).

last_message_at.description:

thread without messages. An ongoing folder's idle rollover is
measured from it: a client that shows when the conversation moves
on reads it here rather than timing the turns it saw.

mcp_tools.description:

thread with `lmgw` (the self-admin toolset) among them is listed for a
device key only when the device may use lmgw's admin tools.

media_defaults.description:

pinned.description:

voice_resolved.description:

way into the thread.

id.description: lmgw's id of the task: the cancel route's `{task}`.

`working` or `input_required` while it runs; `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled` or `abandoned` once it ended.

status_message.description: The server's last word on it, when it gave one.

task_id.description: The server's id of the task.

ttl_ms.description:
How long the server keeps it, as it stated; `null` when it stated
none.

waiting_for.description:
What it waits for, when it waits: a device that is not connected
(its tasks are asked about again when it links), a turn of the
thread that runs (a result enters the thread once it ended), or the
decision on the calls the thread's last reply waits on.

ThreadVoice.description:
A thread's own voice settings. Every field is optional and absent when
unset: an absent field takes the Chat's voice settings.

asr_alias.description:
The speech-to-text alias for dictation, voice mode and audio
attachments.

language.description:
The language the user speaks, a two-letter ISO 639-1 code, or `auto`
to let the speech-to-text model detect it.

read_aloud.description: Read every reply aloud as it streams.

reply_language.description:
The language replies are in, a two-letter code, or `auto` to follow
the language the user speaks.

seed.description:
The thread's text-to-speech seed, so one thread keeps one voice on a
model that draws its voice. Set on first use.

speech_style.description:
The speaking style the text-to-speech model is given; an empty text
is none for this thread.

tts_alias.description: The text-to-speech alias for read-aloud and voice mode.

voice.description: A voice of that text-to-speech model.

ThreadsFate.description: What a folder delete does with the threads in the folder.

oneOf.description: The threads stay, in no folder.
The threads are deleted with the folder.

Timings.description:
Server-measured prefill and decode timings of a local model: the `stats`
frame (live per token while it streams) and the `done` frame's final
`timings`.

cache_n.description: Prompt tokens served from the KV cache.

draft_n.description: Draft tokens proposed (speculative or MTP decoding).

predicted_ms.description: Milliseconds spent generating; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

predicted_per_second.description: Tokens generated per second; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

prompt_ms.description: Milliseconds spent on the prompt; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

prompt_n.description: Prompt tokens actually processed this turn (the cache excluded).

prompt_per_second.description: Prompt tokens processed per second; absent when llama.cpp gave no finite number.

TokenizeRequest.description: Every key but model is forwarded to the backend's own /tokenize verbatim. Refused with 501 not_supported_error on any backend but a real llama-server — an id from a tokenizer the backend does not run would be a hidden approximation.

content.description: A string, or a mixed array of strings and token ids.

model.description: Required: llama-server's router mode has no other way to pick a backend. A missing model is a 400 naming GET /v1/models.

tokens.description: An array of integer token ids, or — with_pieces — an array of {id, piece} (piece a string, or a byte array when it is not valid UTF-8).

ToolArgsFrame.description: A fragment of a call's JSON arguments, in order.

format.description:
The native syntax family the template renders (`qwen-xml`,
`hermes-json`, …), `provider` for cloud, `unknown` when the template
renders tools with none of the known markers. Informational.

kind.description:
`native` (lmgw returns structured `tool_calls`), `none` (the template
renders no tools; aux/audio rows), `text` (the template renders tools
in a syntax llama-server has no parser for, so calls may arrive as
prose the caller must read itself).

parallel.description:
The template can render more than one call per turn. Absent for cloud
models, which publish nothing about it.

ToolProgressFrame.description:
The `progress` event of a `tool` frame: a running image or audio call's
stage, step and latest preview. Lossy: a reader that falls behind misses
some (the next one supersedes them), and they are not in the change
feed.

call_id.description: The call's id, as its `ready` frame carries it.

cancel.description:
What a cancel would do now, while an image job runs; absent before
the job exists (a cancel then just stops the wait) and for audio.

free_bytes.description: `waiting_for_room`: the memory free when it was last measured.

model.description:
The model the phase is about: the one being unloaded for
`unloading`, the call's own otherwise.

needs_bytes.description: `waiting_for_room`: the memory the model needs, headroom included.

pass.description:
The sampling pass (a batch item, a high- or low-noise stage, a hires
pass); a new pass starts its steps again.

preview.description:
The latest preview as the image server drew it: base64, PNG. Its
pixel size depends on the row's preview mode (a quick sketch is the
latent's size, an eighth of the picture's side on the spike's
pipeline).

queue_position.description: `queued`: the job's place in the image server's queue.

size_note.description:
`downloading`: why the size is not known, when it is not ("size not
known — …").

total_bytes.description:
`downloading`: the download's whole size; absent when it is not
known.

ToolReadyFrame.description:
A Chat `tool` frame whose `event` is `ready` (also the `data` of a bound
realtime session's `lmgw.chat.frame` for it): a call's arguments are
complete, before it runs — what a host that shows the call's view at once
needs (client-apps design §7.5).

call_id.description: The call's id, as its `result` frame carries it.

index.description: The call's position in its turn.

name.description: The tool's exposed name, as the model called it.

needs_approval.description:
The call waits for an approval and does not run now: an `approval`
frame follows. `false` for a call that runs (a resumed turn's decided
calls included). Absent from an lmgw before 2026-10-09.

server_label.description: The label the tool came from; `null` for a client's own function.

ui_resource.description: The UI resource the tool links to, as on the result frame.

ToolResultFrame.description:
A Chat `tool` frame whose `event` is `result` (also the `data` of a
bound realtime session's `lmgw.chat.frame` for it), as an MCP Apps host
reads it. MCP's `CallToolResult` for the view is `{content,
structuredContent: structured_content, isError: is_error}`.

attachments.description:
The files the call stored in the thread — an image or audio tool's
pictures and recordings in a Chat turn — so a page shows them
without reading the thread again. Their bytes are at
`GET /chat/api/attachments/{id}`; `content` names them as
`lmgw:attachment/N` resources. Empty for every other call.

call_id.description: The call's id, as its `ready` frame carries it.

content.description:
The MCP result's `content` blocks as the server sent them (resource
URIs namespaced as `/mcp` sends them; images in full — no bound of
lmgw's own, a device's result is bounded by `mcp.host_max_message_mb`
on its link); a tool lmgw runs itself, or a call that never reached
a server, says its result in the same shape. Absent from an lmgw
before 2026-10-09: `output` as one text block then.

index.description: The call's position in its turn.

name.description: The tool's exposed name (`<prefix>__<tool>`).

server_label.description:
The label the tool came from: a server's tool prefix (else its
name), or a built-in toolset's (`lmgw`, `docs`, `kb`).

structured_content.description:
The MCP result's `structuredContent`, for the view. The model was
given it only when `content` is empty.

task.description: For a call that started an MCP task: which. Absent otherwise.

ui_resource.description:
The UI resource the tool links to (`_meta.ui.resourceUri`),
namespaced as `/mcp` serves it: `resources/read` it there.

id.description: The model's id of the call; only a turn without tools says it.

index.description: The call's position in its turn.

name.description: The tool's exposed name.

app_id.description: The app id the offer names; the receiver declared it at pairing.

end_reason.description:

the offer", "canceled by device 'phone'"), naming no setting and no
raw time; `null` while in progress and once delivered. `state` is
what a client acts on.

ended_at.description: When it ended (RFC 3339 UTC); `null` while in progress.

expires_at.description:

`devices.transfer_expiry_days` after the offer.

filename.description: The receiver's name for the file.

kind.description: The app's own word for what the file is.

received.description:
Bytes lmgw holds: the resume point while `uploading` (the next
upload's range starts here), `size` from `ready` on, and how far it
got for one that ended before.

sha256.description:
The file's sha256, 64 lowercase hex digits; checked when the last
byte arrives.

title.description: What the card and the receiver show; may be empty.

TransferParty.description:
One side of a transfer: the device by its key id, as the owner's
`KeyRow` shows it, and its paired name without `device:`, as it was when
the offer was made.

oneOf.description: Offered to the caller (from `ready` on).
Offered by the caller.

anyOf.description: Offered; the sender uploads its bytes. The receiver does not see it.
Every byte arrived and its sha256 matched: offered to the receiver.
The receiver said it got the bytes; they are deleted.
The receiver declined it; the bytes are deleted.

The sender or the owner canceled it, or a party device was disabled
or deleted; the bytes are deleted.
Not delivered by `expires_at`; the bytes are deleted.
The uploaded bytes' sha256 was not the offer's; they are deleted.
A turn model decides when the speaker is done.
Silence windows only.
A turn is what is spoken while the talk key is held.

threads.description: Stored threads that picked it, archived ones included.

apiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key

bearer.description: An lmgw API key: a client, owner or agent key. A paired device presents none: it authenticates by its client certificate on the device listener, which refuses a bearer there 400 credential_on_device_listener. A bearer key a device was paired with before TLS (lmgw-device-…) is refused 401 device_key_unknown on every listener: pair the device again.

session.description: The dashboard's own session cookie. Same-origin only, and only ever an owner row.
session.name: lmgw_session

info.description: What a developer builds on lmgw: the inference plane (OpenAI-, Anthropic- and llama.cpp-compatible routes, plus MCP), the device (Chat) API a paired client uses, and the run API an agent uses with its own token. The owner's admin plane, the dashboard that configures the gateway, is in the admin document, GET /api/openapi.json.
info.title: lmgw

get.description: One run with its rows: the executor's live buffer while it is in flight, the stored result once it has ended. Ownership is checked before existence, so a run that belongs to another caller and a missing one get the same refusal.

schema.description: `GET /api/agents/runs/{job_id}` — the job plus its rows.

batch.description:
The agent's current review shape, so the table can be drawn from a run
alone — including one finished last week, which is what "reopen this
run's review" needs. For a ledger run its `columns` carry the undeclared
keys the events brought, appended after the declared ones in first-seen
order.

log.description:
The run log: `log` events, rejected events, and the lines lmgw itself
wrote. Empty for an in-process run, which has none yet.

result.description:
The apply step's structured output and the run's usage total, once the
run has finished.

rows.description:
The reviewed rows: the executor's live buffer while running, the job
result after. Rows are deliberately **not** pushed through the generic
jobs feed.

schema.title: AgentRunDetail

post.description: Closes a run this caller owns with its terminal status.

schema.description:
The answer of a write that has nothing to report but that it
happened: `{"ok": true}`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a failure is an error answer instead.

schema.title: Ack

post.description: Appends one ledger event, an array of them, or an NDJSON batch to a run this caller owns, straight into the run's live buffer, which the dashboard's Run tab reads.

schema.description: Newline-delimited JSON: one value per line, each decoded as the application/json form's single-object case.
`POST /api/agents/runs/{job_id}/events` — what became of the batch.

applied.description: How many events went into the run.

ok.description: Always `true`: rejected events are reported below, not failed.

rejected.description:
One line per event the run did not take (unparseable, or refused by
the run's rules), in the order they were sent.

schema.title: AgentEventsApplied

get.description: One agent's full definition: the complete document for owner credentials or, for the agent's own token, the same document with host paths substituted out.

schema.description: `GET /api/agents/{id}` — everything the detail page's three tabs need.

batch.description:
The run surface a `batch` or `container` agent offers. `None` for a
`chat` agent.

budget.description: The two Responses settings a turn is bounded by, shown next to Apply.

config.description:
Stored config values with every `secret` field replaced by
`{ "has_value": bool }`. The value itself never leaves the process.

currency.description:
The gateway's display currency, so a run's cost is printed the way the
Usage page prints every other one.

dev_url.description:
The dev-server override. While it is set, `/agents/<id>/app/**`
goes there and no container is started for the app; runs and applies
still use the image. Empty means "served from the image".

error.description:
Set when the stored manifest could not be read at all — a row written by
a newer build. The document still comes back `200` with whatever could
be read, so the Definition editor stays reachable for the very manifest
that needs fixing; a `400` here would lock the client out of it.

fields.description: The config schema flattened into form fields, in document order.

last_run.description:
The agent's most recent run, with its outcome (`status`, `error`, tokens,
cost) — the same summary the catalog card carries. While a run is in
flight it is that run. Absent when the agent has never run, when
retention pruned its runs, and on a row this build cannot read.

live_job.description: The run in flight, if any.

manifest.description:
The manifest as stored: the canonical serialization, **as text** — what
the Definition editor loads and what Export writes.

Text and not a `serde_json::Value` on purpose. `serde_json::Map` is a
`BTreeMap`, so a `Value` here would alphabetize the config schema's
properties and silently re-sort the form the author laid out.
Parse it client-side if a tree is needed, and post it back to
`agent_set` as a **string**: an object argument is accepted but arrives
already re-sorted, and the import report says so.

portability.description:
Whether an export of this agent would land on another box, and what the
receiver would have to do if not. The same answer the export file's
`portability` key carries, on the page that offers the download.

provenance.description:
Where this row was installed from. `None` for a row that came
from a pasted manifest rather than from an image.

resettable.description: A shipped manifest exists for this id, so "Reset to shipped" applies.

runtime.description: What a `container` agent runs under. `None` for every other kind.

service.description:
Service mode, when the manifest declares it.
`None` means no App tab, no proxy route and no `agent:<id>` MCP row.

token.description:
The agent's own token — its name, whether one has been minted, and the scope it
currently carries. **Never the value**:
that comes from `agent_token_get`, which is what Copy token calls.

warnings.description:
Warnings that are not tool gaps. Start is disabled while any of them carries
`blocks_start`.

schema.title: AgentDetail

get.description: This agent's run history. For the agent's own token, a run's error text has host paths substituted out the same way the detail read does.

post.description: Opens a run from outside lmgw, exactly as the manifest's own trigger would. An agent has at most one live run: a second open while one is live is refused with the running job's id.

schema.description: `POST /api/agents/{id}/runs` — a run opened from outside lmgw.

deadline_seconds.description: How long the run has before lmgw ends it; `0` is no deadline.

run.description:
The run's job id, for `/api/agents/runs/{job_id}` and its events and
close routes.

schema.title: AgentRunOpened

schema.description:
`POST /api/agents/{id}/runs` refused with `409`: the agent already has a
run in flight, and `run` is its job id, so the caller can watch that one.

run.description: The job id of the run that is in flight.

schema.title: AgentRunConflict

409.description: Error, with this body rather than the default one.

get.description: The one /api read a page may do before it has a session: the dashboard's footer and its login view print this.

schema.description: `GET /api/version` — build identity, also serves as the liveness probe.
schema.title: VersionInfo

get.description: The stored file as uploaded, with the media type the bytes were sniffed as (image/png, application/pdf, audio/wav, ...); a text file is served as text/plain; charset=utf-8. The answer carries X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: sandbox, so a file opened in a browser cannot run anything, and Accept-Ranges: bytes. One Range (bytes=a-b, bytes=a- or bytes=-n) answers 206 with Content-Range, as a media player resumes or seeks; a Range lmgw does not read (several ranges, another unit), or any If-Range, serves the whole file. 416 range_not_satisfiable, with Content-Range: bytes */size, for a range that names no byte of the file. 404 not_found for an attachment that is not there or not the caller's.

post.description: Removes an attachment that was not sent yet. 404 not_found for one that is not there or not the caller's; 409 attachment_sent once it was sent with a message (it belongs to that message then).

schema.description:
The answer of a write that has nothing to report but that it
happened: `{"ok": true}`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a failure is an error answer instead.

schema.title: Ack

post.description: Runs one action on a picture of a thread, directly — no chat model is called: reroll draws it again with the same prompt and settings and a new seed (an edit is made again from the picture it started from), vary makes a variation of it on a model without instruction edits and edit changes it by an instruction on a model with them (prompt defaults to the picture's own, strength to its own for vary), upscale runs an ESRGAN upscaler (upscaler: a file stem of the image models dir's upscalers/, the server's first one when omitted; repeats 1 to 4) on a local image model — a resident one that can upscale, preferring the one that made the picture, else that one, else the smallest. The model rows are the caller's. The answer is SSE: `action` first (call_id act-<boot>-<n>, unique across restarts, the action, the model, the source attachment), `progress` frames while it runs (lossy: a newer one supersedes an older), then `done` with the stored picture's attachment metadata and a sentence about it, or `error`. The picture is stored as an attachment of the thread with source action, bound to the source's message, its meta.media naming parent; it is not shown to the thread's model, nor named to it by att:N, unless the user attaches it (a copy as an upload). The action goes on when the stream is closed; a key that is revoked stops it and ends the stream with an `error` frame (code revoked), a gateway that stops ends the stream with code gateway_stopping; a thread deleted or kept as a stored chat while it runs stops it, its `error` code thread_gone, and nothing of it is kept. An upscale whose result would exceed the chosen image model's max_upscale_width/height is refused with too_large, naming the numbers. Refused before any frame: 404 not_found for an attachment that is not there or not the caller's, 422 not_an_image, 409 not_sent for a picture of no message yet (a draft, a reply still being written), 422 no_model, model_unavailable, not_rerollable, source_missing, wrong_action, prompt_required, no_upscaler, no_image_model, unknown_upscaler or bad_request for what the picture or the body lacks.

schema.description:
`POST /chat/api/attachments/{id}/media` (design §8.3): run one action on
a picture of the thread. Every field but `action` is optional; what a
field does not say is the source picture's own (its prompt, its strength)
or the server's (the upscaler, one repeat).

prompt.description: `vary` and `edit`: the prompt, the source's own when omitted.

repeats.description: `upscale`: how many times to run it, 1 to 4 (sd-server's bound).

strength.description:
`vary`: how far to move from the picture, 0 to 1; the source's own
when omitted, else the row's default.

upscaler.description:
`upscale`: the upscaler's name (a file stem of the image models dir's
`upscalers/`); the server's first compatible one when omitted.

schema.title: MediaActionRequest

action.description:
The action stream's first frame (`event: action`): the id the action
runs under — what its progress frames carry as `call_id`, and what the
media cancel route takes — and the model it runs on.

call_id.description:
`act-<boot>-<n>`: `<boot>` 32 random bits (eight hex digits) drawn
once per gateway process, `<n>` a counter, so a later process repeats
an id only if it draws the same bits.

model.description:
The model the action runs on (`image/z-image-turbo`); absent for an
upscale, whose row the gateway picks when it runs (its `done` names
it).

source.description: The attachment the action started from.

action.title: MediaActionStarted

done.description:
The action's last frame on success (`event: done`): the picture it made,
stored as the thread's attachment (`source = "action"`, bound to the
source's message, `meta.media.parent` the source), and a sentence about
it.

text.description: What happened, in words: `Made image att:58 (1024x1024) with …`.

done.title: MediaActionDone

error.description:
`error`: something went wrong; the stream goes on to `done`. `code` is
what a client branches on (`gpu_hold`, `context_length_exceeded`,
`vram_queue_timeout`, `not_saved`, `superseded`, ...); a failure that has
none sends only the message. A stream whose key was disabled, rotated,
deleted or expired, or whose gateway stops, ends with a last `error`
frame instead of `done`: `revoked` (with `kind`) or `gateway_stopping`.
An MCP label the thread or its folder attached that offers the turn no
tools gets one frame each, with `server_label` and a `LabelCode`
(`tool_unreachable`, `tool_offline`, `tool_disabled`, `tool_unknown`,
`tool_failed`), and the turn goes on without it.

kind.description:
What a client does about a `revoked` frame, the token a realtime
session's 4003 close starts its reason with (`key_unknown` means pair
the device again). Sent with `revoked` only.

server_label.description:
The MCP label the frame is about, as the thread or folder attached
it; sent with a `LabelCode` only.

error.title: ErrorFrame

progress.description:
The `progress` event of a `tool` frame: a running image or audio call's
stage, step and latest preview. Lossy: a reader that falls behind misses
some (the next one supersedes them), and they are not in the change
feed.

call_id.description: The call's id, as its `ready` frame carries it.

cancel.description:
What a cancel would do now, while an image job runs; absent before
the job exists (a cancel then just stops the wait) and for audio.

free_bytes.description: `waiting_for_room`: the memory free when it was last measured.

model.description:
The model the phase is about: the one being unloaded for
`unloading`, the call's own otherwise.

needs_bytes.description: `waiting_for_room`: the memory the model needs, headroom included.

pass.description:
The sampling pass (a batch item, a high- or low-noise stage, a hires
pass); a new pass starts its steps again.

preview.description:
The latest preview as the image server drew it: base64, PNG. Its
pixel size depends on the row's preview mode (a quick sketch is the
latent's size, an eighth of the picture's side on the spike's
pipeline).

queue_position.description: `queued`: the job's place in the image server's queue.

size_note.description:
`downloading`: why the size is not known, when it is not ("size not
known — …").

total_bytes.description:
`downloading`: the download's whole size; absent when it is not
known.

progress.title: ToolProgressFrame

post.description: Sets how a PDF whose every page has text goes to the model: mode text sends the extracted text, images sends the pages as images. Drafts only. 400 bad_request for another mode, 404 not_found for an attachment that is not there or not the caller's, 409 attachment_sent once it was sent, 422 mode_not_applicable for any file but a text-class PDF (scanned and hybrid ones, and every other kind, are sent automatically).

schema.description: `POST /chat/api/attachments/{id}/mode`'s body.

mode.description:
`text` sends the PDF's extracted text, `images` its pages as
images.

schema.title: ModeRequest

schema.description: The answer to a mode change.

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

schema.title: ModeSet

post.summary: Choose how a PDF is sent

get.description: A text file as it is, a PDF's or office file's extracted text, or an audio file's transcript, as text/plain; charset=utf-8, with X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: sandbox. 404 not_found for an attachment that is not there or not the caller's, and 404 no_text for an image, or an audio file with no transcript yet.
get.summary: Read what the model reads of an attachment

post.description: Runs the speech-to-text call again for an audio draft, after it failed at upload or once a model is set, and answers the attachment's new `meta` (the transcript's alias and token estimate in place of `transcript_error`). The body is empty. 404 not_found for an attachment that is not there or not the caller's, 409 attachment_sent once it was sent, 422 not_audio for any other kind, 422 stt_not_set when no speech-to-text model is set for the thread, 422 transcription_failed with the call's own message.

schema.description: The answer to a new transcription.

meta.description:
The attachment's `meta` now, the transcript's alias and token
estimate in place of the earlier `transcript_error`. The same object
as `AttachmentMeta::meta`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a refusal is an error answer instead.

schema.title: Transcribed

get.description: A zip with one file per stored thread, in the format asked for (md or json, as for one thread), a directory per folder named after it, and a README.txt. archived=0 takes the active threads, 1 the archived ones, all (the default) both; another value is a 400 bad_request, as is a format other than md, markdown or json. The answer carries Content-Disposition: attachment (lmgw-chats-{date}.zip), Content-Length and Cache-Control: no-store; it is as large as the Chat is and not capped. Temporary threads are not part of a zip. A device key's zip leaves out Admin Chat threads.

schema.description:
Zips only: `0` active threads, `1` archived threads only, `all`
(default) both.

`md` (default; `markdown` is accepted too) for a readable
transcript, `json` for the lossless `lmgw.chat.v1` file. A zip holds
one file of this format per thread.

get.description: One SSE stream per client. `hello` first: the epoch, the cursor the stream continues from, the keep-alive interval and the retention, who the feed is for, the hold, the turns and voice sessions live now, and open_approvals: every call still waiting for a decision at that cursor in a thread the reader may see (a thread's last reply's open calls), each as approval.requested renders it. For a device, hello also carries its own facts: urls (its row's lmgw URLs, https, in the owner's order: replace the stored list with them), cert ({not_after, notice_after}, RFC 3339 UTC, the dates of its certificate: show the notice from them) and dashboard_url (where the dashboard is, as a URL derived from bind_addr: sent to a device paired as this computer, and to any other only when bind_addr is not loopback; null otherwise). A device's feed also sets TCP_USER_TIMEOUT on its connection to its keep-alive, so a keep-alive a vanished device never acknowledges ends the stream within one more interval. Then stored events (thread.*, folder.*, folder.current, message.*, profile.*, approval.*, task.*, device.revoked), each with an `id:` that is its cursor "<epoch>:<seq>:<tag>" (opaque: hand it back as it came), rendered as the thread or folder is when it is delivered (message.added and message.updated carry the thread's id, its title now (thread_title) and the messages the change wrote, whole, as GET /chat/api/threads/{id} lists them now — a user message as stored, a reply once saved (never while it streams), a task result entering the thread, an edit, a continue, a resumed turn, a spoken reply cut to what was heard or annotated, a stored retrieval, a call a reply waits on decided — so a client shows the message or a notification without a fetch; a message gone by delivery is left out, and an event whose messages or thread are all gone is not sent; message.deleted names the ids that went (a delete, the cut of an edit's resend or a regenerate, a spoken reply nobody heard); a thread deleted whole is thread.deleted alone; a profile.* event names the profile's id and name as its write left them; every reader receives it, devices included; approval.requested and approval.decided name a call a turn waits on and its decision, with the call's call_id as the turn's ready, approval and result frames carry it, rendered from the reply (approval.requested with the thread's title now, thread_title, so a client shows it or a notification without a fetch), and are not delivered once the reply is gone (approval.requested neither once its call is decided: the decision follows); task.started names an MCP task a turn's tool call started, task.done its result entering the thread as a message of role tool, both as their write left them; device.revoked names a paired device whose key was deleted, as {kind: device, name}, so a client running work it started (a host of its MCP tasks) may cancel that work — the owner receives every one, a device only one about a device the feed showed it changes of, or that started a task it hosts that was still running; a disable, a rotate or an expiry is no delete and says nothing); and live events (turn.*, voice.*, hold, state, caught_up), which have no id. caught_up {cursor} comes once per stream, when every stored event up to the cursor hello named has been delivered (or passed as not for this reader): right after hello, and the resync and profile list a cursor may owe, when there was nothing to catch up, else right after the catch-up's last event. The approval.* events before it are already reflected in hello.open_approvals; from caught_up on, approval.requested adds to that set and approval.decided removes from it, as does the deletion of its thread or its reply. Every `state` carries open_approvals again, read when it is sent, and replaces that set, matched by approval_request_id (null when lmgw could not read it for a state sent for another reason: keep the set you have; one sent because the set moved ends the stream instead, and the reconnect's hello carries it); the feed sends one after any move of what a device may see, after a thread or folder came into a device's reach (its *.created), and after a resync that passed records — before caught_up when the retention pruned past a stream still catching up, so caught_up hands over the true set. Open the feed first, then load the list: a turn in `hello` may name a thread whose thread.created follows in the catch-up. Resume with ?since=<cursor> or Last-Event-ID (which wins: a browser reconnects with the URL it opened). A cursor the feed cannot honour — another database's, one whose event is not the one the gateway holds at that number now (its data restored from an older copy), older than the retention, newer than the newest — gets `resync` with the reason, then events from now; so does a stream still catching up when the retention prunes past it, and one at an event that cannot be read after a few attempts. Every `resync` is followed by the whole profile list again, as profile.created events without an id. A client that reads live events slower than they happen, past the live buffer, gets `state` instead of the events it missed. Keep-alive comments every keepalive_s seconds: the stream's own when the request asks for one (?keepalive_s=, from 1 to chat_feed_keepalive_max_s, Settings → Chat → Change feed → Longest keep-alive, default 900; outside that a 400 bad_request naming the bound and the setting), else the gateway's chat_feed_keepalive_s; hello.keepalive_s says which. Only the comments follow it: stored events are never held back by a long one. One may carry an `id:` and no data, which only moves the cursor. When the key is disabled, rotated, deleted or expires, `revoked` and the end. When the gateway shuts down, the stream ends without an event: reconnect with the last cursor once it is back. A device key never receives an event about an Admin Chat thread, nor about a folder a device deleted while it held threads the device could not see (until it is shown to devices again); and about a thread or folder with the self-admin toolset (lmgw) attached only while what the device's admin tools may do is above off (hello.self_admin: its level capped by the gateway's self-admin level). The gaps that leaves in the sequence are expected, and a thread in a folder the device does not see is in no folder for it. When a thread or folder leaves a device's reach (the toolset attached), the device receives its deletion, and a fresh `state` when that changed what is live for it; when it comes back (the toolset taken off, the folder shown again), its creation, and the same. When what the device's admin tools may do moves above off (its own level raised, or the gateway's self-admin level raised from off), the threads and folders with the toolset arrive as thread.created and folder.created (and its threads in such a folder as thread.updated), then a fresh `state`; when it moves to off, they go as thread.deleted and folder.deleted, in a delete's order, then a fresh `state`. `state` carries self_admin, what the device's admin tools may do now (its level capped by the gateway's self-admin level), and follows every change of the device's level and every change of the gateway's that moves it, so a connected device learns there that it changed. A device that resumes from a cursor older than a change above off or back gets `resync` at that point instead, and nothing about those threads and folders that it may not see now, or that was written while it could not see them: reload what you show.

schema.description:
Seconds between this stream's keep-alive comments, from 1 to
`chat_feed_keepalive_max_s` (Settings → Chat → Change feed → Longest
keep-alive, default 900); a value outside is a 400 `bad_request`
naming the bound and the setting. Without it the stream keeps the
gateway's `chat_feed_keepalive_s`. `hello.keepalive_s` says the value
the stream keeps. Only the comments follow it: stored events are
read at the gateway's own interval whatever this one is. A phone
holding its feed in the background asks a long one (about 120), so
its radio wakes less.

Resume after this cursor (`"<epoch>:<seq>:<tag>"`). A `Last-Event-ID`
header wins over it: a browser's `EventSource` reconnects with the
URL it opened, so its `since` is the old one and the header the new.

approval.decided.description:
`approval.decided`: a waiting call was decided — approved or declined
by a client, or declined because a new message came
(`chat_approvals::MOVED_ON`).

approve.description:
Whether the call was approved — and, once that is known, could run:
`false` with `not_run` for one approved whose turn could not
start.

by.description:
Who decided, as every author is named ("the dashboard", "device
'phone'").

call_id.description:
The call's id, as `approval.requested` has it. Absent from an lmgw
before 2026-10-09.

not_run.description:
Approved, but the turn that was to run it could not start (its
reply moved on, its starter went, its slot was refused), so it never
ran and its result says so. Recorded as a second `approval.decided`
for the call; both render this.

approval.decided.title: ApprovalDecided

approval.requested.description:
`approval.requested`: a turn in the thread stopped on a call that waits
for an approval (client-apps design §6.5). Rendered from the reply's
pending state at delivery; a reply gone by then (deleted, regenerated),
or a call decided by then (its `approval.decided` follows),
is not delivered. With `thread_title`, `server_label`, `name` and
`arguments` a client shows it, or a notification, without a fetch. Also
the shape of `Hello::open_approvals`' entries.

call_id.description:
The call's id, as the turn's `ready`, `approval` and `result` frames
carry it. Absent from an lmgw before 2026-10-09.

name.description: The tool's own name, as `chat_approvals::ApprovalRequest`.

thread_title.description: The thread's title at delivery (in `hello`, at the head it read).

approval.requested.title: ApprovalRequested

caught_up.description:
`caught_up`: the stream has delivered, or passed as not for this reader,
every stored event up to the head it opened at (`Hello::cursor` when
the client gave no cursor). Live, so no `id:`; sent once per stream: right
after `hello` (and the `resync` and profile list a cursor may owe) when
there was nothing to catch up, else right after the catch-up's last
event. From here on every `approval.*` changes `Hello::open_approvals`.

cursor.description:
Where the stream stands now (`"<epoch>:<seq>:<tag>"`): a client may
resume from it, as from a keep-alive's `id:`.

caught_up.title: CaughtUp

device.revoked.description:
`device.revoked`: a paired device's key was deleted, so the device is
gone for good; a client that runs work it started — a host of MCP tasks
whose `lmgw/caller` named it — may cancel that work now (MCP Tasks
design §4.1; client-apps design §2.2). Its tasks' results still enter
their threads as they end.

Received by the dashboard and admin keys; by a device the feed showed
the deleted device's changes to (a stored event it may see carries the
deleted device's `by`), and by a device hosting a task the deleted
device started that was still running. No other device hears of it: it
names no device the reader was not shown.

Only a delete is said: a disabled or expired key can be enabled or
renewed again, and its tasks wait meanwhile; a rotated one keeps its
row and pairs again under its name; a cleared hosting grant ends the
device's own hosted tasks, each said by its `task.done` (`abandoned`).

device.description:
The deleted device, as `Hello::principal` names a device (kind
`device`, its paired name) and as `lmgw/caller` names it on a
forwarded call; `FeedPrincipal::by` is the `by` its changes
carried.

device.revoked.title: DeviceRevoked

folder.created.description: The folder as GET /chat/api/folders lists it now (its counts as the reader may see them), with `by` beside its fields; or, when the folder is gone by the time the event is delivered, {folder_id, deleted: true, by}. `deleted` tells the two apart.

folder.current.description: `folder.current`: an ongoing folder's current thread moved.

reason.description:
Why it moved. To a new thread: `first` (the folder had none the
reader can reach), `gone` (its thread could no longer be continued
in it; only the dashboard and admin keys read this reason for a new
thread), `idle` (no message for the folder's idle minutes) or
`requested` (a client asked for a new thread, or created one in the
folder). To none: `gone` (the thread was deleted, moved out of the
folder or archived) or `not_ongoing` (the folder stopped being an
ongoing conversation).

thread_id.description: The current thread now; `null` when the folder has none any more.

folder.current.title: FolderCurrent

folder.deleted.description:
`folder.deleted`, and `folder.created` / `folder.updated` for a folder
that is gone by the time the event is delivered.
folder.deleted.title: FolderGone

folder.updated.description: The folder as GET /chat/api/folders lists it now (its counts as the reader may see them), with `by` beside its fields; or, when the folder is gone by the time the event is delivered, {folder_id, deleted: true, by}. `deleted` tells the two apart.

cert.description:
The dates of the certificate the device connected with (§5.3); `null`
on a feed that is not a device's.

cursor.description:
Where the stream continues from: the cursor the client resumed with,
or the newest record when it gave none (or one the feed answers with
`resync`).

dashboard_url.description:
Where the dashboard is, for a client that offers to open it: the
plain listener's address as a URL (`http://127.0.0.1:8001/`), derived
from `bind_addr`. Sent to a device paired as "this computer"
(`local_only`) and to every other device when `bind_addr` is not
loopback, since a loopback address reaches nothing from another host.
`null` otherwise, and on a feed that is not a device's.

hosts_label.description:
The label a device may host MCP tools under; `null` without a
hosting grant, and on a feed that is not a device's.

keepalive_s.description:
Seconds between keep-alive comments, fixed for this stream: the
`keepalive_s` the request asked for, else the gateway's
`chat_feed_keepalive_s`. A client derives its dead-link timeout from
it. Stored events are never held back for it: the stream reads the
table at the gateway's own interval whatever this one is.

open_approvals.description:
Every call still waiting for a decision at `cursor`, in the
threads this reader may see, oldest reply first and each reply's
calls in the model's order, as `approval.requested` renders it (the
thread's title as it was then). Read with the head, so it is the open
set there: the `approval.*` events of the catch-up up to `caught_up`
are already reflected in it; after `caught_up`, `approval.requested`
adds to it and `approval.decided` removes from it, as does the
thread's deletion or its reply's, and every `state` replaces it
(`LiveState::open_approvals`). A waiting call is one of the
thread's last message: a reply a later message followed waits no
more (a new message declines its calls).

retention_days.description:
How many days the feed keeps its records (`chat_feed_retention_days`,
`0` = all): a client away longer gets a `resync`.

self_admin.description:
What this device's admin tools may do now: `off`, `read_only` (read
lmgw's configuration and state) or `full` (also change it) — the
level set on the device, capped by the gateway's own self-admin
level. Above `off` the device sees the threads and folders that
carry the self-admin toolset (`lmgw`), and at `full` it may attach it
and change them; at `read_only` it reads them and sends to them only;
at `off` it sees none of them. When this value moves above `off` or back while
the feed is open, whether the device's level or the gateway's moved
it, those threads and folders arrive (`*.created`) or go
(`*.deleted`) in order. A `state` with this value follows any change
of the device's level, and any change of the gateway's that moves
this value. When this value moved above `off` or back within what a
resumed feed catches up, the feed sends `resync` at that point
instead: reload what you show. `off` on a feed that is not a
device's.

urls.description:
A device's lmgw URLs as its row holds them now: `https` base URLs in
the owner's order (device link design §7.2). The device replaces its
list with them (`lmgw-client`'s `refresh_urls`). Empty on a feed that
is not a device's.

voice.description: The realtime sessions bound now.

hold.description:
The GPU hold: whether local models are paused. A held model answers with
its own fallback, where one is set (each thread's model says which). The
`hold` event and part of `Hello`.

active.description: The owner's GPU hold is on: models on the graphics card are paused.

benchmark.description:
A benchmark run holds the graphics card: every local model waits
until it ends, one on the CPU too, or answers with its fallback
(chat-plane design D6).

hold.title: FeedHold

message.added.description:
`message.added` and `message.updated`: messages of a thread were written
(client-apps design §2.2). Added: a user message as it is stored (typed,
dictated or spoken in a bound session), a reply as it is saved, a late
MCP task result entering the thread (role `tool`). Updated in place: an
edit, a continue, a resumed turn saved onto its reply, a spoken reply
cut to what was heard or annotated with how it was spoken, a user
message's retrieval stored, a call the reply waits on decided (or
declined by a new message, or closed as not run). A reply still being
generated is in no event until it is saved: its tokens are the send
stream's.

Rendered at delivery, so a catch-up never replays a stale copy: each
message as `GET /chat/api/threads/{id}` lists it now, whole, so a client
shows it, or a notification, without a fetch. A message gone by then is
left out (its `message.deleted` follows), and an event whose messages
are all gone, or whose thread is, is not delivered. Two events may carry
the same state of a message: apply them by id.

by.description:
Who wrote them: the sender of a user message, the starter of the
turn whose reply it is, the client that edited one or decided a call,
the client whose voice session cut or annotated a spoken reply (that
session's, even after another client took the thread over); `null`
for the gateway's own (a task result entering the thread, a call
closed as not run).

messages.description: The messages written, oldest first, each as the thread lists it now.

thread_title.description:
The thread's title at delivery, so a notification names the
conversation without a fetch.

message.added.title: MessagesChanged

message.deleted.description:
`message.deleted`: messages of a thread were deleted (client-apps design
§2.2): one by itself, every one after a point (an edit's resend, a
regenerate), or a spoken reply nobody heard. Their attachments went with
them. A thread deleted whole says so with `thread.deleted` alone.

by.description: Who deleted them; `null` for the gateway's own.

message.deleted.title: MessagesDeleted

message.updated.description:
`message.added` and `message.updated`: messages of a thread were written
(client-apps design §2.2). Added: a user message as it is stored (typed,
dictated or spoken in a bound session), a reply as it is saved, a late
MCP task result entering the thread (role `tool`). Updated in place: an
edit, a continue, a resumed turn saved onto its reply, a spoken reply
cut to what was heard or annotated with how it was spoken, a user
message's retrieval stored, a call the reply waits on decided (or
declined by a new message, or closed as not run). A reply still being
generated is in no event until it is saved: its tokens are the send

the client whose voice session cut or annotated a spoken reply (that

thread_title.description:
The thread's title at delivery, so a notification names the
conversation without a fetch.
