profile.created.description:
`profile.created`, `profile.updated` and `profile.deleted`: a
personality profile (`GET /chat/api/profiles`) was created, changed or
deleted, named as that write left it. Every reader receives them,
devices included. After a `resync` the feed sends the whole list again
as `profile.created` events (with no `id:`), so a client that keeps the
names (a menu of profiles) has them again without a request.

by.description:
Who made the change; `null` for the gateway's own, and on the list
repeated after a `resync`.

profile.created.title: FeedProfile

profile.deleted.description:
`profile.created`, `profile.updated` and `profile.deleted`: a
personality profile (`GET /chat/api/profiles`) was created, changed or
deleted, named as that write left it. Every reader receives them,
devices included. After a `resync` the feed sends the whole list again
as `profile.created` events (with no `id:`), so a client that keeps the
names (a menu of profiles) has them again without a request.

by.description:
Who made the change; `null` for the gateway's own, and on the list
repeated after a `resync`.

profile.deleted.title: FeedProfile

profile.updated.description:
`profile.created`, `profile.updated` and `profile.deleted`: a
personality profile (`GET /chat/api/profiles`) was created, changed or
deleted, named as that write left it. Every reader receives them,
devices included. After a `resync` the feed sends the whole list again
as `profile.created` events (with no `id:`), so a client that keeps the
names (a menu of profiles) has them again without a request.

by.description:
Who made the change; `null` for the gateway's own, and on the list
repeated after a `resync`.

profile.updated.title: FeedProfile

resync.description:
`resync`: the cursor cannot be honoured; reload what you show. The
stream continues from now.
resync.title: Resync

revoked.description:
`revoked`: the key was disabled, rotated, deleted or expired; the stream
ends after it.

kind.description:
What a client does about it, the token a realtime session's 4003
close starts its reason with: `key_unknown` means pair the device
again. Every event this gateway sends carries it. An event without it
(an older gateway's) is of an unknown kind, as a close reason without
a token is: tell the user the sentence in `message`.

message.description:
The reason in a sentence: "device 'phone' was rotated — pair it
again".

revoked.title: Revoked

state.description:
`state`: `Hello`'s live part again. Sent when the stream could not
keep a client's live events in order — it read slower than they
happened past `chat_feed_live_buffer`, or the buffer was resized — and
to a device when what it may see or do changed: a thread it reaches took
or lost the self-admin toolset, its own admin-tools level moved, or the
gateway's self-admin level moved what its admin tools may do. Also after
a `resync` that passed records (the retention pruned past a stream still
catching up, which gets it before `caught_up`; a change that could not be
read, after `caught_up`), and to a device after a thread or folder came
into its reach after `caught_up` (its `*.created`), so the open
approvals in it arrive.
Stored events are never lost; `reason` says what happened and names the
setting.

open_approvals.description:
The calls waiting for a decision as they are when this `state` is
sent, in the threads this reader may see now, as
`Hello::open_approvals` lists them: they replace the set a client
keeps. Read at sending, which may be a little past the stream's
cursor: match by `approval_request_id`, and an `approval.*` event
that follows changes nothing it already says. `null` when lmgw
could not read them for a `state` sent for another reason (a lag, a
resize, a refresh of what is live; said in its log): keep the set
you have. A `state` sent because the set may have moved never says
`null`: lmgw ends the stream instead, and the reconnect's `hello`
carries the set.

self_admin.description:
`Hello::self_admin` as it is now: a device learns here that what
its admin tools may do moved while the feed is open.

state.title: LiveState

task.done.title: TaskDone

task.started.description:
`task.started`: a tool call of a turn in the thread became an MCP task
(MCP Tasks design §4.1); its result enters the thread later. Named as
the write left it, so it renders after the task is gone.

by.description: Who started the turn that called it.

id.description: lmgw's id of the task (the cancel route's `{task}`).

task_id.description: The server's id of the task.

task.started.title: TaskStarted

thread.created.description: The thread as GET /chat/api/threads lists it now, with `by` beside its fields; or, when the thread is gone by the time the event is delivered, {thread_id, deleted: true, by}. `deleted` tells the two apart.

thread.deleted.description:
`thread.deleted`, and `thread.created` / `thread.updated` for a thread
that is gone by the time the event is delivered.

by.description: Who made the change; `null` for the gateway's own (the sweep).

thread.deleted.title: ThreadGone

thread.updated.description: The thread as GET /chat/api/threads lists it now, with `by` beside its fields; or, when the thread is gone by the time the event is delivered, {thread_id, deleted: true, by}. `deleted` tells the two apart.

transfer.updated.description: A transfer, as every route and `transfer.updated` answer it.

app_id.description: The app id the offer names; the receiver declared it at pairing.

end_reason.description:
Why it ended, a sentence for people ("not delivered within 7 days of
the offer", "canceled by device 'phone'"), naming no setting and no
raw time; `null` while in progress and once delivered. `state` is
what a client acts on.

ended_at.description: When it ended (RFC 3339 UTC); `null` while in progress.

expires_at.description:
When it expires unless delivered first (RFC 3339 UTC):
`devices.transfer_expiry_days` after the offer.

filename.description: The receiver's name for the file.

kind.description: The app's own word for what the file is.

received.description:
Bytes lmgw holds: the resume point while `uploading` (the next
upload's range starts here), `size` from `ready` on, and how far it
got for one that ended before.

sha256.description:
The file's sha256, 64 lowercase hex digits; checked when the last
byte arrives.

title.description: What the card and the receiver show; may be empty.

transfer.updated.title: Transfer

code.description:
The code of the last error the turn reported (`superseded`,
`gpu_hold`, `not_saved`, …); `null` when it reported none.

message_id.description: The reply row it saved or continued; `null` when it saved none.

voice.description: A bound realtime session's voice turn.

voice.bound.description: `voice.bound`: a realtime session bound to the thread.
voice.bound.title: VoiceBound

voice.ended.description: `voice.ended`: a bound session let its thread go.

by.description: Who had bound the session that ended.

reason.description:
`closed`, `taken_over`, `thread_gone` (its thread was deleted while
it was bound; a device's feed does not receive this event for a
deleted thread, only its `thread.deleted`, as for a thread taken out
of its reach) or `revoked` (the binder's key was revoked, or the
thread was taken out of the binding device's reach).

voice.ended.title: VoiceEnded

get.description: Every folder in the list's order: its defaults (what a new thread in it starts with), whether it is one ongoing conversation and which thread is current, its own retention, and its thread counts as the caller may see them. Folder names need not be unique, so a client that looks its folder up by name keeps the id it found.

schema.description: `GET /chat/api/folders`.
schema.title: FolderList

post.description: A new folder, last in the list, answered as the list carries it. `ongoing` marks it as one ongoing conversation, which needs a model in its defaults: without one the answer is a 400 naming defaults.model_alias. A device key writes only within its own scopes: a tool server or knowledge base its tool scope does not reach is a 403 tool_label_out_of_scope, an alias outside its alias scope a 403 key_scope, and the self-admin toolset (lmgw) is its to attach only when its admin tools are full: below that the answer is a 403 chat_toolset_needs_full, or tool_label_out_of_scope when they are off. A device key only tightens require_approval: a rule that gates fewer calls than the stored one or the owner's last (its floor, which a removed entry keeps) is a 403 approval_loosen_refused, naming the label and the tool; a turn runs each server under the strictest of its entries and that floor. For every caller, two mcp_tools entries that name one server (its tool prefix and its name) or a require_approval of another shape than OpenAI's are a 400 bad_request where the write changed the entry; labels are stored trimmed. A device key cannot set archive_days or purge_days (403 forbidden, naming the fields): a folder's own retention is set from the dashboard.

schema.description: `POST /chat/api/folders`'s body.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; absent
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. A device key cannot set it (403
forbidden): a folder's own retention is set from the dashboard.

ongoing.description:
Marks the folder as one ongoing conversation; its defaults must then
name a model.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; absent
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. A device key cannot set it, as
`archive_days`.

schema.title: FolderCreate

schema.description:
A Chat folder as `GET /chat/api/folders` lists it, with its thread
counts as the caller may see them.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

schema.title: Folder

post.description: A patch: a field left out is unchanged. Answers the folder as the list carries it, with `applied`: for an ongoing-conversation folder whose defaults changed (and apply_to_current not false), the current thread and the settings that reached it, otherwise null. The folder's other threads are never touched. defaults replaces the defaults whole; defaults_patch changes the fields it names (null unsets one) so a client never writes back what another changed meanwhile; both together are a 400 bad_request. ongoing needs a model in the defaults. What reaches the current thread passes the checks of a thread settings write, and a field the thread refuses fails the whole patch. A device key's default mcp_tools pass its tool scope, as on a folder create; it cannot set archive_days or purge_days, nor devices_hidden (403 forbidden). devices_hidden: false shows a folder to devices again that a device's delete hid from them; true is a 400. A folder the caller cannot see is a 404 not_found.

schema.description:
`POST /chat/api/folders/{id}`'s body: a **patch**. An absent field is
unchanged. Unknown fields are a 422 bad_request.

apply_to_current.description:
For an ongoing folder: also apply the defaults' changes to its
current thread. Default `true`.

archive_days.description:
The folder's own retention in days before an inactive thread is
archived; `null` goes back to the Chat's setting, `0` never. A device
key cannot set it (403 `forbidden`).

defaults.description:
Replaces the folder's defaults whole (`{}` clears them). Not beside
`defaults_patch`.

defaults_patch.description:
Changes the defaults field by field instead: each field given
replaces the stored one (`null` unsets it), the others stay as
stored, so a save of the fields one client changed never writes back
what another changed meanwhile. `voice` is laid field by field the
same way (`voice: null` unsets the whole voice). Not beside
`defaults`.

devices_hidden.description:
`false` shows a folder that a device's delete hid from devices to
them again; the owner's alone. `true` is refused (400): a device's
delete is what hides a folder.

name.description: The new name; names need not be unique.

ongoing.description:
An object marks the folder as one ongoing conversation (or changes
its idle minutes; its defaults must name a model); `null` ends that.

purge_days.description: Days after archiving before a thread is deleted; as `archive_days`.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

schema.title: FolderPatch

schema.description:
`POST /chat/api/folders/{id}`'s answer: the folder as the list carries
it, and what the patch applied to its current thread.

applied.description:
For an ongoing folder whose defaults changed: the current thread
and the settings that reached it; `null` otherwise.

archive_days.description:
Days without activity before one of its threads is archived; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

devices_hidden.description:
Set when a device deleted this folder while it held threads that
device could not see: the folder stays for them, hidden from every
device, until it is shown to devices again from the dashboard. Always
`false` for a device key, which never sees such a folder.

name.description: Folder names need not be unique.

ongoing.description: `null` for a folder that is not one ongoing conversation.

purge_days.description:
Days after archiving before one of its threads is deleted; `null`
for the Chat's setting, `0` never. Set from the dashboard: a device
key cannot change it.

sort.description: The folder's place in the list.

schema.title: FolderPatched

post.description: The thread every client of an ongoing-conversation folder continues in. A new one starts when the folder has none the caller can reach (first), when no message came for the folder's idle minutes while no turn runs there (idle), or on new: true (requested) — except that a current thread with no message yet is answered instead, so no empty threads pile up. The body may be left out: it is new: false. A new thread starts from the folder's defaults, and every client hears of it as the feed's folder.current. Two clients asking at once get the same thread. A folder that is not an ongoing conversation is a 409 not_ongoing, one whose defaults name no model a 409 folder_no_model, and one the caller may not see a 404.

schema.description: `POST /chat/api/folders/{id}/current`'s body.

new.description:
Start a new thread now. A current thread without any message is
answered instead, so no empty threads pile up.

schema.title: CurrentRequest

schema.description: `POST /chat/api/folders/{id}/current`'s answer.

note.description:
The same in a sentence that names the folder setting behind it (the
idle minutes, for `idle`); `null` when this call did not start it.

reason.description: Why this call started it; `null` when it did not.

thread.description:
The current thread, as `GET /chat/api/threads/{id}` answers its
`thread`.

schema.title: CurrentThread

post.summary: Get an ongoing conversation's current thread

post.description: threads: keep leaves the folder's threads in no folder, threads: delete deletes them with it; there is no default for destroying conversations. A device key's delete touches only the threads it can see: a folder that also holds Admin Chat or self-admin threads it cannot reach stays for them, hidden from every device from then on, and the answer is the same ok. A folder the caller cannot see is a 404 not_found.

schema.description:
`POST /chat/api/folders/{id}/delete`'s body. The choice is required:
there is no default for destroying conversations.
schema.title: FolderDelete

schema.description:
The answer of a write that has nothing to report but that it
happened: `{"ok": true}`.

ok.description: Always `true`; a failure is an error answer instead.

schema.title: Ack

get.description: A zip with one file per stored thread of the folder, in the format asked for (md or json, as for one thread), and a README.txt. archived=0 takes the active threads, 1 the archived ones, all (the default) both; another value is a 400 bad_request, as is a format other than md, markdown or json. The answer carries Content-Disposition: attachment (lmgw-folder-{name}-{date}.zip), Content-Length and Cache-Control: no-store; it is as large as the folder is and not capped. Temporary threads are not part of a zip. A device key's zip leaves out Admin Chat threads; a folder that is not there, or not the caller's to see, is a 404 not_found.

schema.description:
Zips only: `0` active threads, `1` archived threads only, `all`
(default) both.

`md` (default; `markdown` is accepted too) for a readable
transcript, `json` for the lossless `lmgw.chat.v1` file. A zip holds
one file of this format per thread.

get.description: Every knowledge base with its file counts and whether its embedding model still resolves (without one a search is by keyword only), for a thread's Knowledge section and the composer's # picker. A thread's bases are its own choice, so a base's MCP visibility does not narrow the list. A device key reads the bases only with kb__search within its tool scope, the tool a thread's base is searched with: without it the answer is 403 tool_label_out_of_scope, naming the tool and no base.

schema.description:
`GET /chat/api/knowledge/bases`: the knowledge bases a thread may
search, for the Chat's Knowledge section, its `#` picker and its chips.
schema.title: ChatKnowledgeBases

get.summary: List the knowledge bases a thread may search

get.description: The uploaded bytes, with the media type they were sniffed as and Content-Disposition: attachment under the file's name (an ASCII fallback plus the RFC 5987 filename*). The owner's: a device key is refused (403 forbidden, said before the file is looked up), since the original carries more than any kb tool hands out; it reads the extracted text. 404 not_found for a file that does not exist or whose original is gone from disk.

The source viewer a citation opens: the file's extracted text (null until it has been ingested once), every chunk's byte range in it, and the chunk named by `chunk` as `highlight`; a citation whose chunk id a re-ingest renamed is found again by its stored span_start, span_end and sha, and `notice` says so. The file is described by what the viewer shows (name, kind, status, pages), without its ingest record; `original` says whether the caller may download the original. A device key reads it only with kb__search and kb__read within its tool scope and kb__read switched on by the owner (403 tool_label_out_of_scope otherwise, said before the file is looked up). 400 op_failed for a file that does not exist.

schema.description: The chunk to highlight (a citation's chunk id).
... and the file's sha256 when it was cited.
... its end ...

What a citation stored besides the chunk id, for one whose chunk id a
re-ingest renamed: the passage's start (byte offset into the text) ...

`GET /chat/api/knowledge/files/{id}/text`: a cited file's extracted text,
as the Chat's source viewer shows it. The Knowledge page's own answer
(`KnowledgeSource`) also carries the file's ingest record — its error,
its notes, its size and digest — which can name the models and upstreams
that ingested it; the Chat's carries what the viewer shows.

chunks.description: Every chunk's span, in file order.

highlight.description: The cited chunk (or the one found by the citation's position).

kb_name.description: The base the file is in.

notice.description:
Said when the highlight is not the cited chunk itself: it was found by
the citation's stored position because the chunk id no longer exists.

original.description:
Whether this caller may download the file's original
(`GET /chat/api/knowledge/files/{id}/original`): the owner may, a
device key not yet.

text.description: The extracted text; `null` until the file has been ingested once.

schema.title: ChatKnowledgeSource

get.summary: Read a knowledge file's extracted text

get.description: Which model image__generate, image__edit, audio__speak and audio__transcribe use when a call leaves out `model`, and the voice audio__speak uses when it leaves out `voice`. Three levels, the narrowest that says something winning: a thread's own (its settings' media_defaults), its folder's (the folder defaults' media_defaults, read at each turn rather than copied), Settings → Chat's (chat_media_defaults). In a thread or a folder an absent field inherits and an empty one is no default. The answer has Settings' always, ?folder=<id> adds a folder's and ?thread=<id> a thread's and its folder's; `inherited` is what the narrowest level asked takes from above it, `resolved` what a call uses now, and `choices` every model each tool's `model` enum offers this caller (a device key's alias scope narrows it), with a label and each speech row's voices. A stored default that no longer resolves — its model switched off or deleted, an alias that lost the route, a model outside the caller's key scope, a voice its model does not have — is listed under `unavailable` with the reason and is no default: the tool requires `model` again, and no other model is put in its place. A folder or thread the caller does not reach is 404 not_found.

What a call that leaves the argument out uses now at the narrowest

unavailable.description:
Every stored name in the levels above that does not resolve, with

Only stored threads are answered: a temporary id, one that is not there and one out of the caller's reach are left out, so a missing row is never an error. post.description: A tool whose MCP server runs it as a task (its execution.taskSupport is required) answers the turn at once: its result frame's output is `started, job <task_id>` and carries task {id, task_id, server_label}, and the turn goes on. lmgw follows the task; when it ends, its result enters the thread as a message of role `tool` with task {task_id, server_label, tool, status: completed | failed | cancelled | abandoned, ended_by}, its content the result as text — only while no turn of the thread runs (a turn that runs takes it in when it ends; one that starts, before it reads the history), and not while the thread's last reply waits for approvals or for the turn that runs the calls decided on it. The feed records task.started and task.done. Every later turn sees it as a call of lmgw__job_result and its result, in chronological order: where it is stored among the thread's messages, so a message sent after it follows it; an edit or a regenerate keeps it, and the reply after it answers it again. lmgw starts no turn for a result: this route asks for one, a continuation with no new user message, streaming the frames a send streams; a send answers it too. It needs a result nothing answered yet (a result row with no reply after it, or one waiting to enter the thread), else 409 nothing_to_answer; while a turn of the thread runs it is 409 turn_running (that turn's end lets the results in, and its reply may answer them). It runs on the thread's alias with its configured fallbacks, as every turn does. The body may be empty; speak reads the answer aloud as a send's does. GET /chat/api/threads/{id} lists the thread's tasks still running or waiting to enter it as `tasks` (ThreadTask: id, task_id, server_label, tool, status, status_message, ttl_ms, started_at, by, waiting_for). A temporary thread's calls wait for their task instead, within the server's timeout_ms.

reasoning_note.description: The model reasoned although off was asked, in a sentence.

deleted or expired, or whose gateway stops, ends with a last `error`
frame instead of `done`: `revoked` (with `kind`) or `gateway_stopping`.
An MCP label the thread or its folder attached that offers the turn no
tools gets one frame each, with `server_label` and a `LabelCode`
(`tool_unreachable`, `tool_offline`, `tool_disabled`, `tool_unknown`,
`tool_failed`), and the turn goes on without it.

post.description: A thread's MCP tools may wait for an approval (the thread's mcp_tools entry's require_approval: "never", "always" or {always: {tool_names}, never: {tool_names}}, as OpenAI's; any other shape, read_only included, is refused, and a device key may only tighten it, 403 approval_loosen_refused). A turn that calls one stops: it streams a tool frame {event: approval, approval_request_id, server_label, name, arguments, call_id} for each waiting call (call_id the id the call's ready and result frames carry) and done {pending_approvals}, and saves its reply with them; the other calls of that model turn wait with them. The thread's messages list them as the reply's pending_approvals, and the feed records approval.requested, each with the call_id. This route takes a verdict for every waiting call and resumes the turn as a continuation, streaming the frames a send streams (delta, reasoning, tool, usage, stop, error, done): the declined calls are answered "The user declined this tool call: <reason>", the approved ones and the calls that waited with them run, and the model answers; what it adds is appended to the same reply. The resumed turn runs as the principal that started it — its scope, key policy and attribution — whoever approves. The approver is on each approved call's request row (approved_by), in the feed's approval.decided, and in _meta["lmgw/approval"] {decision: approved, by: {kind, name}} of a call forwarded to a device-hosted server; a call nobody approved carries null there. The first decision wins: a call decided already is 409 approval_decided, naming who decided. A body that is not JSON is 400 bad_request, JSON of another shape 422 bad_request. A waiting call without a verdict is 400 approval_missing, naming each; an id nothing waits under 404 approval_not_found; a starter whose key is gone or disabled 409 approval_starter_unavailable, naming it (nothing is decided then; nor when the starter's key is at its concurrency limit, its 429 key_rate); a reply that is no longer the thread's last message 409 approval_moved_on. A device approves only within its own reach: a call its key's tool scope does not admit, or one of lmgw's admin tools unless its own admin tools may do everything (full, capped by the gateway's level), is 403 approval_out_of_scope, naming each, and nothing of the request is decided; declining is open to any client that sees the thread. A decided turn that never starts closes its calls as not run, and the feed's approval.decided says approve: false, not_run: true for an approved one. A new message in the thread declines whatever still waits, "the user moved on without deciding", so every call is answered. speak reads the resumed reply aloud as a send's does.

post.description: The body is the file's bytes, not multipart; ?name= is its name. The kind is sniffed from the bytes (image, text, pdf, office, audio), never taken from the name or the Content-Type. The file is stored as a draft of the thread, to be sent with the next message (`attachments` of POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/send), and answered as its metadata, with `blockers` and `hints` saying what the thread's current model cannot take. A PDF is read at upload (text-class, scanned or hybrid in `meta.class`; a text-class one starts with the Chat's PDF mode, or none to ask), an office file likewise, and an audio file is transcribed at once when its model cannot hear it and a speech-to-text model is set (a failure is `meta.transcript_error`, not a refusal). The body is bounded by max_body_mb (413 body_limit naming it, for a declared or a chunked body). 400 empty_attachment for an empty file, 404 not_found for a thread that is not there or not the caller's, 415 unsupported_attachment for bytes of no supported kind, 422 extract_failed (the file could not be read) or tool_missing (the PDF reader is not installed).

schema.description:
The file's name, shown on its chip and kept in an export. The kind
is sniffed from the bytes, never taken from the name or a content
type. Blank is stored as `untitled`.
One attachment's metadata, never its bytes.

blockers.description: For a draft: why it cannot be sent to the thread's current model.

call_id.description:
The tool call that made a `tool` file, or the card action that made
an `action` file (its `act-<boot>-<n>` id, the one its stream's
frames carried); absent for an upload.

extracted_tokens.description: The extracted text's token estimate; `null` when there is none.

hints.description:
For a draft: what it becomes on the way, sent all the same (an image
as a placeholder, a PDF's pages as its text) under a fallback that
cannot see.

kind.description: `image`, `pdf`, `text`, `audio`, ... as the upload was classified.

meta.description:
What extraction found: pages, text-less pages, class, sheets,
transcript alias or error, tokens. `{}` for an image.

mode.description:
A text-class PDF's choice, `text` or `images`; `null` when it does
not apply or is not chosen yet.

source.description:
Where the file came from: `upload` (the user sent it), `tool` (an
image or audio tool of a turn made it) or `action` (an image card's
action made it).

schema.title: AttachmentMeta

post.description: The model continues the thread's last reply (an assistant prefill) and streams the continuation only: the delta frames are what is added, done's message_id is the continued reply, and the stored reply's text and reasoning grow by what came (its token counts become this call's). The body is optional (a body that is not JSON is 400 bad_request, JSON of another shape 422 bad_request); with `speak` the continuation is read aloud as it streams, from the clause the reply broke off in. 409 continue_unavailable when the thread's `continue` state says no (its reason is the message): there is no reply yet, the last message is not a reply, the reply ran tools, or the thread's model cannot take a prefill. The same code answers a reply that stopped being the last message meanwhile. A route the request is re-routed to that cannot take a prefill is refused in the stream, with an error frame. 404 not_found, and a device key's own refusals. The frames are those of a send, without the `turn` frame.

schema.description:
The optional body of a continue and of a regenerate; an empty request is
accepted.

speak.description: Read the answer aloud as it streams.

post.description: Stops the image or audio tool call {call_id} (the call_id of its tool frames) of the turn that runs in the thread, as the turn's Stop stops it, without stopping the turn: the call's result tells the model the picture was not made, and the turn goes on. It also stops a card action of the thread (POST /chat/api/attachments/{id}/media), named by the act-<boot>-<n> id of its stream's action frame; the action's stream then ends with an error frame and nothing is stored. A running image job is cancelled by what its image server can do, which the call's last `progress` frame named as `cancel` and the answer repeats: native, the server's own cancel (the model stays loaded); restart, the server cannot stop a running picture and this call is the model's only request, so lmgw stops its container and the next picture loads it again; abandon, another request uses the model, so the call stops waiting and the picture finishes in the background and is thrown away. An upscale has no job: restart or abandon by the same rule, an abandoned one holding its claim until the image server is done. No `cancel` in the answer: no job ran yet (the call was loading its model or waiting for room, and stops waiting), or an audio call. The body is ignored. A thread the caller does not reach is 404 not_found; a call that is not running, 404 not_running.

post.description: What the answer is depends on the message. A reply is rewritten in place and nothing is sent: its reasoning, token counts and tool record are cleared, since they no longer describe the text, and so are a spoken reply's unheard rest and timing; the answer is JSON, `ok` and the message as the thread lists it. A user message is rewritten in place (its attachments stay bound), every later message is deleted, and it is answered again: the answer is the event stream of a send, opening with a `turn` frame. An empty text is a 400 empty_message unless the message carries files. Its stored knowledge retrieval goes with the old text, so auto mode searches again; kb_refs, when sent, replaces its `#` picks. A dictated message whose text changed becomes a typed one. Everything that can refuse happens before anything is written. Any other role is a 400 bad_request. A device key below full admin level edits no message of a thread with lmgw's admin tools (403 chat_toolset_needs_full); its kb_refs pass its tool scope. A thread or message that is not there is a 404 not_found.

post.description: Cuts the thread at the message and streams a new answer. On a reply, it and every later message are deleted and the model answers the history before it, which has to end with a user message (or a job's result): 409 nothing_to_answer otherwise, and nothing is deleted. On a user message, every later message is deleted, it is answered again, and the stream opens with a `turn` frame carrying its id. Any other role is 400 bad_request; 404 not_found for a thread or message that is not there; a device key below full admin level changes no message of a thread with lmgw's admin tools (403 chat_toolset_needs_full). The model's capabilities are read before anything is cut. The body is optional (a body that is not JSON is 400 bad_request, JSON of another shape 422 bad_request); with `speak` the answer is read aloud as it streams. The frames are those of a send.

post.description: Reads the reply as it is shown (its content, then a spoken reply's unheard rest) with the thread's text-to-speech model and voice, and streams the audio as it is made: `state` while the speech model is not resident (loading, then ready, fallback, held or failed), `voice` once its route is open, a `speech` frame per clause (seq counting from 0, the text said, pcm: base64 PCM16 little-endian, 24 kHz, mono) and `speech_done` with the totals. A thread that cannot speak (no speech model, no such voice, a voice that needs instructions) and a voice that fails mid-way end with a `speech_error` frame (codes tts_not_configured, voice_not_found, voice_not_configured, instructions_required, or the failure's kind). One speech row is written per call. Closing the stream stops the synthesis at its next step; POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/speech/stop stops every read-aloud of the thread. A device or owner key that is disabled, rotated, deleted or expired while it streams, and a gateway that stops, end the stream with a last `error` frame (code revoked, with `kind`, or gateway_stopping). Refused before any frame: 404 not_found (thread or message), 400 bad_request (the message is not a reply), 400 empty_message (a reply with no text).

post.description: Writes the user message (with the draft attachments it binds and the knowledge bases it picks) and streams the model's answer. The message is stored before the model is called, so a client that goes away has still recorded what it asked; an untitled thread is titled from it. `content` may be empty when attachments are bound. A dictated message names its origin in `voice` (via: dictation); with `speak`, the reply is read aloud as it streams and the stream also carries voice, speech, speech_done and speech_error frames (the speech frames' audio is base64 PCM16, 24 kHz, mono). The first frame is `turn` with the user message's id. Refused before anything is written: 400 empty_message (no text and no attachment), 400 bad_request (a knowledge base that does not exist), 400 attachment_not_draft (an id that is no draft of the thread), 400 model_no_vision (a new image and a model that cannot see), 422 attachment_blocked (a file the thread's model cannot take, named), 404 not_found and a device key's own refusals (its scope, its budget). A body that is not JSON is 400 bad_request, JSON of another shape (an unknown or mistyped field, `voice` included) 422 bad_request, and a `voice.via` other than dictation (realtime, say) 400 bad_request. 409 attachment_not_draft: a concurrent send took a draft first. A turn that fails after the stream began says so in an error frame. The answer is a server-sent event stream; every frame's data is JSON of the type its event name has below. state: a model stage loading, held, falling back or failing (the thread's model); retrieval: what the knowledge bases found for the user message, before the model answers; delta: a piece of the answer; reasoning: a piece of the model's reasoning; tool: a tool call of the turn, by its `event` (start, args, ready, approval, result); usage: the token counts so far; stop: why the model stopped; stats: a local model's timings; error: a failure, the stream goes on to done — one per MCP label the thread or its folder attached that offers the turn no tools, with its server_label and a code (tool_unreachable: a paired device's tools the caller is not granted, or a server its tool scope keeps out; tool_offline; tool_disabled; tool_unknown; tool_failed), the turn going on without it, as a plain chat turn when every such label is an offline or ungranted device's; done: the end, naming the reply it saved and its token counts, and `pending_approvals` when it stopped on calls that wait for a decision. A turn that is refused before it says anything streams error and done {aborted: true}. A client that closes the stream stops the turn; the partial reply is saved.

schema.description: `POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/send`'s body.

attachments.description:
Draft attachment ids this message binds, in the order the files are
read in; a repeated id counts once.

content.description:
The message's text; may be empty when `attachments` is not (a message
can be just a file).

kb_refs.description:
Knowledge bases picked for this message alone, on top of the thread's
own.

origin.description:
Where the user writes from, in one sentence the client words (a
browser sidebar: "Typed in Kai's sidebar in Firefox, beside the tab
“Example” (https://example.org/)."). Stored on the user message and
put before its text in the model's input on every turn, marked as
what the client says rather than the user's words; the thread reads
it back as the message's `origin`. Absent, or blank: the message
says nothing of where it was written.

speak.description:
Read the reply aloud as it streams: the stream then carries the
speech frames too.

voice.description: How a dictated message was dictated, stored on the user message.

The alias that answered in its place (a fallback, a candidate

deleted or expired, or whose gateway stops, ends with a last `error`

An MCP label the thread or its folder attached that offers the turn no
tools gets one frame each, with `server_label` and a `LabelCode`
(`tool_unreachable`, `tool_offline`, `tool_disabled`, `tool_unknown`,
`tool_failed`), and the turn goes on without it.

state.description:

post.description: A patch: a field left out stays as it is, and for the settings that can be unset, null clears it back to the route's default. Settings that contradict each other (the reasoning and sampling overrides, the knowledge settings, a voice alias that cannot do what it is for) are a 400 bad_request and nothing is written; an unknown profile_id is a 400 unknown_profile. The answer re-judges `continue` under the new settings, and carries the voice as stored and what it resolves to now. A device key's mcp_tools and knowledge bases pass its tool scope first (403 tool_label_out_of_scope), its model and voice aliases its alias scope (403 key_scope); a device below full admin level changes no setting of a thread with lmgw's admin tools (403 chat_toolset_needs_full). A thread that is gone is a 404 not_found.

`null` clears it back to the route's default. The thread's title is not

get.description: The thread's MCP tasks still running or waiting to enter it, oldest first, as GET /chat/api/threads/{id} lists them as `tasks` (ThreadTask), without the history: the Chat page's strip re-reads them at mcp.task_poll_interval_s. A thread the caller does not reach is 404 not_found, as everywhere in Chat; a temporary thread has none (an empty list).

post.description: Cancels task {task} (ThreadTask.id, the feed's task.started id) of the thread: lmgw sends tasks/cancel. The answer is the task as the cancel left it, whether its result is in the thread now, and what happened: the server cancelled it (its result says `cancelled by <who>`), it finished before the cancel (its real result), or the server was not connected (it ends cancelled at once and the server is told when it connects), or the server was asked and has not ended it yet (it is followed until it says it ended). The body is ignored. A thread the caller does not reach is 404 not_found; a task of another thread, or one whose result entered the thread already (it is gone then), 404 task_not_found; one that ended and whose result waits to enter the thread 409 task_ended; a server that does not declare tasks.cancel 409 task_cancel_unsupported, one that answers the cancel with an error 502 task_cancel_refused — the task goes on in both. Deleting the thread cancels its running tasks too.

schema.description: `POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/tasks/{task}/cancel`'s answer.

delivered.description:
Its result is in the thread now (a message of role `tool`); `false`
while it waits for a turn that runs, or while the server has not
ended the task yet.

task.description: The task as the cancel left it.

post.description: The body is a recording, its container named by Content-Type: audio/wav (also audio/wave, audio/x-wav, audio/vnd.wave, none, application/octet-stream), audio/webm, audio/ogg (audio/opus), audio/mpeg (audio/mp3), audio/mp4 (audio/m4a, audio/x-m4a) or audio/flac (audio/x-flac); another is 415 unsupported_media_type. It is transcribed by the thread's speech-to-text model and written nowhere: dictation, and a spoken answer to an approval, which must stay out of the conversation (a new message declines a waiting call). The answer names the alias, the one that answered in its place (a GPU-hold or outside-VRAM fallback, also in x-lmgw-fallback), the call's time, the recording's length (WAV only) and the language heard. The body is bounded by max_body_mb (413 body_limit naming it). 400 empty_audio, 422 asr_not_configured, 503 gpu_hold, and a device key's own refusals. A failure of the transcription itself names the fallback that had the audio in x-lmgw-fallback: the audio may have left this machine although nothing came back.

conversation (client-apps design §6.4).

fallback); `null` when it answered itself.

x-lmgw-candidate.description: On a candidate alias, the id of the local model that answered (or refused) the request. Never sent next to x-lmgw-fallback. The body's model field still names the requested alias.

x-lmgw-fallback.description: The model or alias that answered instead of the one requested: the last hop of its chain of fallbacks (each model and alias has its own, and a fallback can have one in turn); the answer still names the requested model. On the chat routes, a fallback whose capabilities say it cannot see receives the request's images as text placeholders, and x-lmgw-images-omitted gives the count.

x-lmgw-fallback-chain.description: Every hop a fallback-served answer was handed to, in order, each with the reason it was handed on, as an RFC 8941 list: "m2";reason=hold, "cloud";reason=hold. Sent on every answer a fallback served, next to x-lmgw-fallback (the last name) and x-lmgw-fallback-reason (the last reason), so a client reads one header whatever the chain's length. A name that cannot be an sf-string (a byte outside 0x20–0x7E) is left empty, the reason kept. A streamed /v1/responses run names the hops of its first turn only: its headers left with the first event.

post.description: A press of the microphone (or the start of a call) warms the models the voice turn will use before the request it announces. `stages` names them (asr, tts, chat: the thread's own model), each once; they are the thread's resolved aliases, warmed as one group through the request admission, so the warm may evict idle models exactly as the request would, and a group that does not fit together is warmed without evicting. The stream sends one `state` frame per change of each stage (loading, then ready with the time it took, or held, fallback, skipped, failed), then `done` with no fields once every stage has settled. A device or owner key that is disabled, rotated, deleted or expired while it streams, and a gateway that stops, end the stream with an `error` frame (code revoked, with `kind`, or gateway_stopping) instead of `done`. Closing the stream drops what still waits for admission; a container start already in flight finishes. Refused before anything is warmed: 404 not_found, 400 bad_request (no stages, or an unknown name), 422 asr_not_configured or tts_not_configured (no alias for the stage at any level), and, for a device key, its own refusal (scope, budget) for a stage whose alias it may not use — nothing starts then.

get.description: For a thread's tool picker: lmgw's built-in toolsets first (lmgw, docs, kb, image, audio, in that order), each with its tools, then the registered MCP servers and service agents by label, each with its connection's status and how many of its tools, as last listed, the caller may tick. Connects nothing; GET /chat/api/tools/{label} lists a server's tools. Under the caller's tool scope: the owner is listed every built-in toolset, one that offers nothing now with the reason (status unavailable), and every enabled server; a device key is listed what GET /v1/mcp/servers lists it — the toolsets that offer it tools and the enabled servers its scope reaches — and the self-admin toolset (lmgw) only while its admin tools are at full, since below that a device uses the threads that carry it and attaches it to none. post.description: A device sends the pairing link's one-time token with its public key (an EC P-256 key as its DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, standard base64) and the client it is, over TLS 1.3 pinned to the link's fp and without a client certificate (one presented anyway, and any credential header, is ignored: the token decides). It gets its certificate (clientAuth, for that key, valid devices.client_cert_days), lmgw's device CA, the dates, its URLs and the confirmation code of its key, 201 Created. Every request of the device is then refused 403 device_unconfirmed until the owner confirms that code on the Devices card. The same key presenting the same token again while it lives (devices.token_minutes from its minting, unless the owner ended it) gets the same answer; another key gets 410 pairing_token_used and the device is marked contested. Refusals: 400 bad_request (not this shape), 400 public_key_unsupported (not a canonical EC P-256 SubjectPublicKeyInfo), 401 pairing_token_unknown, 401 device_disabled (the token stays unused), 409 public_key_in_use (another device enrolled the key), 410 pairing_token_used, 410 pairing_token_expired (lapsed or ended; the message says which and names devices.token_minutes), 413 body_too_large (over 16 KiB), 429 pairing_rate_limited with Retry-After (failed enrolments from the address, an IPv6 address by its /64, past devices.enrol_refuse_per_min in a minute), 503 devices_ca_unavailable. Served on the device listener only: the plain listener answers it 404. While no token lives, the device listener's handshake requires a client certificate, so a device without one meets the TLS alert certificate_required instead (lmgw-client: this pairing link has ended).

schema.description: `POST /devices/enrol`'s body.

app_id.description:
The app this install is, as a lowercase reverse-DNS name
(`dev.example.storyplayer`, `transfer::APP_ID_RULE`):
what other devices of the same app offer files to (device transfers
design §2). Optional; a device without one receives no transfer. A
malformed one is refused 400 `bad_request` before the token is used.

client.description:
Free text naming the client, shown on the Devices card
("Kai mobile 0.1.0 (Android 16)"). Optional, and never trusted for
anything.

device_name.description:
The device's own name, as its user chose it on the device ("Anna's
phone"): free text, shown on the Devices card beside the name the
owner gave the link (*added 2026-10-23*). Named `device_name` here,
as the card's field is, because the answer's `device.name` is the
owner's name for the link. Optional, and never trusted for anything.

public_key.description:
The device's public key: standard base64 (RFC 4648 §4, padded) of its
DER SubjectPublicKeyInfo, an EC P-256 key.

token.description:
The link's `token`: `lmgw-enrol-` and 32 lowercase hex digits. Secret
until used.

schema.title: EnrolRequest

schema.description:
`POST /devices/enrol`'s `201 Created`: the device's certificate for the
key it sent, and what it keeps beside it. The same key presenting the
same used token again within its life gets this answer again (§3.3).

ca_certificate.description:
lmgw's device CA certificate: standard base64 of its DER. Its
SubjectPublicKeyInfo hashes to the link's `fp`; a client keeps it only
then.

certificate.description:
The device's certificate: standard base64 of its DER. `clientAuth`
only, issued by the device CA for the key the body sent.

confirm_code.description:
The confirmation code (`confirm_code`): the device shows it, and
the owner confirms the same code on the Devices card (§3.5).

confirmed.description:
Whether the owner confirmed this enrolment already (an answer asked
again after the Confirm). Until then every request of the device is
refused 403 `code::DEVICE_UNCONFIRMED`.

device.description: The device row the token belongs to.

notice_after.description:
From when the client says "this device's certificate lapses on

validity (RFC 3339, UTC; §2.3).

post.description: MCP Streamable HTTP: single JSON-RPC request/notification/response per POST, no batching. initialize negotiates MCP-Protocol-Version and assigns Mcp-Session-Id, which every later request on the session must carry; a notification answers 202 with no body. tools/list and tools/call reach the registered southbound MCP servers' tools, namespaced <prefix>__. resources/list, resources/templates/list (one page; a cursor is -32602) and resources/read pass their resources through, a prefixed server's URIs namespaced before the authority (ui://weather/card from prefix p is ui://p__weather/card) — in tools' _meta.ui.resourceUri and in tool results' resource links too; a read of a URI no server has, or of a server the caller's tool scope does not reach, is -32002. initialize advertises resources {listChanged} and the MCP Apps extension io.modelcontextprotocol/ui (mimeTypes [text/html;profile=mcp-app]); every tool is listed with its _meta, and app-only ones (_meta.ui.visibility without "model") only to a session whose initialize declared that extension. Every tool of a registered server also carries _meta["lmgw/server"] {label, name, tool}: the server's label (its tool prefix, else its name), its name, and the tool's name as the server lists it — so a host routes a view's call of its server's tool to the listed name, also one a name collision moved to <server name>__<tool> or the owner renamed; lmgw sets it, replacing anything the server put there.

get.description: A paired device offers its own MCP server over this WebSocket, and lmgw lists its tools under the device's hosting label (<label>__<tool>) while the link is open, as it lists a registered server's. Needs a device key with a hosting grant (403 host_not_granted otherwise) and no Origin header (403 cross_origin_refused: a browser page never hosts tools). Every tools/call lmgw forwards carries _meta with lmgw/caller ({kind: owner | gateway | device | key | agent, name}: who the call runs as), lmgw/approval (null, or {decision: approved, by}) and lmgw/timeout_ms (the row's timeout_ms, when lmgw stops waiting). lmgw sends notifications/cancelled {requestId, reason} for every call it stops waiting on: at the timeout, when its caller stops waiting, and before it closes the link. Tasks (MCP 2025-11-25): a tool whose execution.taskSupport is required, on a device that declares capabilities.tasks.requests.tools.call, is called with task: {} and _meta lmgw/task ({delivery: thread | wait, thread_id}); lmgw/timeout_ms then bounds the wait for the CreateTaskResult only. lmgw follows the task with tasks/get at its pollInterval (else mcp.task_poll_interval_s), acts on notifications/tasks/status, fetches tasks/result, and sends tasks/cancel (never notifications/cancelled) for a task; a link drop ends no task, and -32602 for its id ends it abandoned. A device's notifications/tools/list_changed makes lmgw list again. Sampling requests are refused -32601. Pings every mcp.host_ping_interval_s seconds; a missed pong closes 1011 naming the setting. A frame or message over mcp.host_max_frame_mb / mcp.host_max_message_mb closes 1009 naming the setting; a binary frame, a batch or text that is no JSON-RPC message closes 1002. A second link of the same device takes over: the older one closes 4000 ("another connection of device '<name>' took over"). The key's revocation closes 4003 with the realtime session's token and sentence (device_disabled, key_expired, key_unknown); the hosting grant cleared or the row switched off closes 1000; a stopping gateway closes 1001. Who may call the hosted tools: the owner, the gateway's own runs, the device itself, keys and devices whose policy's device_tools grants the label (their tool scope then filtering its tools as any server's), and agents whose manifest names it — never an anonymous caller, and never a key through its tool scope alone.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the connection is now a WebSocket. Each frame is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message as text, no batches. The roles are reversed at the message level: lmgw is the MCP client and the device the server. lmgw sends initialize, the device answers, lmgw sends notifications/initialized and pages through tools/list.

426.description: Upgrade Required: the request carried no WebSocket upgrade headers.

post.description: llama.cpp's own /tokenize, for llama.cpp clients: the client object is forwarded to the backend's own /tokenize with model rewritten, and the answer — token ids, or {id,piece} with with_pieces — comes back verbatim, the backend's own errors included (but an upstream 401/403 is a 502: that is lmgw's credential). The body is read as JSON whatever its Content-Type, as llama-server reads it. 501 not_supported_error on any backend that is not a real llama-server: an id from a tokenizer the backend does not run would be a hidden approximation. Enforces the key's alias scope (a logged 403 key_scope); no budget applies. Errors are llama.cpp-shaped, except the shared /v1 layers' own: the gate's 401, 403 and 429, and the 413 for a declared Content-Length over max_body_mb, which are OpenAI-shaped.

parameters.description: on|off: run this one request as background work, for speculative or prefetching clients. On a local model it uses the model only when that disturbs nobody: it joins the model if it is loaded and no foreground request is waiting for room, or starts it into free GPU memory (evicting only idle background-started models), and never evicts, waits for or climbs a model foreground work uses. Otherwise the model's configured fallback answers (x-lmgw-fallback, x-lmgw-fallback-reason: background), or the request is refused with 503 gpu_deferred: retry later. Foreground work never interrupts a background request that has started; close the request to cancel it. On a candidate alias it makes the alias walk as a background alias. A cloud model and a model running on the CPU are unaffected. Absent or off: an ordinary request. Any other value is a 400.

get.description: The receiver's, while the transfer is ready: the file, streamed from lmgw's disk, with Accept-Ranges: bytes, ETag "sha256:<hex>" and Content-Disposition naming its filename. One Range (bytes=a-b, bytes=a- or bytes=-n) answers 206 with Content-Range; If-Range with the ETag serves the range, with anything else the whole file. A Range lmgw does not read (another unit, several ranges, an invalid one) is ignored: the whole file, 200. 416 range_not_satisfiable, with Content-Range: bytes */size, for a range that names no byte of the file (it starts at or past the end, or asks the last 0 bytes). 404 transfer_not_found but for the receiver; 409 transfer_state with state when it is not ready. A transfer that ends while its bytes stream (a cancel, an expiry, a device's end) breaks the body off short of its length. HEAD answers the same head without the body. After its own hash check the receiver sends …/received.

put.description: The sender's, while the transfer is uploading. Content-Range: bytes a-b/size is required, size the offer's and a the transfer's received; the body is the range's raw bytes (any Content-Type), streamed to lmgw's disk. Chunks are any size; a body that breaks off keeps every byte that arrived, so received (read the transfer) is where to go on. A newer upload of the same transfer stops one still being read. Answers {received, state}; the last byte has the file's sha256 checked: state ready (offered to the receiver), or 422 transfer_hash_mismatch, the transfer failed and its bytes deleted. When lmgw already holds every byte (the last range's answer was lost), any upload of it completes it the same, whatever range it names; Content-Range: bytes */size with no body is the form that asks only that: where the upload stands, and its completion when it is whole. 400 bad_request for a missing or malformed Content-Range, another total, a Content-Length that is not b-a+1, or a body shorter or longer than its range when that was not the last byte (what arrived of the range is kept); 404 transfer_not_found but for the sender; 409 transfer_offset with received when a is not it (or a newer upload stopped this one); 409 transfer_state with state once it is not uploading, also for an upload a cancel, an expiry or a device's end stopped (ready: it is done); 507 transfer_storage_full with free_bytes when the disk filled.

post.description: Forced alignment against a task: "align" row — lmgw's own route, multipart/form-data only. Every family answers the same shape: the words with their seconds, samples where known, and their character span in the submitted text; a model whose answer has no word timings lmgw can read is a 502 naming its family.

parameters.description: on|off: run this one request as background work, for speculative or prefetching clients. On a local model it uses the model only when that disturbs nobody: it joins the model if it is loaded and no foreground request is waiting for room, or starts it into free GPU memory (evicting only idle background-started models), and never evicts, waits for or climbs a model foreground work uses. Otherwise the model's configured fallback answers (x-lmgw-fallback, x-lmgw-fallback-reason: background), or the request is refused with 503 gpu_deferred: retry later. Foreground work never interrupts a background request that has started; close the request to cancel it. On a candidate alias it makes the alias walk as a background alias. A cloud model and a model running on the CPU are unaffected. Absent or off: an ordinary request. Any other value is a 400.
parameters.name: x-lmgw-background

parameters.description: The job id of the live agent run to attribute this request's cost, tokens and call count to. Only an agent token may attribute, and only to its own runs. An id that names no live run, a run that belongs to another agent, or a caller without an agent token is ignored with a log line and never refused.
parameters.name: x-lmgw-run

schema.description:
A forced alignment: the submitted transcript and where each of its words
is spoken in the clip.

language.description:
The language as the model reported it (`en`, `de`; the model's own
spelling). Absent when the model says none.

A model may report the language it assumes rather than the one it was
asked to align in: CrisperWhisper's aligner answers its default, `en`,
to any `language` (checked 2026-10-22 with `de`, `german` and none).

sample_rate.description:
The rate, in Hz, the `start_sample` and `end_sample` of the words
count in: the model's own figure when its answer states one, else
derived from the words' seconds and samples (they are what the
samples count in, even where the engine resampled the clip), else the
uploaded WAV's header. Absent when none of the three works; the
seconds are always there.

text.description:
The transcript as the client submitted it (the multipart `text`
field), not what the model echoes. `char_start` and `char_end` of the
words index into this string.

timing.description:
How long the engine took, as it reports it (audio.cpp's `timing`
object, which both aligners send). Absent when the answer has none.

words.description:
The words in the order the model answered them, which is the
transcript's order.

schema.title: AudioAlignment

x-lmgw-candidate.description: On a candidate alias, the id of the local model that answered (or refused) the request. Never sent next to x-lmgw-fallback. The body's model field still names the requested alias.

x-lmgw-fallback.description: The model or alias that answered instead of the one requested: the last hop of its chain of fallbacks (each model and alias has its own, and a fallback can have one in turn); the answer still names the requested model. On the chat routes, a fallback whose capabilities say it cannot see receives the request's images as text placeholders, and x-lmgw-images-omitted gives the count.

x-lmgw-fallback-chain.description: Every hop a fallback-served answer was handed to, in order, each with the reason it was handed on, as an RFC 8941 list: "m2";reason=hold, "cloud";reason=hold. Sent on every answer a fallback served, next to x-lmgw-fallback (the last name) and x-lmgw-fallback-reason (the last reason), so a client reads one header whatever the chain's length. A name that cannot be an sf-string (a byte outside 0x20–0x7E) is left empty, the reason kept. A streamed /v1/responses run names the hops of its first turn only: its headers left with the first event.

x-lmgw-fallback-reason.description: Why x-lmgw-fallback answered (the last hop's reason; x-lmgw-fallback-chain has every hop's); always sent next to it. hold: the GPU hold pauses local models. benchmark: a benchmark run has the GPU to itself until it ends. external_vram: GPU memory used outside lmgw by another program left too little room to load the model, so the fallback answered at once instead of waiting. background: a background job's model could not load without disturbing foreground work (any request that is not background traffic: a background candidate alias's, or one sent with x-lmgw-background: on). unavailable: a candidate alias's primary cannot be used at all (missing, disabled, or lacking a capability the alias enables) and none of its other models is loaded. quota: the upstream answered that its account's quota is exhausted (insufficient_quota), or lmgw remembers it so until its next check; nothing was charged for the refused attempt. unreachable: the upstream could not be connected to, so nothing reached it. disabled: the model or alias asked for is disabled, or its upstream is. gpu_setup: the local model could not start on the graphics card, and lmgw's machine check names why (the card, its driver, or the piece that lets models use it, not ready on the computer lmgw runs on); while that check still describes the machine, the fallback answers without a start being tried. engine_download: the engine the local model runs in is not on the computer yet, and downloading it failed or cannot be done.

x-lmgw-speech.description: On POST /v1/audio/speech (and on /v1/tasks/run and /v1/tasks/stream, for their chars part), what lmgw changed in the request so the model understands it; a '; '-separated list. voice=options.voice_id: a voice the model ships, which this family (MagpieTTS) reads from options.voice_id. voice=preset->options.voice_id: the same for a preset's voice id. voice=<name>: a shipped voice sent in the model's own spelling. language=<asked>-><sent>: the language in the model's own vocabulary, e.g. de->german for Qwen3-TTS, en->en-us for Kokoro. instructions=options.instruct: instructions moved to where the family reads them. instructions=also:options.instruct or instructions=also:options.instruction: the model's default request options describe the voice under that other key, which the engine would merge in beside the request's and refuse as conflicting, so the request's text went there too and replaces the default. instructions=dropped: the model reads none (capabilities.speech.instructions is none). tags=mapped:<n>,stripped:<n>: inline tags in input were rewritten into the model's spelling, or removed so they are never read out. chars=replaced:<U+XXXX/...>,dropped:<U+XXXX/...>: characters of input the model's engine has no entry for in its package's vocabulary (Supertonic refuses the whole request over one), replaced by an equivalent it has (a typographic quote by a plain one, a dash by -) or removed (an emoji). Each list names at most 64 codepoints and then ends in +<n> more; lmgw's log has the full list. An input left with nothing to say is 400 empty_input, which carries the header too. The voice, language and chars parts apply to local audio models only. Absent when the request went as it came; input changes only for its inline tags and those characters.

x-lmgw-speech.description: On POST /v1/audio/speech (and on /v1/tasks/run and /v1/tasks/stream, for their chars part), what lmgw changed in the request so the model understands it; a '; '-separated list. voice=options.voice_id: a voice the model ships, which this family (MagpieTTS) reads from options.voice_id. voice=preset->options.voice_id: the same for a preset's voice id. voice=<name>: a shipped voice sent in the model's own spelling. language=<asked>-><sent>: the language in the model's own vocabulary, e.g. de->german for Qwen3-TTS, en->en-us for Kokoro. instructions=options.instruct: instructions moved to where the family reads them. instructions=also:options.instruct or instructions=also:options.instruction: the model's default request options describe the voice under that other key, which the engine would merge in beside the request's and refuse as conflicting, so the request's text went there too and replaces the default. instructions=dropped: the model reads none (capabilities.speech.instructions is none). tags=mapped:<n>,stripped:<n>: inline tags in input were rewritten into the model's spelling, or removed so they are never read out. chars=replaced:<U+XXXX/...>,dropped:<U+XXXX/...>: characters of input the model's engine has no entry for in its package's vocabulary (Supertonic refuses the whole request over one), replaced by an equivalent it has (a typographic quote by a plain one, a dash by -) or removed (an emoji). Each list names at most 64 codepoints and then ends in +<n> more; lmgw's log has the full list. An input left with nothing to say is 400 empty_input, which carries the header too. The voice, language and chars parts apply to local audio models only. Absent when the request went as it came; input changes only for its inline tags and those characters.

parameters.description: on|off: run this one request as background work, for speculative or prefetching clients. post.description: The chat-completions API, plus lmgw's own reasoning controls and chat_template_kwargs passthrough. `model` may be an alias, a local model id, a candidate alias, or an exposed upstream's `prefix/…` id. An anthropic-beta header is forwarded when the route is an Anthropic upstream.

parameters.description: on|off: per-request thinking switch; it wins over body fields. On a cloud model, off goes out in the form the model takes: no reasoning control where the model has none, its lowest level where it cannot stop (x-lmgw-reasoning-ignored then lists enabled), thinking type between_tools on an Anthropic model whose catalog says it takes that type and not disabled. An off never ends in an error: a refused one is retried with what the refusal names and, failing that, with no reasoning control, so a model that cannot run without reasoning answers with its default reasoning. Accepted on /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/messages/count_tokens, /v1/responses and /v1/responses/input_tokens.
parameters.name: x-lmgw-reasoning

parameters.description: An effort level (see capabilities.reasoning.levels of the model); 'none' turns reasoning off. Accepted on /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/messages/count_tokens, /v1/responses and /v1/responses/input_tokens.
parameters.name: x-lmgw-reasoning-effort

parameters.description: Integer thinking-token budget; 0 turns reasoning off. Expressible on llama.cpp, Gemini and budget-style Anthropic models only. Accepted on /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/messages/count_tokens, /v1/responses and /v1/responses/input_tokens.

x-lmgw-max-tokens-defaulted.description: The max_tokens value lmgw chose because the request set none and the route (an Anthropic upstream) requires one: the catalog's published maximum when streaming, 4096 when not streaming (the provider refuses non-streamed requests that could run too long).

x-lmgw-max-tokens-raised.description: The max_tokens value lmgw raised the request's cap to, because the requested thinking budget would not fit underneath it.

x-lmgw-params-ignored.description: Comma-separated list of the request's sampling parameters (top_k, min_p, repeat_penalty, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, seed) the answering model's provider does not take, so lmgw did not send them: the OpenAI platform takes no top_k, min_p or repeat_penalty; Anthropic none of the six but top_k; Gemini no min_p, repeat_penalty or penalties. llama.cpp and OpenAI-compatible providers are sent all of them. Also context_management and compaction, a /v1/messages request's Anthropic context management and on-demand compaction, which only an Anthropic model's route takes (both sent on as written), and thinking.display, which goes only to an Anthropic model, beside a thinking type that takes it (adaptive or enabled). Request fields lmgw does not model are sent as they came and never listed. Absent when every parameter was sent.

x-lmgw-params-refused.description: Comma-separated list of the request's sampling parameters the answering model refused, which lmgw left out of the send (stop is not left out; its refusal reaches the client). x-lmgw-reasoning-ignored.description: Comma-separated list of the reasoning controls (enabled, effort, budget) the route could not express. enabled is also listed when an off went out as no control or as the model's lowest level, either because the model cannot take the off itself or because the provider refused every form of off and the model answered with its default reasoning. An off sent to an Anthropic model as thinking type between_tools (its own lowest setting, when it takes no disabled) is not listed. between_tools: a /v1/messages request's thinking type between_tools went to a model of another provider as that provider's off. Absent when every control was applied.

x-lmgw-rung.description: On a ladder model, the rung that answered (or refused) the request, as '<k>/<n>; ctx=<per-slot context>; gguf=<weights file>', counted from 1 (the gguf part is left off when the file name cannot be a header value). Absent on models without a ladder and on responses a fallback answered.

post.description: The legacy text-completions shape. Refuses a non-OpenAI-protocol upstream with 400 rather than sending it a request its own API cannot answer. A missing model is a 400 (missing 'model'), as on every other ingress.

parameters.description: on|off: run this one request as background work, for speculative or prefetching clients. On a local model it uses the model only when that disturbs nobody: it joins the model if it is loaded and no foreground request is waiting for room, or starts it into free GPU memory (evicting only idle background-started models), and never evicts, waits for or climbs a model foreground work uses. Otherwise the model's configured fallback answers (x-lmgw-fallback, x-lmgw-fallback-reason: background), or the request is refused with 503 gpu_deferred: retry later. Foreground work never interrupts a background request that has started; close the request to cancel it. On a candidate alias it makes the alias walk as a background alias. parameters.description: The job id of the live agent run to attribute this request's cost, tokens and call count to. Only an agent token may attribute, and only to its own runs. An id that names no live run, a run that belongs to another agent, or a caller without an agent token is ignored with a log line and never refused.

x-lmgw-candidate.description: On a candidate alias, the id of the local model that answered (or refused) the request. Never sent next to x-lmgw-fallback. The body's model field still names the requested alias.

x-lmgw-fallback.description: The model or alias that answered instead of the one requested: the last hop of its chain of fallbacks (each model and alias has its own, and a fallback can have one in turn); the answer still names the requested model. On the chat routes, a fallback whose capabilities say it cannot see receives the request's images as text placeholders, and x-lmgw-images-omitted gives the count.

x-lmgw-fallback-chain.description: Every hop a fallback-served answer was handed to, in order, each with the reason it was handed on, as an RFC 8941 list: "m2";reason=hold, "cloud";reason=hold. A name that cannot be an sf-string (a byte outside 0x20–0x7E) is left empty, the reason kept. A streamed /v1/responses run names the hops of its first turn only: its headers left with the first event.

post.description: The Anthropic Messages API. A server tool (no input_schema) is refused with 400. A content block lmgw does not model (redacted_thinking, the provider's own tool blocks, a type newer than lmgw) goes between client and an Anthropic upstream as written, whole and streamed, where it stood; any other upstream is sent none of it (x-lmgw-params-ignored: content.<type>), and a Chat Completions or Responses client is given none (a whole answer's x-lmgw-params-ignored: answer.<type>). Thinking blocks keep their signature. A block without a type is refused with 400. A missing max_tokens is filled in rather than refused (x-lmgw-max-tokens-defaulted). anthropic-beta reaches an Anthropic upstream as one header, merged with the upstream row's own; other protocols have no equivalent and are sent none. context_management and the top-level compaction go to an Anthropic upstream as written and its answer's context_management comes back; any other upstream is sent neither, and x-lmgw-params-ignored names them. A compaction block (in the answer, streamed, or sent back in messages) goes between client and an Anthropic upstream as Anthropic wrote it, with stop_reason compaction and usage.iterations; any other upstream is sent the summary as text where the block stood and nothing before it, as Anthropic itself drops that history. thinking: {type: between_tools} and thinking.display go to an Anthropic upstream as written; elsewhere the off is that provider's own (x-lmgw-reasoning-ignored: between_tools) and display is named in x-lmgw-params-ignored. An unknown thinking type is refused with 400.

parameters.description: on|off: per-request thinking switch; it wins over body fields. An off never ends in an error: a refused one is retried with what the refusal names and, failing that, with no reasoning control, so a model that cannot run without reasoning answers with its default reasoning. x-lmgw-params-ignored.description: Comma-separated list of the request's sampling parameters (top_k, min_p, repeat_penalty, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, seed) the answering model's provider does not take, so lmgw did not send them: the OpenAI platform takes no top_k, min_p or repeat_penalty; Anthropic none of the six but top_k; Gemini no min_p, repeat_penalty or penalties. llama.cpp and OpenAI-compatible providers are sent all of them. Also context_management and compaction, a /v1/messages request's Anthropic context management and on-demand compaction, which only an Anthropic model's route takes (both sent on as written), and thinking.display, which goes only to an Anthropic model, beside a thinking type that takes it (adaptive or enabled). Also content.<type>, a /v1/messages request's content block lmgw does not model (redacted_thinking, a type newer than lmgw), which only an Anthropic model's route is sent, and answer.<type>, such a block in an Anthropic model's whole answer, which a Chat Completions or Responses client is not given (a streamed answer's headers leave before it). On an Anthropic model's route, content.thinking and content.<type> name a thinking or other Anthropic block lmgw recorded from an answer at another provider's address (a stored /v1/responses chain), which this provider cannot read and is not sent. answer.citations and content.citations name an Anthropic text block's citations, which only a /v1/messages client and an Anthropic model's route are given (citations lmgw recorded from an answer only at that provider's address, and a citation with no text not at all). Request fields lmgw does not model are sent as they came and never listed. Absent when every parameter was sent.

Nothing is left out without a refusal on record. On a streamed /v1/responses run the header names what was on record when the stream opened. Absent when every parameter was sent.

An off sent to an Anthropic model as thinking type between_tools (its own lowest setting, when it takes no disabled) is not listed. between_tools: a /v1/messages request's thinking type between_tools went to a model of another provider as that provider's off. Absent when every control was applied.

Absent on models without a ladder and on responses a fallback answered.
