A name that cannot be an sf-string (a byte outside 0x20–0x7E) is left empty, the reason kept. A streamed /v1/responses run names the hops of its first turn only: its headers left with the first event.

x-lmgw-fallback-reason.description: Why x-lmgw-fallback answered (the last hop's reason; x-lmgw-fallback-chain has every hop's); always sent next to it. hold: the GPU hold pauses local models. benchmark: a benchmark run has the GPU to itself until it ends. external_vram: GPU memory used outside lmgw by another program left too little room to load the model, so the fallback answered at once instead of waiting. background: a background job's model could not load without disturbing foreground work (any request that is not background traffic: a background candidate alias's, or one sent with x-lmgw-background: on). unavailable: a candidate alias's primary cannot be used at all (missing, disabled, or lacking a capability the alias enables) and none of its other models is loaded. quota: the upstream answered that its account's quota is exhausted (insufficient_quota), or lmgw remembers it so until its next check; nothing was charged for the refused attempt. unreachable: the upstream could not be connected to, so nothing reached it. disabled: the model or alias asked for is disabled, or its upstream is. gpu_setup: the local model could not start on the graphics card, and lmgw's machine check names why (the card, its driver, or the piece that lets models use it, not ready on the computer lmgw runs on); while that check still describes the machine, the fallback answers without a start being tried. engine_download: the engine the local model runs in is not on the computer yet, and downloading it failed or cannot be done.

get.description: OpenAI's GA Realtime protocol over a WebSocket (ws://<host>/v1/realtime), answered by a cascade of this gateway's own aliases: voice activity and end-of-turn detection inside lmgw (Silero VAD; Smart Turn for semantic_vad), speech to text with realtime.asr_alias, the chat model, and text to speech with realtime.tts_alias — local models first, any of them a cloud alias if so configured (Settings → Realtime, which also shows what the cascade holds on the GPU). `model` is resolved in this order: a realtime.model_map name, an OpenAI Realtime name (gpt-realtime*, never taken as an alias), which realtime.default_model answers, or a chat alias; it may be left out and named in the first session.update instead. What a name resolved to is echoed in session.lmgw.resolved. Implemented: conversation sessions (session.type realtime) with audio or text output, PCM16 at 24 kHz in and out, server_vad, semantic_vad and manual turns, barge-in with a word check, session.update, input_audio_buffer.append/commit/clear, conversation.item.create/retrieve/truncate/delete, response.create and response.cancel, client-side function tools, and MCP tools the gateway runs itself on a session not bound to a Chat thread. An MCP session tool {"type": "mcp", "server_label"} names one of this gateway's own MCP servers (by its tool prefix or name) or a built-in toolset (docs, kb, and lmgw for an owner credential or a device allowed lmgw's admin tools, while the self-admin tools are on), resolved as on /v1/responses under the key's tool scope; GET /v1/mcp/servers lists the labels a caller may use and GET /v1/mcp/servers/{label} one label's tools. server_url, connector_id, headers, authorization and server_description are accepted and never used: lmgw dials no URL a client names, and echoes authorization and header values as [redacted]. allowed_tools takes a name list or {tool_names}; read_only and a require_approval that would gate a tool are refused (approvals are not built here yet: leave it out or send "never"); one entry per server_label. The session lists a label's tools as an mcp_list_tools item (mcp_list_tools.in_progress, then .completed or .failed — a failed label also gets an error with code mcp_list_tools_failed saying why, and a later session.update naming it lists it again), and a response waits for the listings in flight. A model's call to one of those tools is an mcp_call item (server_label, name — the server's own tool name — arguments, output, error, always present), streamed as response.mcp_call_arguments.delta and .done, then run by the gateway before response.done (response.mcp_call.in_progress, then .completed with the output or .failed with a tool_execution_error). The call ends the response: the client sends response.create for the answer, as OpenAI's Realtime API has it (@openai/agents does so by itself, once per response). A cancel or barge-in abandons a running call, which then fails saying it may or may not have run. A response's tools may narrow to a label the session has listed, and tool_choice takes {"type": "mcp", "server_label"} with an optional name. A client may replay mcp_call items as history; mcp_list_tools and the approval items are refused. Each call writes a realtime-tool usage row. Refused with an error naming what is missing: transcription sessions, G.711 formats, output_audio_buffer.clear (a WebRTC call's) and an input_audio item without its transcript. Accepted and echoed but not applied: noise_reduction, and truncation (lmgw.resolved.truncation says "disabled"; an overflow is an error). WebRTC is served at POST /v1/realtime/calls. Not served at all: the sideband connection to a call (call_id, refused with 400 sideband_unsupported rather than opening an unrelated session), SIP, ephemeral client secrets, live partial transcripts and out-of-band responses. Credentials as on every /v1 route; a browser, which cannot set headers on a WebSocket, may offer its key as the subprotocol `openai-insecure-api-key.<key>` alongside `realtime` — accepted on this route only. A paired device's key is refused before the upgrade with 401 device_key_unknown when it matches no device (pair it again), 401 device_disabled while the device is disabled, and 401 key_expired past its expiry date, as on every Chat route. A beta client (OpenAI-Beta: realtime=v1) is refused with 400 beta_protocol_unsupported, and with Require API key off an anonymous upgrade from another page's Origin is refused with 403. Chat models list this route in their capabilities.endpoints on GET /v1/models once an ASR and a TTS alias are configured, and /v1/realtime/calls beside it while the WebRTC UDP socket of the listener asked is bound. The TTS gets lmgw's speech instructions — session.lmgw.speech_instructions, a response.create's response.lmgw.speech_instructions, else realtime.speech_instructions — as a style, or as the description a voice-design (vdes) model designs its voice from; session.lmgw.resolved.speech says what is in effect, and the transcript leaves out the inline tags ([laughter]) the voice renders. Markdown a voice cannot read is not spoken: fenced code blocks and tables (lines that start with |, from one that ends with | or is followed by a delimiter row) are skipped — the transcript leaves them out, and the model's history keeps them. On a style or passthrough TTS that renders no tags (Qwen3 CustomVoice, Auk, MOSS-TTS; a cloud TTS only when its alias's capabilities.speech override declares instructions 'style'), the tags that open a sentence, or a part of one spoken on its own, are a delivery cue instead ([laughing]): sent after the style as the instructions until that sentence ends, best effort, never read out (resolved.speech.cues). A voice mode binds a session to a Chat thread with chat_thread=<id> (negative for a temporary chat): the chat capability only — the dashboard's cookie, an owner key or a paired device's key; refused before the upgrade, in the OpenAI error shape ({"error": {code, message, type, param}}) and checked in this order, with 403 chat_thread_not_allowed, 400 owned_by_thread beside model, 404 chat_thread_not_found (also an Admin Chat thread a device names, and a thread with the self-admin toolset a device not allowed lmgw's admin tools names: for that device they do not exist), 409 chat_thread_admin for an Admin Chat thread the owner names (no voice mode there), and, with takeover=never, 409 chat_thread_bound while another session is bound to the thread ("voice is in use on device 'phone'"; nothing is taken over), whose error.held_by names the holder as the Chat feed's voice.bound.by does ("device 'phone'", "the dashboard") so a client shows it without reading the message; no other refusal carries held_by. A session bound with the same key, or one that is already ending (after its 1001, a revocation or its close, while it writes its last turns), does not count: takeover=never takes it over, so a client's rebind after a restart or a dropped link is not refused in its own name. A device binds as its key: the thread's chat, speech-to-text and text-to-speech aliases pass its scope and budget before the upgrade (refused as an unbound session's aliases are, 403 key_scope or key_budget; the speech aliases' missing price, budget_unpriced, too), while the chat alias's price check comes at the first turn, as an error event, not before the upgrade; every model call of the session is checked and counted against it as an unbound session's, and each refusal writes its request row. session.created then names the thread in session.lmgw.resolved.chat_thread ({id, title, temporary, admin_tools}) and its turn mode in session.lmgw.turn_mode (below), and the connect warm loads the thread's chat, speech-to-text and text-to-speech models as one group, which may evict idle models as the requests it announces would, whatever realtime.warm_on_connect says (that setting is for unbound sessions). chat_folder=<id> binds an ongoing folder's current thread instead, decided by the rules of POST /chat/api/folders/{id}/current and bound in one step under the folder's lock, so no other client moves the folder in between: the current thread, or a new one from the folder's defaults when there is none, when it is out of the caller's reach, when it idled past the folder's idle minutes, or with new=true unless it has no message yet; a new thread is recorded as folder.current on the Chat feed with its reason, and the thread bound is reported in session.lmgw.resolved.chat_thread as for chat_thread. It is refused beside chat_thread (400 invalid_value) and model (400 owned_by_thread), new without chat_folder and takeover with neither parameter are 400 invalid_value, then come 404 chat_folder_not_found (a folder the caller cannot see), 409 not_ongoing and 409 folder_no_model, then the thread's own refusals, checked on the thread the decision picks before a new one is made. takeover=ask is a WebRTC call's and 400 invalid_value here. A bound session carries session.lmgw.turn_mode, automatic or push_to_talk, resolved from the thread's turn detection at the bind (push_to_talk there is push_to_talk, anything else automatic), and lmgw sets audio.input.turn_detection to match: the thread's rule (server_vad or semantic_vad, semantic_vad where it names none) in automatic mode, null in push_to_talk; session.created echoes both. A session.update naming turn_mode switches it and gets the turn detection it implies (the mode in effect named again leaves the detection as it is); one that also names audio.input.turn_detection must agree with it (null with push_to_talk, a rule with automatic), as an echo of the whole session does, else invalid_value; turn detection named alone still works and turn_mode follows it. A change of the thread's turn detection applies at the next bind. An unbound session has no turn_mode, and refuses one with invalid_value. The thread then owns the chat model, prompt, tools, speech models, voice, speech style, language, seed and conversation: a session.update that changes one of them, a response.create that overrides one, and conversation.item.create or .delete are refused with owned_by_thread (an echoed value is accepted). Each response is the thread's own chat turn — its model, prompt with the spoken-style instructions after it, sampling, attachments, knowledge bases and MCP tools, which never become function_call items — written to the thread's history: the user turn with how it was spoken, the reply cut to what was heard (the unheard rest kept beside it, a reply nobody heard deleted unless it ran tools), never over a turn another window started meanwhile. Code blocks and tables are announced rather than skipped silently ("Code block, rust.", "Table."; in the thread's language for en, de, fr, es and it), and the dashboard's read-aloud of a reply speaks the same way. No audio is stored: a spoken turn is kept as text. With chat_voice_audio_input on (Settings, or the thread's voice.audio_input), a turn whose answering model takes audio input — the thread's chat model, or the fallback a GPU hold, a benchmark run, an outside-VRAM verdict or a candidate alias hands it to, wherever it runs — goes to it as audio at the commit, while the speech-to-text model transcribes it beside (a model that does not take audio input, one whose capabilities lmgw cannot read, or one lmgw cannot send audio to, such as an Anthropic upstream, is refused it before anything is sent, and the turn goes again as its transcript); the reply is held until the transcript is in, then plays (a thread with no speech-to-text model that resolves always goes as its transcript: only the transcript tells words from noise). A turn that came back without words ends the response quietly as response.done {cancelled, reason no_words}, with no error and nothing written; a failed transcription of a turn the model heard (it answered from the audio) plays the reply and marks the user message (voice.transcript_error) instead of sending transcription.failed, while one no model heard yet, or a turn never transcribed at all (no speech-to-text model, the key's policy, the session's end), is said as with the setting off and ends the response quietly as response.done {cancelled, reason transcription_failed}. A new turn cuts a held reply whatever interrupt_response says, and a held reply's tools run only once its user message is written (a turn that came back without words runs none). A model's server that refuses the audio gets the transcript once, and the session's later turns to that model go as text when the refusal names the audio or the transcript retry answered (a server that went away under the audio is not retried, and its later turns go as text too). One session per thread: a second bind takes the thread over, and the older session gets error chat_thread_taken_over and the close 4000, both naming who bound it ("voice mode moved to device 'phone'", "… to the dashboard") — unless the second bind gives takeover=never, which a client uses for its own automatic rebinds so it never takes the voice from another device; a user's explicit choice to talk binds without it. A bound session — and no other — also sends lmgw's own events: lmgw.chat.frame ({response_id, event, data}: the chat turn's frames verbatim — turn, retrieval, delta, reasoning, tool, usage, stats, stop, state, error, done; a tool frame's ready and result carry call_id, server_label and ui_resource (the namespaced MCP Apps UI resource the tool links to, for resources/read on /mcp; null when none), ready needs_approval, and result structured_content (the MCP result's structuredContent; null when none) and content (its content blocks as the server sent them), and approval the waiting call's approval_request_id, server_label, name, arguments and call_id (the id its ready frame carried); reasoning is shown, stored with the reply and never spoken, and done's reasoning_note says in a sentence when the model reasoned although the turn asked for reasoning off — a voice turn does unless the thread sets reasoning; no off ends in an error — and its images_note when a fallback that cannot see answered and got the turn's images as placeholders), lmgw.chat.user ({message_id, content, voice (a MessageVoice), response_id}: response_id when that response heard the turn as audio, whose user message is written once the turn is transcribed, after the reply may have started — the page puts it before that reply), lmgw.chat.input ({response_id, input: audio or transcript, why}: how a response's turns reach the chat model and why the transcript, sent at each launch, when an audio attempt was refused, and when a llama-server that went away under the audio sends the session's later turns to it as text; never with chat_voice_audio_input off), lmgw.chat.reply (the ChatReply type: {message_id, content, unheard, voice (a MessageVoice)}, {message_id, removed: true} or {message_id, skipped, voice}: the reply as stored once its response ended, cut to what lmgw knew was heard; a conversation.item.truncate that arrives after that cuts it again at the position the client heard, and sends a second lmgw.chat.reply for the same message_id, which replaces the first), lmgw.model.state ({stage, alias, state, ms, …}: the connect warm's and each turn's model loading), lmgw.chat.thread ({chat_thread: {id, title, temporary, admin_tools}}: the thread as a response re-read it, when that differs from session.lmgw.resolved.chat_thread — a title the first spoken turn named, the admin tools switched on or off) and lmgw.response.timing (a VoiceTiming, flat: {response_id, message_id, end_of_turn_ms, asr_ms, first_token_ms, reasoning_ms, first_clause_ms, first_audio_ms, total_ms, to_first_audio_ms, cold, models: {asr, chat, tts}, input, input_why, transcript_wait_ms}: the timing log line as data, each stage measured from the one before, reasoning_ms the part of first_token_ms the model reasoned (absent when it did not), cold naming the stages that loaded, input whether the chat model heard the turn as audio or read its transcript, input_why why the transcript, transcript_wait_ms how long the first output was held for the transcript (the three absent with chat_voice_audio_input off, transcript_wait_ms on the transcript path), each model with the alias that answered when a fallback did, first_clause: "announcement" when the first clause said was one; sent once the reply is written, message_id null when nothing was saved, and stored with the reply), lmgw.approval.decided ({approval_request_id, approve, by}: a call whose mcp_approval_request item the session showed was decided by another client, `by` naming who as the feed names authors; approve false and by null for one whose reply was edited or deleted) and lmgw.task.done ({thread_id, message_id, id, task_id, server_label, tool, status, by}: a late MCP task result entered the thread as message message_id of role tool — the feed's task.done facts; it enters only while no turn of the thread runs, so one that ended during a response is said once that response's turn ended; one said while a response runs entered at that response's start, and that response answers it). Three more lmgw events belong to a WebRTC call bound to a Chat thread and are never sent or read on this WebSocket, whose closes say the same with their codes: lmgw.session.bind_pending ({held_by}: under takeover=ask the thread was held when the call's channel opened; no session runs until the client sends lmgw.session.take_over ({}) to take it, the holder ends and the call binds by itself, or the wait of one realtime.ping_interval_s runs out; a holder that changes brings another), and lmgw.session.closed ({kind, by, message}: the bound call's last event, kind one of taken_over, revoked, out_of_reach, shutting_down, closed and thread_bound, by the new binder, the holder or who hung up and otherwise null, message the sentence a WebSocket close's reason carries, led by the revocation token for revoked). by and held_by name a client as voice.bound.by does. lmgw starts no response for a result: the client's own response.create with no new words and no turn the client committed before it, while the thread holds results no reply answered (said in this session, or there before the bind), is a continuation that answers them, as POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/answer does (turn detection's automatic response to a turn without words stays empty_turn, and so does a push-to-talk commit of silence and its response.create; a continuation a cough cut before any of it was heard runs again after the cough) — it never cancels a turn of the thread (response.done failed with turn_running while one runs), and is empty_turn when a turn of another window answered the results meanwhile. A bound turn's call that waits for an approval (the thread's require_approval) is OpenAI's mcp_approval_request item (conversation.item.added and .done; its id is the approval id; OpenAI's shape, so no call id: the lmgw.chat.frame relaying the turn's approval frame, sent right after the item, carries call_id beside the same approval_request_id) and its response ends; the client answers with conversation.item.create of {type: mcp_approval_response, approval_request_id, approve, reason?} — the one item a bound session takes — then response.create, and that response resumes the thread's turn as POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/approvals does, the session's principal the approver: the approved calls run and the answer comes in that one response. A refusal of the answers fails the response with the route's code (approval_missing, approval_not_found, approval_decided, approval_starter_unavailable, approval_moved_on, approval_out_of_scope, key_rate). A committed turn with words is a new message, which declines what waits: a response that answers one runs as ever. Keep a spoken answer out of the session (transcribe it with POST /chat/api/threads/{id}/transcribe). A refusal mid-session is an error event; its codes: owned_by_thread (a client event changing what the thread owns), empty_turn (a response that would answer no turn and no job result), turn_running (a continuation while a turn of the thread runs), superseded and not_saved (another turn took the thread, or the reply could not be saved; its speech stops), chat_thread_not_found and chat_thread_admin, tts_not_configured, voice_not_configured, voice_not_found, instructions_required, voice_needs_transcript and speech_unavailable (the thread's speech, judged per response after response.created), chat_history_write_failed (the store refused the spoken turn; its words lead the next user message), and chat_thread_taken_over before the takeover's close. A session opened with a key ends when the key is revoked — disabled, rotated or deleted on the Keys page, or past its expires_at — with the close 4003 (any key's session, a device's or not). Its reason starts with a token saying what to do, then a colon and the sentence: device_disabled (a paired device was disabled), key_expired (a paired device's key expired), key_unknown (a paired device's key was replaced or deleted: pair it again), certificate_expired (a paired device's client certificate passed its notAfter: pair it again) or revoked (any other kind of key), e.g. "device_disabled: device 'desktop' was disabled"; reconnecting with the same key is refused. A device's session bound to a thread that leaves the device's reach — the self-admin toolset attached to it, or what the device's admin tools may do set to off — closes with 4004 and the neutral reason "chat thread <id> is out of reach for this key": the key is still good, and a client asks for its current thread again. Another client binding the thread closes the session with 4000. Every session closes with 1001 ("lmgw is stopping or restarting") when the gateway stops or restarts.

schema.description:
OpenAI's sideband connection: a server-side WebSocket attached to a
WebRTC call's session. lmgw serves none, so it is refused, 400
sideband_unsupported, rather than opening an unrelated session.

A voice mode bound to an ongoing folder's current thread: the bind
decides the thread by the rules of `POST
/chat/api/folders/{id}/current` and binds it in one step, under the
folder's lock — the current thread, or a new one from the folder's
defaults when there is none, when it is out of the caller's reach,
when it idled past the folder's idle minutes, or with `new=true`
(unless it has no message yet). A new thread is recorded as
`folder.current` on the Chat feed with its reason. The thread bound
is reported in `session.lmgw.resolved.chat_thread`, and is then as
with `chat_thread`. Refused beside `chat_thread` (400 invalid_value)
and beside `model` (400 owned_by_thread); 404 chat_folder_not_found
for a folder the caller cannot see, 409 not_ongoing for one that is
no ongoing conversation, 409 folder_no_model for one whose defaults
name no model, then the thread's own refusals.

A voice mode bound to a Chat thread: bind the session to this thread
(negative for a temporary one). The thread then owns the chat model,
prompt, tools, speech models, voice and conversation, and the session
sends lmgw's `lmgw.*` extension events. Needs the chat capability
(the dashboard's cookie, an owner key or a paired device's key),
refused beside `model`, and refused for an Admin Chat thread (a
device is told there is no such thread). A device binds as its key:
the thread's aliases pass its scope and budget first.

The chat model: a `realtime.model_map` name, an OpenAI Realtime name
answered by `realtime.default_model`, or a chat alias — in that
order. Optional — a session may name its model in its first
`session.update` instead.

With `chat_folder`: start a new conversation — a new thread unless
the folder's current one has no message yet. Refused without
`chat_folder` (400 invalid_value).

With `chat_thread` or `chat_folder`: whether this bind may take the
thread from a session already bound to it. Left out, it does — the
other session closes (a WebSocket with 4000), naming who took it.
`never`: it does not — while another session is bound to the thread
the request is refused, 409 chat_thread_bound naming who holds it
("voice is in use on device 'phone'", and as `error.held_by`), and
nothing is taken over; a WebRTC call whose thread is taken between
its POST and its channel's open ends with lmgw.session.closed
{kind: thread_bound}. For a client's own automatic rebinds (after a
conversation moved to a new thread), so it never takes the voice
from another device that followed the same move; a user's explicit
choice to talk binds without it. `ask` is a WebRTC call's own (POST
/v1/realtime/calls): a thread held when the call's channel opens is
asked about, lmgw.session.bind_pending; on GET /v1/realtime it is
400 invalid_value. Without `chat_thread` or `chat_folder`, 400
invalid_value.

101.description: Switching Protocols: the connection is now a WebSocket. Each frame is one JSON text event of OpenAI's GA Realtime protocol: client events in, server events (each with a server-minted event_id) out. session.created arrives first.

Sec-WebSocket-Protocol.description: The subprotocol selected, present when the client offered it.

426.description: Upgrade Required: the request carried no WebSocket upgrade headers.

post.description: OpenAI's WebRTC transport for the Realtime API. The client POSTs its SDP offer — audio with Opus, and the data channel oai-events created before createOffer — as application/sdp, or as multipart/form-data with the part sdp and an optional session part: a JSON object, the session as session.update takes it. The answer is 201 Created with the SDP answer (application/sdp: ICE-lite, one UDP host candidate — the local address this POST arrived on, on the WebRTC UDP port: realtime.webrtc_port, by default the HTTP port's number, or on the device listener its own port — Opus only, with RED when the offer carries it) and Location: /v1/realtime/calls/{call_id}, the call's id rtc_ and 24 hex digits. Behind it runs the session GET /v1/realtime runs — the same cascade, binding and policy — its events as JSON text on oai-events and its audio on RTP. lmgw's audio is one Opus stream for the call's whole life, a frame every 20 ms (realtime.webrtc_output_kbps, capped by the offer's maxaveragebitrate; DTX only when the offer's Opus format says usedtx=1; in-band FEC following the client's receiver reports), silence between answers; the client's audio is heard from its first frame after DTLS connects, what it sent before oai-events opened included, and an input_audio_buffer.commit takes the frames captured up to realtime.webrtc_commit_window_ms after it arrived. oai-events carries no audio: no response.output_audio.delta, input_audio_buffer.append is answered invalid_event, and session.lmgw.output_lead_ms is 0. Every call hears OpenAI's output_audio_buffer.started ({response_id}) with an answer's first frame, and .stopped right after the response.done of one that played out, or .cleared after the response.done of one that was cut (a barge-in, a cancel, a clear, a stop); output_audio_buffer.clear cancels the answer whose audio plays and is silent with none. An event over the client's max-message-size (or realtime.max_message_mb below it) arrives on an unbound call with its largest fields emptied, each followed by an error event_too_large naming the field's path. A call bound to a Chat thread also hears lmgw.output_audio.starved ({response_id, starved}) when an answer's audio runs dry and when it comes again, and may report its playout with lmgw.output_audio.playout ({playout_ntp_ms?, jitter_buffer_ms?}), which the answer's end follows; it stops with lmgw.response.stop ({playout_ntp_ms?}: the open response, the one owed and a held response.create cancelled, heard cut at the client's playout position when it sends one and what was sent otherwise, as on an audio-only call, where libwebrtc does not fill estimatedPlayoutTimestamp (calls design Q5); nothing with nothing open); an event over the limit travels both ways as lmgw.event.part ({id, index, count, data}, back to back, id the event's event_id), joined by the receiver, a client's up to realtime.max_message_mb. An unbound call answers these lmgw events invalid_event. The session starts when oai-events opens: session.created, then the session part applied as the session's first update (session.updated, or an error as for any update; on a call bound to a Chat thread it may change only what a bound session's client owns). Credentials, model resolution and the key's scope, budget and concurrency slot are /v1/realtime's — the slot held from this POST until the call ends — the subprotocol key aside; with Require API key off, an anonymous call from another page's Origin is refused with 403 cross_origin_refused. The query is /v1/realtime's: model, chat_thread or chat_folder with new, and takeover. A call bound to a Chat thread or folder only checks at this POST — nothing is bound and no thread is made — and binds when oai-events opens, checking again: takeover left out takes the thread over (its holder closes as taken over); never ends the call with lmgw.session.closed {kind: thread_bound, by} when the thread is held then, and is the 409 chat_thread_bound, the holder in error.held_by, when it is held at this POST; ask, this route's own, makes the call wait with lmgw.session.bind_pending ({held_by}): the client's lmgw.session.take_over ({}) takes the thread, a holder that ends lets the call bind by itself, a third client taking the thread brings another bind_pending, every other event meanwhile is answered with error bind_pending and the audio is discarded, and one realtime.ping_interval_s after the latest bind_pending the call ends with thread_bound (no bound at 0). A take_over that crosses the bind is ignored. A bound call's last event before lmgw ends it is lmgw.session.closed ({kind, by, message}: kind taken_over, revoked, out_of_reach, shutting_down, closed or thread_bound; by the new binder, the holder or who hung up, else null; message the sentence a WebSocket close's reason carries, led by the revocation token for revoked). A refusal when oai-events opens is that event — out_of_reach for a thread or folder out of the caller's reach, revoked for a key revoked since this POST, closed after an error carrying the refusal's code otherwise. by and held_by name a client as the Chat feed's voice.bound.by does. An unbound call sends no lmgw event and closes with nothing in band, as OpenAI's do. A call whose ICE, DTLS or data channel never comes up ends one realtime.ping_interval_s after its answer, binding nothing. Refused before the answer: 400 invalid_value (the query, a parameter rule, or a session part that is no JSON object or is over realtime.max_message_mb, which bounds a session event on either transport), 400 bad_request (a multipart body that does not parse), 400 sideband_unsupported (call_id), 400 owned_by_thread, 400 missing_sdp (a multipart body without sdp), 400 invalid_sdp (the offer does not parse; the reason quoted), 400 unsupported_offer (no Opus audio, or no data channel), 400 beta_protocol_unsupported, 403 cross_origin_refused, the bind's refusals (403 chat_thread_not_allowed, 404 chat_thread_not_found and chat_folder_not_found, 409 not_ongoing, folder_no_model, chat_thread_admin and chat_thread_bound), the key's 401, 403 and 429, 413 over max_body_mb, 415 unsupported_media_type, and 503 webrtc_unavailable when realtime.webrtc_enabled was off at lmgw's start, or the listener's UDP sockets failed to bind or are not bound (the message names the setting or the error), and, with a Retry-After header, while the device listener's group moves with it or when the POST's connection belongs to an earlier start of it. The device listener's UDP sockets follow its addresses and port: a change of the device listener ends its calls, a bound call's last event lmgw.session.closed {kind: shutting_down}, and leaves the plain listener's running. Not served: the sideband WebSocket, SIP's accept, reject and refer, and ephemeral client secrets.

schema.description:
OpenAI's sideband connection: a server-side WebSocket attached to a
WebRTC call's session. lmgw serves none, so it is refused, 400
sideband_unsupported, rather than opening an unrelated session.

A voice mode bound to an ongoing folder's current thread: the bind
decides the thread by the rules of `POST
/chat/api/folders/{id}/current` and binds it in one step, under the
folder's lock — the current thread, or a new one from the folder's
defaults when there is none, when it is out of the caller's reach,
when it idled past the folder's idle minutes, or with `new=true`
(unless it has no message yet). A new thread is recorded as
`folder.current` on the Chat feed with its reason. The thread bound
is reported in `session.lmgw.resolved.chat_thread`, and is then as
with `chat_thread`. Refused beside `chat_thread` (400 invalid_value)
and beside `model` (400 owned_by_thread); 404 chat_folder_not_found
for a folder the caller cannot see, 409 not_ongoing for one that is
no ongoing conversation, 409 folder_no_model for one whose defaults
name no model, then the thread's own refusals.

A voice mode bound to a Chat thread: bind the session to this thread
(negative for a temporary one). The thread then owns the chat model,
prompt, tools, speech models, voice and conversation, and the session
sends lmgw's `lmgw.*` extension events. Needs the chat capability
(the dashboard's cookie, an owner key or a paired device's key),
refused beside `model`, and refused for an Admin Chat thread (a
device is told there is no such thread). A device binds as its key:
the thread's aliases pass its scope and budget first.

The chat model: a `realtime.model_map` name, an OpenAI Realtime name
answered by `realtime.default_model`, or a chat alias — in that
order. Optional — a session may name its model in its first
`session.update` instead.

With `chat_folder`: start a new conversation — a new thread unless
the folder's current one has no message yet. Refused without
`chat_folder` (400 invalid_value).

With `chat_thread` or `chat_folder`: whether this bind may take the
thread from a session already bound to it. Left out, it does — the
other session closes (a WebSocket with 4000), naming who took it.
`never`: it does not — while another session is bound to the thread
the request is refused, 409 chat_thread_bound naming who holds it
("voice is in use on device 'phone'", and as `error.held_by`), and
nothing is taken over; a WebRTC call whose thread is taken between
its POST and its channel's open ends with lmgw.session.closed
{kind: thread_bound}. For a client's own automatic rebinds (after a
conversation moved to a new thread), so it never takes the voice
from another device that followed the same move; a user's explicit
choice to talk binds without it. `ask` is a WebRTC call's own (POST
/v1/realtime/calls): a thread held when the call's channel opens is
asked about, lmgw.session.bind_pending; on GET /v1/realtime it is
400 invalid_value. Without `chat_thread` or `chat_folder`, 400
invalid_value.

schema.description:
`POST /v1/realtime/calls` as `multipart/form-data` (calls design §2.1),
OpenAI's shape: the parts. The offer may come alone instead, as an
`application/sdp` body.

sdp.description:
The SDP offer (`application/sdp`): audio with Opus, and the data
channel `oai-events`, created before `createOffer`.

session.description:
The session (`application/json`): a JSON object, the session as
`session.update` takes it — OpenAI's GA session object. Not checked
before the answer: the session applies it as its first update, right
after `session.created` and before any event of the client's, and
answers it as any update, `session.updated` or an `error`. On a call
bound to a Chat thread only what the client owns applies (turn

Location.description: The call's path, /v1/realtime/calls/{call_id}: its last segment is the call id the hangup takes.

post.description: Ends a call: its session ends as if the client had closed it, a bound call's last event being lmgw.session.closed {kind: closed, by} naming who hung up. Answered 200 with an empty body once the call has let go — its Chat thread's binding marked as ending and its concurrency slot back — so a call posted right after it is neither refused (takeover=never) nor left pending (takeover=ask) by the call it ended. A call whose session or bind has not let go 10 s after the hangup (the bound a stopping server gives its sessions) is closed by force and answered 200 then; its binding is marked as ending only once its session notices, so a takeover=never call right after such a 200 may still be refused by it for that moment. A call that has let go but still waits for its last events' delivery (closing) is closed at once, without them, and answered 200. Takes no concurrency slot and counts no request, so a key at its limit can still hang up. Allowed for the key that made the call and for the owner; anyone else, and a call that has ended, gets 404 call_not_found.

parameters.description: on|off: run this one request as background work, for speculative or prefetching clients. On a local model it uses the model only when that disturbs nobody: it joins the model if it is loaded and no foreground request is waiting for room, or starts it into free GPU memory (evicting only idle background-started models), and never evicts, waits for or climbs a model foreground work uses. Otherwise the model's configured fallback answers (x-lmgw-fallback, x-lmgw-fallback-reason: background), or the request is refused with 503 gpu_deferred: retry later. Foreground work never interrupts a background request that has started; close the request to cancel it. On a candidate alias it makes the alias walk as a background alias. A cloud model and a model running on the CPU are unaffected. Absent or off: an ordinary request. Any other value is a 400.

x-lmgw-candidate.description: On a candidate alias, the id of the local model that answered (or refused) the request. Never sent next to x-lmgw-fallback. The body's model field still names the requested alias.

x-lmgw-fallback.description: The model or alias that answered instead of the one requested: the last hop of its chain of fallbacks (each model and alias has its own, and a fallback can have one in turn); the answer still names the requested model. On the chat routes, a fallback whose capabilities say it cannot see receives the request's images as text placeholders, and x-lmgw-images-omitted gives the count.

x-lmgw-fallback-chain.description: Every hop a fallback-served answer was handed to, in order, each with the reason it was handed on, as an RFC 8941 list: "m2";reason=hold, "cloud";reason=hold. Sent on every answer a fallback served, next to x-lmgw-fallback (the last name) and x-lmgw-fallback-reason (the last reason), so a client reads one header whatever the chain's length. A name that cannot be an sf-string (a byte outside 0x20–0x7E) is left empty, the reason kept. A streamed /v1/responses run names the hops of its first turn only: its headers left with the first event.

x-lmgw-fallback-reason.description: Why x-lmgw-fallback answered (the last hop's reason; x-lmgw-fallback-chain has every hop's); always sent next to it. hold: the GPU hold pauses local models. benchmark: a benchmark run has the GPU to itself until it ends. external_vram: GPU memory used outside lmgw by another program left too little room to load the model, so the fallback answered at once instead of waiting. background: a background job's model could not load without disturbing foreground work (any request that is not background traffic: a background candidate alias's, or one sent with x-lmgw-background: on). unavailable: a candidate alias's primary cannot be used at all (missing, disabled, or lacking a capability the alias enables) and none of its other models is loaded. quota: the upstream answered that its account's quota is exhausted (insufficient_quota), or lmgw remembers it so until its next check; nothing was charged for the refused attempt. unreachable: the upstream could not be connected to, so nothing reached it. disabled: the model or alias asked for is disabled, or its upstream is. gpu_setup: the local model could not start on the graphics card, and lmgw's machine check names why (the card, its driver, or the piece that lets models use it, not ready on the computer lmgw runs on); while that check still describes the machine, the fallback answers without a start being tried. engine_download: the engine the local model runs in is not on the computer yet, and downloading it failed or cannot be done.

parameters.description: on|off: per-request thinking switch; it wins over body fields. get.description: A stored response, exactly as it was served. It is present only when lmgw stored it — the creating call left store on (the default) while the gateway's response store was on — and only until retention evicts its conversation as a whole: by default 168 hours after the conversation's last activity, or once it falls outside the 500 most recently active conversations. A response an upstream that implements the Responses API made itself (created with store left on) is fetched from that upstream, query string included, and relayed as it answers, for as long as the same retention keeps lmgw's record of it. A client key reads only the responses it made, an owner key every one; another key's response is a 404 like an unknown id. 404 otherwise.

post.description: TypeSafe's System One API as llama.cpp serves it: a state and a map of typed questions (choice, score, noul), answered with calibrated probabilities and no generated text. The client object is forwarded with only model rewritten, members in the order sent (a choice question's criteria order is its option order), and the answer comes back verbatim, its model included: the id that answered upstream, not the name asked for (x-lmgw-fallback names a fallback alias). The body is read as JSON whatever its Content-Type. Routes to a local decision model (an aux row of kind decision) or to an openai_compatible or llama_cpp upstream whose catalog does not rule the model out; any other model is 501 not_supported_error before a container starts. A local row whose image predates the route is a 501 too, once its container is up and answers the route 404. The upstream's own errors are relayed as sent (llama.cpp's 500 for a prompt over the ubatch included), except a 401/403, which is lmgw's credential and a 502. The key's alias scope and budgets apply; the row is priced from lmgw's own price rows, input tokens and, where the price row charges them, output tokens (Jev's does not). Errors lmgw answers itself are llama.cpp-shaped, except the shared /v1 layers' own: the gate's 401, 403 and 429, and the 413 for a declared Content-Length over max_body_mb, which are OpenAI-shaped.

schema.description:
`POST /v1/systemone`'s body: a state and the questions to answer about it.

lmgw reads only `model` from a client's body and forwards the rest as it
came; the upstream validates its own wire (TypeSafe answers a malformed
question with 422, llama.cpp with 400).

criteria.technical: bugs, outages, errors in the product

department.instructions: Which team should handle this ticket?

example.state: Hi, my invoice from last month charged me twice for the Pro plan. Can you refund one of the charges?

files.description: llama.cpp's extension: files as data URLs (`images` is its alias).

images.description:
llama.cpp's extension: images as data URLs, for a model started with a
projector and a type that reads images (501 otherwise). An alias of
`files`. TypeSafe takes text only.

model.description:
Required: lmgw routes by it, as TypeSafe requires it and llama-server's
router mode needs it. Rewritten to the route's upstream model on the
way out; nothing else is.

questions.description:
The questions, keyed by ids the caller picks; the answers come back
under the same keys.

state.description:
What the questions are about: a string, or an object or array (a chat
log, a record), which llama.cpp gives the model as JSON text. `null`
only for the types that take none (LiquidAI's d1 models); llama.cpp
refuses it on the others.

x-lmgw-speech.description: On POST /v1/audio/speech (and on /v1/tasks/run and /v1/tasks/stream, for their chars part), what lmgw changed in the request so the model understands it; a '; '-separated list. voice=options.voice_id: a voice the model ships, which this family (MagpieTTS) reads from options.voice_id. voice=preset->options.voice_id: the same for a preset's voice id. voice=<name>: a shipped voice sent in the model's own spelling. language=<asked>-><sent>: the language in the model's own vocabulary, e.g. de->german for Qwen3-TTS, en->en-us for Kokoro. instructions=options.instruct: instructions moved to where the family reads them. instructions=also:options.instruct or instructions=also:options.instruction: the model's default request options describe the voice under that other key, which the engine would merge in beside the request's and refuse as conflicting, so the request's text went there too and replaces the default. instructions=dropped: the model reads none (capabilities.speech.instructions is none). tags=mapped:<n>,stripped:<n>: inline tags in input were rewritten into the model's spelling, or removed so they are never read out. chars=replaced:<U+XXXX/...>,dropped:<U+XXXX/...>: characters of input the model's engine has no entry for in its package's vocabulary (Supertonic refuses the whole request over one), replaced by an equivalent it has (a typographic quote by a plain one, a dash by -) or removed (an emoji). A cloud model and a model running on the CPU are unaffected. Absent or off: an ordinary request. Any other value is a 400.
parameters.name: x-lmgw-background

parameters.description: The job id of the live agent run to attribute this request's cost, tokens and call count to. Only an agent token may attribute, and only to its own runs. An id that names no live run, a run that belongs to another agent, or a caller without an agent token is ignored with a log line and never refused.
parameters.name: x-lmgw-run

schema.x-lmgw-untyped: audio.cpp's own per-task stream, relayed verbatim

x-lmgw-candidate.description: On a candidate alias, the id of the local model that answered (or refused) the request. Never sent next to x-lmgw-fallback. The body's model field still names the requested alias.

x-lmgw-fallback.description: The model or alias that answered instead of the one requested: the last hop of its chain of fallbacks (each model and alias has its own, and a fallback can have one in turn); the answer still names the requested model. On the chat routes, a fallback whose capabilities say it cannot see receives the request's images as text placeholders, and x-lmgw-images-omitted gives the count.

x-lmgw-fallback-chain.description: Every hop a fallback-served answer was handed to, in order, each with the reason it was handed on, as an RFC 8941 list: "m2";reason=hold, "cloud";reason=hold. Sent on every answer a fallback served, next to x-lmgw-fallback (the last name) and x-lmgw-fallback-reason (the last reason), so a client reads one header whatever the chain's length. A name that cannot be an sf-string (a byte outside 0x20–0x7E) is left empty, the reason kept. A streamed /v1/responses run names the hops of its first turn only: its headers left with the first event.

x-lmgw-fallback-reason.description: Why x-lmgw-fallback answered (the last hop's reason; x-lmgw-fallback-chain has every hop's); always sent next to it. hold: the GPU hold pauses local models. benchmark: a benchmark run has the GPU to itself until it ends. external_vram: GPU memory used outside lmgw by another program left too little room to load the model, so the fallback answered at once instead of waiting. background: a background job's model could not load without disturbing foreground work (any request that is not background traffic: a background candidate alias's, or one sent with x-lmgw-background: on). unavailable: a candidate alias's primary cannot be used at all (missing, disabled, or lacking a capability the alias enables) and none of its other models is loaded. quota: the upstream answered that its account's quota is exhausted (insufficient_quota), or lmgw remembers it so until its next check; nothing was charged for the refused attempt. unreachable: the upstream could not be connected to, so nothing reached it. disabled: the model or alias asked for is disabled, or its upstream is. gpu_setup: the local model could not start on the graphics card, and lmgw's machine check names why (the card, its driver, or the piece that lets models use it, not ready on the computer lmgw runs on); while that check still describes the machine, the fallback answers without a start being tried. engine_download: the engine the local model runs in is not on the computer yet, and downloading it failed or cannot be done.

x-lmgw-speech.description: On POST /v1/audio/speech (and on /v1/tasks/run and /v1/tasks/stream, for their chars part), what lmgw changed in the request so the model understands it; a '; '-separated list. voice=options.voice_id: a voice the model ships, which this family (MagpieTTS) reads from options.voice_id. voice=preset->options.voice_id: the same for a preset's voice id. voice=<name>: a shipped voice sent in the model's own spelling. language=<asked>-><sent>: the language in the model's own vocabulary, e.g. de->german for Qwen3-TTS, en->en-us for Kokoro. instructions=options.instruct: instructions moved to where the family reads them. instructions=also:options.instruct or instructions=also:options.instruction: the model's default request options describe the voice under that other key, which the engine would merge in beside the request's and refuse as conflicting, so the request's text went there too and replaces the default. instructions=dropped: the model reads none (capabilities.speech.instructions is none). tags=mapped:<n>,stripped:<n>: inline tags in input were rewritten into the model's spelling, or removed so they are never read out. chars=replaced:<U+XXXX/...>,dropped:<U+XXXX/...>: characters of input the model's engine has no entry for in its package's vocabulary (Supertonic refuses the whole request over one), replaced by an equivalent it has (a typographic quote by a plain one, a dash by -) or removed (an emoji). Each list names at most 64 codepoints and then ends in +<n> more; lmgw's log has the full list. An input left with nothing to say is 400 empty_input, which carries the header too. The voice, language and chars parts apply to local audio models only. Absent when the request went as it came; input changes only for its inline tags and those characters.

tags.description: The Chat API a client app uses as a paired device (the `chat` capability), with its client certificate on the device listener: the threads and folders it follows, an ongoing conversation's current thread, and the change feed that keeps them current. Every route here refuses a device with 401 device_key_unknown once its key opens no device (it was replaced or deleted: pair the device again), 403 device_unconfirmed until the owner confirms its enrolment, 401 device_disabled while the device is disabled, 401 device_certificate_expired past its certificate's notAfter, and 401 key_expired past its expiry date. What is open when that happens ends: the feed with `revoked`, a turn's stream with an `error` event whose code is revoked. Both carry `kind`, what to do: device_disabled and key_expired wait for the gateway's side, key_unknown and certificate_expired mean pair the device again, and revoked is any other kind of key's revocation.
tags.name: chat

tags.description: Files between paired devices of one app (device transfers design): a device offers a file to another device that declared the same app id at pairing, uploads it to lmgw in ranges it can resume, and the other device is offered it once every byte matched its sha256, downloads it with ranges and says it arrived; lmgw then deletes the bytes. The transfer capability: paired devices (on the device listener) send and receive; the owner lists every transfer and cancels any; a client key or an agent token is refused 403 transfer_device_only. A refusal is the flat {code, message}, with free_bytes, received or state where its code names one. JSON bodies are at most 16 KiB (16384 bytes), refused 413 body_too_large; the only bound on a file is the free space of lmgw's data directory. The Chat feed's transfer.updated says each offer, ready and end to the sender, to the receiver from ready on, and to the owner.
tags.name: transfers

tags.description: The device listener's own routes (device link design §4.6): served on the device listener only, over TLS 1.3, and the 404 an unknown path is on the plain listener. Their bodies are at most 16 KiB (16384 bytes), refused 413 body_too_large naming it, not max_body_mb. Every answer carries Connection: close.
tags.name: devices

tags.description: The routes an agent container calls with its own token: reading its own definition and runs, and opening and driving a run.
tags.name: agent-runtime
